items.statement: Management projects acquired group EBITDA of EUR 35 million for FY26 and EUR 90-100 million by FY28-29
items.quote: We after seeing this business for 5 to 6 months now and my team feel very confident that we would be able to d eliver not only this year's number, but financial year '28 or '29. We would be on track to delivering the 90 million to 100 million EBITDA out of the acquired

items.statement: Legacy Sudarshan targets 8-10% revenue growth for full year FY26
items.quote: I think we should -- the aim at the end of the year is to get the 10% in that region, 8% to 10 % number from the year-end perspective.

items.statement: Acquired group Q1 EBITDA margin at 4.1% on revenue of INR 1,882 crores
items.quote: Revenue for the quarter is at INR1,882 crores versus one month revenue of March '25 post deal closure, which was at INR525 crores. In absolute EBITDA is at INR78 crores, which is 4.1%.

items.statement: Legacy Sudarshan pigment EBITDA margin improved to 15.1% in Q1 FY26 from 12.7% last year
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter is at INR87 crores compared to INR90 crores last year and the EBITDA margin is at 15.1%.

items.statement: Combined global pigment business adjusted EBITDA margin at 6.7% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Revenue from global pigment business, which is lega cy Sudarshan’s pigment business and acquired group stood at INR2,456 crores for Q1 FY '26 with the adjusted EBITDA of INR165 crores, which is at 6.7

items.statement: Integration and restructuring costs expected at EUR 10 million plus for FY26 excluding IT and org restructuring
items.quote: We plan the integration cost for this year and the integration cost should be Eur 10 million plus for this year, excluding the IT or the organization restructuring, Rohitji.

items.statement: Current integration/restructuring cost run rate at INR 32.8 crores per quarter
items.quote: So firstly, on the in tegration costs, the current integration /restructuring cost is at INR32.8 crores, and we ex pect the similar run rate

items.statement: Manufacturing footprint: ~50% India, ~30% Germany, balance LATAM, America, Japan
items.quote: I would say, ballpark, 50% from India, 30% from Germany and balance from LATAM, America and Japan, right, other geographies.

items.statement: Non-specialty Azo pigment production transfer from Germany to India nearly complete
items.quote: First was as there was a process, whic h was in place, where some of the non- specialty Azo pigments, were being moved from Germany to India So that process is just getting completed now

items.statement: Europe seasonal shutdown in August creates new seasonal impact
items.quote: Also this, we are learning new areas where we see from August Europe is almost shut. So because of th at, this is a new seasonal impact, which even I have learned about from that perspective

items.statement: Net debt increased to INR 1,084 crores from INR 652 crores due to purchase consideration payment in June
items.quote: Net debt for the quarter is at INR1,084 crores compared to INR652 crores in the Q4 of the last financial year. And this is because of the part of the purchase consideration, which was paid in June, which is as per the agreement.

items.statement: Average cost of borrowing at 6.5-7.5%; higher reported finance cost includes lease accounting impact
items.quote: If I see on the gross state, the interest cost should be in the range of 6.5% to 7.5%. There are also other accounting impact in the interest cost, which is on account of the lease accounting, where the finance cost on the lease is also captured here.

items.statement: Procurement shifting from Europe to Asia for competitive sourcing and volume leverage
items.quote: Procurement has been a big lever, wher e I think the procurement initially by the acquired group was more focused on Europe, but we are shifting this to Asia to more competitive sources and also taking advantage of our combined volumes

items.statement: IT costs benchmarked 3-4x higher than world benchmark; significant reduction opportunity
items.quote: When we benchmark IT costs, the IT cost by at least 3 to 4 times higher than th e world benchmark was. So we deliver both from a cost reduction and also bringing in efficiency and processes

items.statement: European power costs no longer a headwind; winter seasonal increase only
items.quote: The big surge, which had happened during the Ukraine, Russia, for energy at that time, is not prevalent anymore, And hence, the power differential cost during the normal months other than the winter is not significantly very different. Raja: Okay. So it's no longer a headwind for us

items.statement: Acquired group adds specialty dyes, anti-corrosion pigments, pigment preparations broadening portfolio
items.quote: But now we also have an expanded portfolio into specialty dyes anti corrosion with pigments, pigment preparations which has really given us a great a boost in our product range, probably the most comprehensive broadening product portfolio.

items.statement: Only two global pigment players remain; Sudarshan only pure-play pigment company
items.quote: Five or six years ago, there were five global players. Today, there are only two global players, with Sudarshan as the only player who is focused on only pigment business.

items.statement: Legacy Sudarshan ROCE at 14.3% in Q1 FY26 vs 13.7% last year
items.quote: Return on capital employed f or the quarter is at 14.3% compared to 13.7% last year

items.statement: Depreciation expected at INR 99 crores per quarter for FY26
items.quote: for the quarter, the depreciation is at INR99 crores, and we expect the similar range each quarter going forward for the FY26

items.statement: Tariff situation may require local production in Mexico or Germany instead of India
items.quote: We have a tariff situation and hence, the tariff situation sometimes would kind of lead the strategy to meet this produc t locally in Mexico or Germany and not in India

items.statement: Acquired 100% of Citieffe Group via MediStream for EUR 18.8M equity value plus EUR 4.2M shareholder loan repayment and EUR 8M debt assumed, implying EUR 31M enterprise value at ~10x 2024 EBITDA
items.quote: We have valued the company, an equity valuation of about EUR18.8 million and we'll be repaying shareholder loan of about EUR4.2 million as part of the closing. So that's a EUR23 million payout that will happen on closing, and we're taking over a debt of about EUR8 million. So that values the company at about EUR31 million enterprise value, which on the basis of reported EBITDA of 2024 values the c

items.statement: Expects to double Citieffe revenue in next 5 years with Polymed synergies, from ~EUR 17-18M to EUR 25-30M, without significant capex
items.quote: We believe that the asset has good amount of growth potential going forward. It's been growing. If you look at slightly longer-term trajectory at 10% to 12% CAGR with the help of Polymed and our distribution network, we should be able to double the business in the next 5 years.

items.statement: Citieffe requires only regular capex of EUR 1.5-2M annually; significant capacity headroom exists at 60% utilization with ability to add third shift
items.quote: We don't expect any significant capex to be done. The regular capex for this company is between 1.5 million to 2 million a year.

items.statement: Bologna facility at 60% utilization with 2,100 sqm; third shift available for significant headroom to serve growth
items.quote: They operate close to 2,100 meters square of manufacturing facility in the city of Bologna and it's currently at 60% capacity utilization. And with the third with the ability to add third shift to the business, there is significant headroom available for to serve the customer through this facility.

items.statement: Citieffe gross margins exceed 90%; EBITDA margin ~17-18% in 2024 with operating leverage expected as revenue scales
items.quote: Yes. So the gross margins of the company are in excess of 90% plus in this space.

items.statement: Near-term synergy priority is adding plates to complement nails/screws portfolio; plates represent ~40% of trauma market and enable participation in public tenders
items.quote: One of the most nearest sort of synergy that we see is to introduce plates as part of the product portfolio, something which has been missing in the company's portfolio currently

items.statement: Citieffe has direct sales presence in Italy (12% share, #2), Mexico (12% share), and US via 1099 agents; no GPO contracts in US
items.quote: In Italy, they're the second largest player with about 12% market share. In Mexico, again, they have close to 12% market share amongst the top players in those markets, and US they're slowly gradually increasing their presence and getting greater coverage of the hospitals.

items.statement: US is 67% of global orthopedics market; Citieffe products MDR certified in EU and approved in US plus 25+ other markets
items.quote: US is the biggest market, I mean, like all medical devices segment, orthopedic also is dominated by US with almost 67% of sales in orthopedics being done in US followed up by Europe.

items.statement: All Citieffe products fully MDR certified in Europe; US and 25+ market accreditations in place
items.quote: As I mentioned, the product is fully MDR-compliant. One of the few companies of this size, we've been able to get all the products certified in the even the new MDR regulations, and I have accreditation in US and other 25 plus markets.

items.statement: Existing management led by CEO Pascal Govi (since 2019) retained; variable incentive plan linked to 5-year financial targets created for key team
items.quote: I'm also very pleased to inform that the existing management team, which has been around for a long time, is continuing to has joined the Polymed Group and is going to be driving the future growth. Mr. Pascal Govi, who has been the CEO of the company since 2019 will continue to remain the CEO and build the business with the help of Polymed Group.

items.statement: No blended margin guidance yet for Citieffe; operating leverage expected as revenue grows from EUR 17-18M to 25-30M without significant fixed cost increase
items.quote: Early to provide guidance on how the margin will expand. I think it's very clear that there is an operating leverage play that will happen in this company as the sales increase.

items.statement: PendraCare acquisition closed 23 Sep; expects high single-digit to low double-digit organic growth for PendraCare and similar profile for Citieffe before synergies
items.quote: We think that on the PendraCare, we had mentioned that the asset could grow in high single digit to low double digit on its own currently. And we expect similar kind of growth profile for even this asset.

items.statement: Global orthopedics market $61B growing 3-4%; trauma & extremities $12B growing 6-7% (expected to reach $16B); India 3% of global orthopedics
items.quote: orthopedics is obviously a large segment in the overall medical devices sector, it's about $61 billion, growing at about 3% to 4%. Within that, trauma and extremity is the largest segment at about $12 billion, and it's growing the fastest at about 6% to 7%.

items.statement: No plans to shift Citieffe manufacturing to India; customers value European origin; integration execution risk acknowledged with executive committee being formed under Himanshu and Rishi
items.quote: We have currently no such plans. I think the facility there is doing a very good job. And the customers, they know the product being manufactured in Europe. So we currently have no plans to move the manufacturing to India.

items.statement: M&A strategy focuses on high-tech medical device adjacencies driven by disease burden; will pause after two recent acquisitions to absorb and integrate
items.quote: We have also very clearly called out that there are certain segments which are very exciting for us. And we've been obviously investing in those segments over the course of last 5 years. And these are all effectively driven by the disease burden pattern, right, that's been evolving over the course of the last few years.

items.statement: Proposed merger of promoter group companies into Dollar Industries Limited to consolidate brand, reduce compliance burden, related party transactions, and bring business properties under listed entity
items.quote: Today, I stand before you to share with pride and confidence the details of our proposed merger of the promoter group companies into Dollar Industries Limited, a move that we believe will be a game changer for the company and all its stakeholders.

items.statement: Promoter holding to increase by 1.39% from 72.21% to 73.60% post-merger
items.quote: Fifth, it is important to highlight that promoter holding will increase by only 1.39%. That is from 72.21% to 73 .60%.

items.statement: Promoter trust to hold 51% of promoter stake for continuity and alignment with long-term growth
items.quote: Sixth and most importantly, we are creating a promoter trust that will hold 51% of the promoter stake in Dollar Industries Limited.

items.statement: Merger expected to be EPS neutral with PAT impact of INR4.5-5 crores; pre-merger EPS INR16.05, post-merger INR16.01
items.quote: So overall impact on the PAT is INR4.5 crores to INR5 crores. So basically, EPS is very neutral, same EPS, last year is INR16.05. After this merger, it is negligible INR16.01, only INR0.4 impact, no more than that.

items.statement: 90% of related party transactions to vanish post-merger; remaining 1-2 individual/firm transactions to continue
items.quote: Basically, 90% of the related party transaction is vanished. Only there is -- if you check the RPT personnel, there is 1 or 2 individual and 1 or 2 firm also. So that is remained intact only.

items.statement: Business properties worth over INR100 crores to come under Dollar Industries Limited ownership
items.quote: Physical assets is more than INR100 crores actually. The business property, which is related to Dollar -- is only dedicated to Dollar is more than INR100 crores.

items.statement: Merger valuation done by KPMG using three approaches; brand taken at book value of INR5 crores
items.quote: Basically, all the merger exercise is supervised and completed by the KPMG itself and most of the assets are like brand value. Brand is our -- taken at book value only. It is only INR5 crores.

items.statement: Stamp duty for merger estimated at INR2-3 crores (2-3% in West Bengal)
items.quote: It is only around 2% to 3% in Calcutta in West Bengal for merger 2% of the duties charge. Prashant: So value-wise that would... Ajay Patodia: Around INR2 crores to INR3 crores only

items.statement: No material one-time costs for merger; only 2% court fees and professional expenses
items.quote: No, there is no any such major cost involved. As there is only -- we have to pay only 2% of the total merger fees to the court and the rest of expenses is related to professional capacity only.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin of 12-13% for FY26; currently at 11%
items.quote: We are very hopeful and we really aspire to be between 12 % to 13% this particular fiscal. And currently -- yes. Madhur Rathi: No, sir, sorry, you were saying something. Ankit Gupta: So currently, we are already at 11%. So I think by year-end, we should be able to touch around 12

items.statement: Demand okay but seasonal; monsoon stretched, Q2 not good for innerwear sales; cyclical but better than last year
items.quote: So industry-wide, the demand has been okay, I would say, but it's a seasonal thing since the monsoon season is a bit stretched this particular year. So as it is, second quarter is not very good for the innerwear sales. So overall, from the demand point of view, it's a cyclical thing. So it's good as compared to the last.

items.statement: No further funding required for merger or operations
items.quote: No, no, no further funding is required.

items.statement: Advertisement spend fixed at INR85-100 crores absolute range; planning INR85-90 crores this year
items.quote: So this year also, we are planning to spend around INR85 crores to INR90 crores only in the advertisement spend.

items.statement: Digital ad spend 20-25% of total budget; increasing to ~25% this year; rest TV, retail branding, hoardings, newspaper
items.quote: So every year, we do increase our percentage spend on digital media. So this year, I think we will be spending around 25% of our total ad spend.

items.statement: All distributors sell thermal products; hopeful for good winter season
items.quote: So all the distributors of ours sell the thermal products. And we are very hopeful that it will be a good winter for us as well.

items.statement: No threat from Zudio as they focus on outerwear; Dollar has 50-year history in economy range which provides volume and economies of scale; launching new products across premium, mid-premium, economy segments
items.quote: Currently, we don't see any threat coming in from Zudio or likes of Zudio because they are more focused in the outerwear segment instead of the innerwear segment. Secondly, we have a history of 50 years, right? And we have started this company with economy range of products. So we can't do away with the economy range of products because it's the product segment which gives us volume, which gives u

items.statement: No pricing pressure expected in upcoming quarters; domestic pricing stagnant; raw material prices stagnant; exports only 4.5-5% of sales
items.quote: No. So see, our exports is only 4.5% to our total sales, around 4.5%, 5% only. So in domestic also, we don't see any change in the pricing. It's very stagnant. Even the raw material prices are very stagnant. So we don't see any change in prices in the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Target to reduce receivable days from ~112 to 100-103 days in current year; receivables situation improved significantly
items.quote: It is very much improved. Even current year, we have targeted to reduce our receivable days. Currently, it is around 112 days to reduce to around 100 to 103.

items.statement: Discount schemes: 1% extra benefit at 100% target, 1.5% at 110%+ target; includes Project Lakshya royalty calculation
items.quote: It is mainly scheme part only because the discount already given in the bills itself, it is mainly the scheme part and incentive to the dealers when he complete the target, like if it completes the target of 100%, it gives a 1% extra benefit. If it is target more than 110%, then it gets the 1.5% benefit.

items.statement: Own manufacturing 25-27% of capacity; merger adds stitching units, minimal increase to ~26-27%
items.quote: Not much because it would be adding only the stitching units that we have that will get merged into this. So it would be miniscule, but it would be what like shift making 25% to 27%, 26% maybe.

items.statement: E-commerce grew 80% last year to 8-8.5% of sales from 3%; strong growth continuing this year; margins similar across general trade, e-commerce, quick commerce
items.quote: So last year, we did around 80% of growth. And earlier, it used to contribute around 3% of sales. But last year, we crossed t hat -- crossed to 8%, 8.5% coming in from just e -commerce. And yes, this year also, we are seeing a very good growth coming in from e-commerce only

items.statement: Website sales negligible; focusing on marketplaces; planning performance marketing to drive website traffic
items.quote: So currently, our website sales are almost negligible because we are focusing more on the marketplaces where the traffic is already there. The consumer footfall is already there. And we are currently planning to mov e ahead with performance marketing and create traffic -- drive traffic towards our website also, but we have not started it

items.statement: Competitive pressures remain same; unable to comment on Q2 specifically
items.quote: So we won't be able to comment about Q2 as of now, but things have been pretty much same.

items.statement: Acquired 100% of BioPharm Parent Holdings, Inc. and its two subsidiaries for $104M on a debt-free, cash-free basis plus ~$2M for excess cash and working capital.
items.quote: We have acquired a 100% interest in BioPharm Parent Holdings, Inc., along with its two subsidiaries, BioPharm Communications LLC and Addressable Health LLC, collectively referred to as BioPharm for a total purchase pr ice of US $104 million on a debt -free, cash-free basis plus approximately $2 million for the excess cash and working

items.statement: Purchase price paid in tranches: $65M upfront at closing, $12M deferred to March 2026, plus earn-outs of $8M (CY25) and $19M (CY26).
items.quote: Firstly, a guaranteed payment of US $77 million, which implies approximately 9.8 multiple of t he 2024 EBITDA and a 9.6 multiple of the 2025 EBITDA basis the H1 performance in 2025. This has been divided into 65 million upfront, which has been paid at closing and 12 million as deferred payment to be paid in March 2026. There are also two earn-outs first one of $8 million and the second at $19 mill

items.statement: BioPharm CY24 net revenue $29.2M with ~27% EBITDA margin; employee costs 53%, other expenses ~20% of net revenue.
items.quote: On a net revenue basis, employee costs are 53% and other expenses, including data access and technology costs are about 20%, yielding an EBITDA margin of about 27% on net revenue.

items.statement: Expect ~$1M annual cost synergies from data purchase consolidation and future offshoring, starting post-integration.
items.quote: In terms of cost synergies, we expect around US $1 million annually, which should start accruing beyond the integration phase.

items.statement: Earn-out KPIs tied to 15-20% YoY revenue growth for CY25 and CY26, and order book for CY27.
items.quote: The KPIs are linked actually to revenues and the -- from an employee incentive perspective, even to the order book for the calendar year 2027. So, the revenues for 2025 and 2026 and the order book for 2027 would be the benchmark and achievement in the range of 15% to 20% growth year-on-year is what would result in the full payout of the earn-out.

items.statement: BioPharm has two segments: core BioPharm (~$30M push/programmatic) and Addressable Health (~$7-8M pull/precision media), powered by Tandem data platform.
items.quote: approximately out of the $38 million revenue in calendar year 2024 about $7 million to $8 million is from Addressable Health and $29 to $30 -- close to $30 million, $31 million is the BioPharm business, right? The first one being the push business, the other being the pull business.

items.statement: BioPharm uses output-based pricing (not T&M); revenue per employee and margins higher due to specialized data/tech-driven outcomes.
items.quote: Both of these point towards the specialized nature of work that BioPharm does and its use of data and technology to deliver outcomes for the client rather than just operational engagements, providing people-based expertise and measured based on input or on T&M basis.

items.statement: Incremental go-to-market and integration investments over next 4-6 quarters, offset by cost synergies and revenue growth.
items.quote: we'll be making incremental investments in the business to drive growth, these investments in the business should be offset by the cost synergies and along with the growth in the combined business should result in a 27% to 28% EBITDA on net revenue in around six quarters

items.statement: BioPharm leadership (20+ years avg experience) retained with earn-outs covering revenues for next 5 quarters and CY27 order book; performance stock options planned for FY27-28.
items.quote: revenues for the next 5 quarters, next quarter or the coming quarter and calendar year '26 as well as the order book for '27 is covered in this deal, right, which is going to be paid out of this total amount is for the management team. We will, in the year '27, '28, be creating a performance-linked stock option plan for the management team.

items.statement: Brand-side revenue more variable than enterprise due to FDA approval/competitive risks; mitigation via multi-brand portfolios across customers.
items.quote: However, there will be slightly more variability than the enterprise side of our business on the brand side, given the nature of the engagements there, which would be exposed to risk in terms of FDA approval or other competitive environment. But end of the day, making those large portfolios by working across a larger set of customers is the way to deal with that.

items.statement: Acquisition positions combined entity as powerful player in brand activation with full-funnel precision marketing, differentiating vs traditional healthcare agencies not suited for AI-driven centralization.
items.quote: and Indegene as a combined entity now emerge as a powerful player in the brand activation space, combining the right mix of integrated end -to-end marketing capabilities, creden tials, talent and client access , thus becoming a true force in t he market. It positions Indegene to be future ready for truly omnichannel engagement and strengthens our ability to deliver full -funnel precision marketing

items.statement: Digital marketing spend shifting faster than industry growth; AI adoption driving centralization, creating tailwinds for Indegene's enterprise and brand offerings.
items.quote: We believe we are seeing the next level of centralization and change in operating model. This time, the reason is the top-down pressure on the life science industry and what AI could offer. As companies adopt and use AI, the only way to drive standardization in a compliant manner while securing high adoption of AI in sales and marketing will be through centralization.

items.statement: Transaction closed with all approvals completed by October 1st.
items.quote: Yes, 1st October was the closing and all the closing formalities have been completed and the transaction is fully closed.

items.statement: Management declined to provide specific revenue or EBITDA margin guidance for FY26 and FY27, citing difficulty in forecasting margins but expecting high capacity utilization similar to past years.
items.quote: For the revenue guidelines, we cannot really give the guidance. But what we can say is that we have continuously focused on high-capacity utilization, which is also reflecting in our results in the past, as well as in the current year as well.

items.statement: Order book as of June 30 stands at over 4 GW, comprising medium and long-term orders; spot and distributor orders (25-30% of monthly sales) are not included.
items.quote: Our order book as of June 30th stands at over 4 gigawatts. And the order book generally comprises of medium and long-term orders.

items.statement: Management sees sustained demand growth driven by green hydrogen, green ammonia, battery storage, and technology shift from obsolete Mono PERC to TOPCon, dismissing overcapacity concerns due to low industry utilization (~40%).
items.quote: So, we feel that the demand should keep rising, and because you have alternate demand also adding up to the already prevalent demand. And along with that, battery storage is also adding up to that demand.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin was 19.8% vs 16.5% in Q1 FY25; management expects margins to remain at decent levels similar to historical 16%+ but declined to confirm sustainability of Q1 level.
items.quote: Last year was over 16.5%. And this year, first quarter, the EBITDA is 19.8% in the first quarter. Going forward, it's difficult to really give a number of what EBITDA margin will be, but we feel that it will be a decent number, quite similar to what we have seen in the past.

items.statement: Current installed capacity 3.8 GW (June 2025); added 1 GW at Ambala (operational Q3 FY26) taking total to 4.8 GW; Odisha 4 GW module by April 2026 (full Q2 FY27), 2.4 GW cell stabilized by end Q2 FY27; Phase 2 adds another 2.4 GW cell.
items.quote: We have added another one gigawatt capacity at Ambala, which should be operational henceforth, taking our total capacity to 4.8 gigawatt. Beyond this, we are expanding our capabilities further with a fully integrated cell and module manufacturing facility in Odisha, 4.8 gigawatt for cells and 4 gigawatt for modules, expected to be commissioned by quarter 3 FY27 and FY26, respectively.

items.statement: Demand shifting rapidly to TOPCon (especially G12R); Mono PERC margins shrinking and becoming unsustainable; management estimates ~40 GW of ALMM capacity is obsolete technology.
items.quote: Yes. And also, it is shifting towards G12R TOPCon. So, G12R is in the same size module instead of 590, 595, you can get 625 watt. So, the customer is so sensitive that they also want the highest efficiency even in TOPCon also.

items.statement: Customer mix in Q1 FY26: Utility 80%, Retail 10%, C&I 8%, EPC and Export remainder; over 500 customers, no single name disclosed.
items.quote: It will be -- in the current quarter, it will be 80%, to be precise. Jainam: Abani Jha: So, that is a large area. And the retail, retail is about 10%, C &I is about 8%, and the remaining one is EPC and export

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio improved to 1.28 from 1.36; target to maintain 1.2-1.3x including new capex debt; cell plant debt at MCLR + margin (~8.9-9%), 75% debt / 25% equity funding.
items.quote: We will maintain the debt equity ratio in our current level only. So, it will be about even including the debt we are going to take on the capex. We will maintain the debt equity ratio between 1.2 to 1.3.

items.statement: IPO proceeds (INR 900 crore) primarily for Odisha greenfield project; portion used to repay subsidiary debt. Cell capex (INR 1,300 cr over FY26-27) funded 75% debt (govt bank) / 25% equity (internal accruals).
items.quote: The proceeds from the IPO will primarily be used to fund our upcoming greenfield manufacturing project in Odisha. A portion of the funds will also be utilised to repay debt in one of our subsidiaries, further strengthening our balance sheet and enhancing financial flexibility.

items.statement: Working capital grew proportionally with business; focus on improving efficiency via better treasury management.
items.quote: So, see, working capital has grown in the same proportion of the growth in the business. However, we are putting a lot of focus on effective, making it more effective utilisation and more effective availability of working capital through the better treasury management

items.statement: Backward integration into wafer/ingot planned: 8 GW integrated facility at Narmadapuram, Madhya Pradesh (200-300 acres sought); also considering matching ingot/wafer to Odisha cell capacity.
items.quote: And additionally, we have taken land in Madhya Pradesh also, there is a solar manufacturing park which is being built in Narmadapuram near Bhopal, where we have initially have got 51 acre land, but we are trying to increase it to at least 200 acres, 300 acres is what we've asked. But even if we get 200 acres, we will be able to build 8 gigawatt of integrated ingot wafer cell module kind of a facil

items.statement: ALMM list includes ~35 GW obsolete tech; domestic cell mandate (ALCM) likely extended to 2027-28 due to insufficient commissioned cell capacity (~40-50 GW needed); wafer/ingot draft policy targets 2028.
items.quote: So, until there is a 40 gigawatt-50 gigawatt type of cell up and running, it is difficult to do the entire shift towards domestic cell. So, we feel that there will be some extension into those timelines. Apart from that, there is -- it takes about 18 to 20, rather 30 months to commission a project from awarding till the end.

items.statement: Cell plant stabilization risk (complex process, gases/chemicals); technology obsolescence risk (Mono PERC, 10-busbar); policy timing risk (ALCM/wafer mandates); execution risk on greenfield Odisha project.
items.quote: cell takes little more time to optimize because this is more complex process and gases and chemicals and lot of -- so efficiencies are a big and that stabilization takes little more time. So, we are targeting end of second quarter for our 2.4 gigawatt cell

items.statement: Management targets double-digit growth in transportation and healthcare for FY27; media & communications growth uncertain
items.quote: I'm pretty confident both healthcare and automotive, we will be aiming for double-digit growth in FY '27, right? And Media & Communication, as I said, is still a little bit wait and watch.

items.statement: Transportation H2 expected better than H1; Europe, Japan, India strong; US auto muted but adjacencies growing
items.quote: I feel that H2 will be definitely much better than H1. And so I'm very positive on that from a trajectory perspective.

items.statement: Margin recovery expected in H2 vs H1 driven by utilization improvement to 75% by FY26 end and 80% next year
items.quote: Our target f rom a H2 perspective, we definitely want to do much better than And I'm pretty confident that we will be able to achieve much better margins compared to H1

items.statement: Utilization improved from 66% to above 70% in Q2; target 75% by end FY26 and 80% next FY
items.quote: So yes, we have improved our utilization from about 66% to above 70% in the last quarter. And we see an increasing trend of that. So, the first focus for us is to get to 75% utilization by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: Robust pipeline driven by global OEM SDV programs and large deal wins; Suzuki second engineering center opened
items.quote: We are happy to report a robust pipeline momentum that is driven by global OEM SDV programs and other large deal wins. This quarter, we opened the second engineering center in a partnership with Suzuki that focuses on cloud hardware and loop simulation setup.

items.statement: Media & Communications grew 6.8% QoQ on large deal ramp-ups; Transportation 0.7% QoQ; Healthcare -2.3% QoQ; System Integration 20.5% QoQ
items.quote: Our Media & Communication business reported a smart 6.8% sequential growth, strengthened by ramp-ups of large deals, which we announced in the previous quarters and new deal wins.

items.statement: Customer concentration improving in auto and healthcare with multiple multimillion-dollar accounts; media still concentrated
items.quote: I think both in automotive and health care, I think we have gone a long way. We have multiple now customers that are really touching that multimillion-dollar sort of mark.

items.statement: 90 bps FX gain offset by 40 bps higher employee costs (campus onboarding, sales strengthening) and 30 bps AI/partnership spend; net 20 bps operating margin uptick
items.quote: We got 90 basis point gain from the favorable currency movement, which is net of the cross-currency impact on the cost side also due to the higher salary cost converted into the actual INR reported. The 90-basis point of exchange gain got offset by the 40 basis points of the higher employee costs.

items.statement: Attrition up marginally due to denominator effect; wage hikes for part of team planned in Q3 if cybersecurity situation normalizes
items.quote: I think attrition has gone up marginally. It's not very significant. We are aware of that. We're keeping a watch on it. I think it's also the fact that numbers in the denominator go down, so automatically the calculation goes up.

items.statement: No significant new capex added; depreciation declining and expected to continue for 2-3 more quarters
items.quote: I think there is declining depreciation in our books due to no new capex being added/significant capex that has been added. I think we are well managed capacity that we can live with it for at least some period or may be few more quarters.

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected 26-26.5% for full year; Q2 higher due to non-exempt other income and lower SEZ revenue
items.quote: Otherwise, what we believe is that for the full year our effective tax rate would be anything that would hover around 26% to 26.5%.

items.statement: Cybersecurity incident at top auto client pushed out September project starts; would have shown constant currency positive growth without it
items.quote: If that incident had not happened, we would have definitely shown CC positive growth. And that would give you an idea that, look, that instance did affect us a little bit.

items.statement: Not competing with Chinese firms; customers (European OEMs) compete with Chinese EVs driving outsourcing to best-cost locations
items.quote: So we are not competing with the Chinese. Our customers are competing with the Chinese, right? So number one. And in most countries like Germany, for example, the auto industry is the backbone of the economy there.

items.statement: Europe emission norms (55% reduction vs 1990 by 2030) continue; US norms relaxed causing portfolio reset at legacy OEMs
items.quote: I think Europe - they are focused on the emission norms, right? I think a 55% reduction in carbon emission as compared to 1990 levels and so on, I think that is a norm that they have put in place by 2030 or so.

items.statement: US market grew 7.9% QoQ; Europe #1, US #2 in auto revenue; Japan and India significant; China minimal presence
items.quote: Our key markets continue to be volatile, but we delivered strong quarter-on-quarter growth across key overseas markets led by U.S. market, which grew 7.9% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: No M&A discussed; partnerships with Suzuki, Infineon, Qualcomm, Dell for technology collaboration
items.quote: we've announced a deal with Suzuki last year based out of our center in Pune and that has ramped up pretty well for us. So the deal that we announced recently was a cloud - based hardware and simulation deal

items.statement: AI infrastructure partnerships and investments increasing (30 bps margin impact)
items.quote: Another 30-basis points was compensated with other expenses, which is typically towards the partnerships and AI-related infrastructure that we are building.

items.statement: Dedicated Technology Center launched for Bayer devices and Radiology; multi-year, multi-million dollar deal

items.statement: FY26 International revenue growth expected to be better than FY25 (which was ~70 bps in constant currency)
items.quote: Based on client conversations, Q2 revenue growth and TCV , and a strong demand pipeline, we see FY26 International revenue growth to be better than last fiscal year.

items.statement: Aspirational operating margin band remains 26-28%

items.statement: Deal pipeline shows strong momentum with healthy mix of cost optimization, transformation, services and platform deals
items.quote: Our deal pipeline continues to show strong momentum with a healthy mix of cost optimization and transformatio n deals as well as services and platform deals across new and existing businesses.

items.quote: We expect to achieve 1 gigawatt over a period of five to seven years. And our calculation roughly is about every 150 -megawatt will require a capex of about $1 billion.

items.statement: Mega deal win with Tryg Insurance using AI-enabled differentiated solutions

items.quote: In response to economic and demand volatility, clients are consolidating vendors to achieve transformation objectives effectively and efficiently. We are finding good success in many such large deals using our differentiated, AI-infused solutions.

items.statement: Accounts receivable at 75 days outstanding in dollar terms; net cash from operations $1.5B (110.1% of net income); free cash flow $1.4B; invested funds $6.3B
items.quote: Our accounts receivable was at 75 days outstanding in dollar terms. Net cash from operations was $1.5 billion, which is 110.1% of net income. Free cash flows were at $1.4 billion and invested funds at the end of the period stood at $6.3 billion.

items.statement: Data center subsidiary to use combination of equity and debt; finance partners for equity
items.quote: We also clarified that this would be a combination of equity and debt, and we'll also bring in finance partners for the equity.

items.quote: Today our Board approved creation of a TCS Subsidiary that will focus on building a Sovereign AI datacenter with a capacity of up to 1 Giga Watt.

items.statement: Sudeep Kunnumal appointed CHRO effective Oct 1, 2025
items.quote: I would like to warmly welcome Sudeep Kunnumal who has taken charge as our CHRO w.e.f. 01st October, 2025.

items.statement: H1B usage minimal: ~500 associates travelled to US this financial year; business model adaptable to immigration policy changes
items.quote: Just about ~ 500 associates have travelled to the US in this financial year on H-1B. We believe our business model will be able to adapt quickly to any changes in immigration policy.

items.statement: Revenue: ₹65,799 crore, up 3.7% QoQ and 2.4% YoY reported; 0.8% QoQ constant currency; International revenue 0.6% QoQ constant currency

items.quote: We have already achieved over 50% of our full-year revenue guidance of INR 430 crores within the first half year.

items.quote: We continue to target a 30%, 35% CAGR growth over the next three years, supported by backward and forward integration initiatives expected to enhance operating margins by 3% to 4%.

items.quote: Currently, what we are calculating is at a 20% higher price than what if we would have manufactured. So, when we go into backward integration, that would give us that much more revenue stream and that much PAT increase.

items.statement: Quota baseline calculation: average of 2024-2026 import/production/consumption determines future allocation
items.quote: The baseline years, 2024, 2025, 2026, whatever import, whatever production, whatever consumption, whatever you're doing in these three years, the total is added and divided by three, and that will be the baseline figure.

items.statement: Targets 30% compounded growth through expansion and backward integration
items.quote: The 30% is a very aggressive, very strong target that we have put on ourselves, and we hope to achieve and grow it, meaning through expansion, through backward integrations, through everything.

items.statement: Khalapur plant construction almost complete, fit-out starting, expects operational by December end
items.quote: The Khalapur plant is meaning the construction is almost over. Now, the fit-out of the plant and machinery will be starting currently, number one. items.quote: The Bhilwara plant should be between 3 years and 4 years. Maybe less if it's a good year. Helium, if you come into the good cycle, maybe one year.

items.quote: Like, say, 32%, I'll just give you an example. Two years ago, it was $2.2. It was $1.9 actually. Then it went up to $2.2. Then it went up to $2.7. Then it remained stagnant at $4.7. Then it moved up to $5.5. Now today, it's $7.5. In three years, this is the flow.

The manufacturing capacities in India are much in excess of this. It's like 30,000 to 40,000 tonnes after our plant also comes up.

items.statement: Current non-manufacturing operations have no meaningful capacity utilization; manufacturing capacity utilization critical for profitability
items.quote: Current plants that we have are not manufacturing plants. So, capacity utilization, meaning during the IPO, basically, SEBI and the merchant banker said, we want the capacity, we want the capacity utilization. What is not a manufacturing plant, it's illogical to speak on capacity.

items.quote: China is like Saudi Arabia with oil. If China decides that I want to reduce the price, the whole world's price will come down. The 85% global -- 85%, 90% capacity is with them.

items.statement: Raised full-year Services revenue growth guidance to 4%-5% in constant currency; company-level guidance unchanged at 3%-5%

items.statement: Full-year EBIT margin guidance maintained at 17%-18%

items.statement: Q2 EBIT margin at 17.5%, up 116 bps sequentially

items.statement: Pipeline at record high, well distributed across segments with AI central to nearly every deal

items.statement: Software Subscription, Support & Professional Services revenue grew 8% YoY; perpetual license revenue declined

items.statement: Trained 820 black belts in H1; data and AI principal cohorts embedded in >50% priority accounts; identified 14 top AI skills for scaling talent base

items.statement: Localization and H-1B visa fee revision may require higher training and local hiring investments; wage difference minimal but availability a concern
items.quote: Yes, it is definitely something to watch out for, because obviously this trend will mean some higher investments in training, local hiring and related aspects. items.quote: Our recent CTG assets acquisition from HPE has been delivering financial results in line with our business plan. It has also given us the opportunity to address the needs of a much larger global telecom client base with a richer value proposition.

items.statement: Total deposits rose 1.5% Q-o-Q, 15.1% Y-o-Y to INR 39,211 crores
items.quote: Total deposits rose 1.5% Q-o-Q, up 15.1 % Y-o-Y at INR 39,211 crores.

items.statement: CASA grew 14.9% Q-o-Q, 22.1% Y-o-Y to INR 10,783 crores, crossing INR 10,000 crores first time
items.quote: CASA grew 14.9 % Q-o-Q and 22.1 % Y-o-Y to INR 10,783 crores, crossing INR 10,000 crores for the first time, while retail TD plus CASA deposits remained around 71 % of our total deposits.

items.statement: Annualized attrition rate at ~20%, flat from last quarter
items.quote: Yes, we are at an annualized attrition rate of around 20% now.

items.statement: Deepak Agarwal joined as Head of Strategy and Transformation
items.quote: Before I conclude, I would like to introduce Mr. Deepak Agarwal, who has joined as our Head of Strategy and Transformation.

items.statement: Secured book target 65-70% of total loan book in 5-year strategy
items.quote: As part of our 5-year strategy, we have contemplated that our secured book would be in the region of 65 to 70 % and the remaining would be the unsecured part.

items.statement: Karnataka microfinance stress improving, slippages contribution down from 33% to below 20%
items.quote: This quarter, we have seen that number coming below 20%. So there is a significant improvement in Karnataka portfolio.

items.statement: Written-off pool of ~INR 750 crores, expecting 15-20% recovery in FY26
items.quote: Put together, this is about INR 750-odd crores, and we expect anything between 15% to 20% recovery from this pool during this financial year.

items.statement: Universal bank license application with RBI, no material opex impact expected immediately
items.quote: Our application is with the Reserve Bank of India, and they are evaluating and assessing our application, its contents. So the matter rests there. As we said earlier, we will await the decision of the RBI and as far as expenses or additional expenditure that we will need to do, I think nothing changes immediately as we become a universal bank.

items.statement: Q2 order intake nearly Rs 500 crore with book-to-bill ratio of 1.6; H1 cumulative order intake crossed Rs 1,000 crore, up 130% YoY
items.quote: We reported order intake of nearly 500 crores with a book-to-bill ratio of 1.6. So, this exceeds the expectation we set in our last call of maintaining a B2B ratio of above 1 and is a testament to the consistency and effectiveness of our sales effort. For H1, our cumulative order intake crossed 1,000 crores, reflecting growth of 130% year-over-year.

items.statement: Order book increased to Rs 2,291 crore after net addition of Rs 159.3 crore in Q2; third consecutive quarter of order book growth
items.quote: Our order backlog, as Rajendra indicated, we had an order intake of close to 500 crores in Q2, which means we have added another 159.3 crores to the order book. So, further increasing the or der book to 2,291

items.statement: Full-year book-to-bill ratio expected at 1.4-1.5; YoY revenue growth expected to resume from Q4 FY26; no formal FY27 guidance given
items.quote: And we also expect for the year, as of now, what we see is the book to bill ratio may go to 1.4 to 1.5 for the year. And pipeline strength based on the traction, what we are seeing it in India and B2B segments are really encouraging. H2 outlook is really promising, setting the stage for the growth to revive year-over-year growth story starting from Q4, FY26.

items.statement: EBITDA margin reached double digits at 10.0% in Q2, up 192 bps YoY and over 100 bps QoQ despite 20% revenue decline; margin expansion driven by favorable mix and exit of low-margin large order
items.quote: Despite the year -on-year degrowth in revenue, we have been able to keep the EBITDA almost flat, the reason being the expansion in margins. And so, it is more than 100 basis points increased se quentially and 192 basis points increased in margins year -on-year. Now, this margin growth is despite the loss of volume

items.statement: Management confident of sustaining and growing double-digit EBITDA margins going forward due to high-quality order backlog
items.quote: This quarter, our revenue mix is significantly stronger supported by a substantial backlog of high margin orders which enhances our confidence in sustaining and growing beyond double -digit margins. I am pleased an d you will see in the financials that we have reported double -digit EBITDA margins and we continue to see significant traction in those

items.statement: Strong momentum in build-to-spec orders with wins from global OEMs including Japanese eVTOL company and Indian EV charging solutions client backed by global giant; several accounts in advanced negotiations
items.quote: I am pleased to announce a new logo through a BTS order from a Japanese electric vertical take-off and landing urban air mobility company, focused on the future of mobility. So, this program is currently in the development phase and is expected to enter mass production in the coming year, reinforcing our global footprint. We also secured a strategic win from a key automotive client specializing in

items.statement: Focus on expanding non-A&D sectors (industrial, medical, automotive/EV infrastructure) and domestic Indian market to diversify customer base; new customer pipeline building for Q3-Q4
items.quote: As you've seen in terms of expanding the non-A&D sector, is where we are working out. And we also have the sales team, which is basically right now focusing on the new customers. So, we are seeing some of those things in the pipeline. So, there are a lot of the orders on the pipeline in terms of new customers, where we are driving, and also the focus on the Indian-based customers.

items.statement: Revenue mix shifting: Aerospace 37%, Defence 8%, Industrial 30%, Medical 15% (vs ~70% A&D a year ago); box build mix growing 34% YoY, replacing PCBA; box build stickier and higher margin
items.quote: we see the industry mix on the left side where Aerospace is about 37%, Defence is 8%, Industrial is 30% and Medical is 15%. If you remember this from a year ago, this was very different. We were very heavy on Aerospace and Defence. It was close to 70% of our business. But with the acquisition of Altek and the growth we are seeing in the industrial and tech segments in the res t of the business, th

items.statement: Net working capital improved to 139 days from 165 days; fourth consecutive quarter of positive free cash flow; improvements in DSO and customer advances
items.quote: We have also made some improvements in the DIO in the 2nd Quarter. And you will see the seasonality, the Q1 numbers are usually low and therefore all the metrics around the net working capital show an elevated number. But we see improvement as we go through the year. So, we see that the net working capital has actually dropped to 139 days from 165 days. This also means that we have generated posit

items.statement: US business expected to contribute ~40% of revenue in FY26; tariff discussions ongoing with customers - solutions include shifting ship-to locations, customers absorbing tariffs, or rerouting; company will not absorb tariffs given low margi
items.quote: Our US business is roughly, I think, for this year, we expect 40% of our business to come from the US. And look, I think there are many, many conversations going on with customers to see how we can offset the impact of the tariffs. There is no one solution. It works differently for different customers. Some c ustomers want us to change the ship to location to where their customers are, so that the

items.statement: Build-to-spec (BTS) orders now >10% of order book; BTS revenue ~5% in FY26, expected to grow in FY27; mass production for major BTS contracts from FY28 onwards
items.quote: than 10% of the order book in build to spec in the current order. Maitri Shah: And how do we see it growing forward in the next six months for FY26? Shrinivas Kulkarni: Absolutely, we see it growing heavily because we are focusing on b uild to spec as a focus area as far as they are concerned. I think that's how we differentiate ourselves compared to some of the competitors that are there in the s

items.statement: Israel geopolitical situation significantly impacted revenue quantum and predictability; stability returning expected to support business; some decision-making slowed in region
items.quote: I think it is important to note that Israel is a key market for us and the geopolitical situation there has had a significant impact both in the quantum of revenue and predictability of revenue. Where credit is due and thanks to President Trump, we now can expect stability to return to the region which will also greatly support stability in our business given the importance of I srael as a market

items.statement: Altek earnout reversed due to unmet performance conditions, resulting in extraordinary gain; acquisition intact and positioned for US growth; normalized PAT margin 4% vs reported 10.3%
items.quote: As you all remember, we had made an acquisition about a year ago and there were certain perfo rmance conditions to which the earnouts were tied. And those performance conditions have not been met. Therefore, the earnout is reversed in the books which comes in as other income, giving you an extraordinary gain this time. I want to assure you that the acquisition is intact, the company is doing well.

items.statement: Altek synergies materializing in Year 2: existing DLM India customers moving to Altek US facility; Altek customers also bringing work to India; quotes submitted and orders expected in Q3
items.quote: So right now, we have some of the opportunities going on with the Altek, with our unit there in US in Torrington. So, some of our existing customers, we have submitted some of the quotes, and they are in the positive direction. We will be expecting some of those orders will be coming in this quarter. And a similar thing, we are also seeing this synergy coming from their side to us, year two. So, w

items.statement: Q2 revenue Rs 310.6 crore, down 20% YoY due to completion of large defence order; rest of business grew ~15%; sequential growth trajectory returning; H1 typically 40-45% of full year
items.quote: We did a revenue of 310.6 crores, which signifies a degrowth of 20% year -on-year. Our order backlog, as Rajendra indicated, we had an order intake of close to 500 crores in Q2, which means we have added another 159.3 crores to the order book. So, further increasing the or der book to 2,291 crores. EBITDA is 312 million or 31.2 crores. Despite the year -on-year degrowth in revenue, we have been ab

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance maintained at 25%-30% for FY26
items.quote: We have given a guidance of 25%. We believe because of lot of tailwinds, we should grow a bit higher than that. But we will still keep our guidance conservative saying between 25%-30%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 24%-25%
items.quote: Sustainable EBITDA margin will be around 24%, 25%.

items.statement: H-1B visa changes driving students from US to UK, benefiting business
items.quote: With reference to H-1B visa, yes, there is some sentimental impact for US education. But for us, the number or the revenue contribution from US operations is very low. So for us, any kind of negative news for US is positive.

items.statement: Africa is the main growth driver currently with highest percentage growth
items.quote: The main growth is coming from Africa at the moment, where the percentage growth is a bit higher compared to any other geographies.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin 39% driven by INR 4 crore forex gain and university bonuses; sustainable margin 24%-25%
items.quote: There are two components which has helped in this quarter. One, if you remember last quarter we had roughly INR 4 crores of losses because of forex. Now that we do our hedging and the pound has cooled down, so we have gained roughly INR 4 crores as a forex.

items.statement: University partnerships grew to 250+ from 170 last year
items.quote: Normally, with universities, today we represent more than 250 universities as on end of quarter 2, which was I think 170 last year.

items.statement: Active agent network at ~4,600
items.quote: In terms of our active agents, it's roughly 4600 as of today.

items.statement: Student loan distribution to go live in Q3 FY26 with 7-8 NBFC/bank tie-ups; expected to contribute 1%-2% of EBITDA eventually
items.quote: Yes, we have signed up with more than 7 or 8 NBFC and banks. And we believe the company should go live with loan as a distributor in coming quarter, quarter 3.

items.statement: Accommodation service already live on platform
items.quote: This quarter, we started the accommodation as a service, and it's already live on our platform. We have started getting attraction.

items.statement: Revenue by destination: UK 90%-95% in Q2, Ireland ~7% last year, concentration decreasing
items.quote: In terms of revenue, most of the revenues would be coming from UK, roughly 90%-95% because quarter two, rest of the country don't offer any intake, except one university in Ireland.

items.statement: Tech integration for new university partners typically within a month
items.quote: Once the university confirms that they are happy to onboard, tech integration and others does not take much time. Usually, it is done within a month.

items.statement: Platform adding AI and automation capabilities continuously
items.quote: In terms of platform, we have added a lot of capabilities like automation and AI. Last time when we had a meet, we mentioned that we are looking at adding those ones. So, those capabilities are already integrated and this is a continuous process.

items.statement: UK tightening immigration rules for non-genuine students (ILR 5 to 10 years, language requirements); already baked into growth
items.quote: UK is tightening immigration rules more for work than for students with reference to increasing maintenance or other recommendat ions from white paper that has been announced almost six months, seven months earlier and it is already baked into the growth

items.statement: UK-India FTA positive for sector; 9 UK universities signed up for India campuses (Southampton Delhi live Sept intake)
items.quote: Yes, there are multiple universities. Roughly 9 universities signed up when UK Prime Minister was in India. So they are opening campus in various geographies. For example, Delhi, Gift City, Mumbai, Bangalore.

items.statement: Forex gain of INR 4 crores in Q2 after hedging; pound cooled down
items.quote: Now that we do our hedging and the pound has cooled down, so we have gained roughly INR 4 crores as a forex. So all the losses have been recovered.

items.statement: Negative operating cash flow due to delayed university payments; trade payables INR 95 cr, other financial liabilities INR 56 cr
items.quote: This quarter, the amount of money which were expected to receive from the university, that gets a bit delayed. As a resul t, we have not paid to our channel partners. So the trade table is negative

items.statement: Payment cycle: university pays 15-30 days after student enrollment confirmation; company pays agents immediately upon receipt
items.quote: That's the time we would recognize the revenue. At the same time, that is the time when within 15 to 30 days, the university would make the payment to us and we would make the payment to the agent immediately once we receive the payment from the university.

items.statement: Application conversion rate 8%-10% overall; China 25%-30%, Africa 5%-6%
items.quote: standard conversion is between 8% and 10%. Again, it depends upon where the application source is. If it is, let's say, China, t he conversion can be 25%, 30%. While if it is, let's say, Africa, the conversion rate is typically 5%, 6

items.statement: Student distribution: 60%-70% via agents, 30%-35% direct to university
items.quote: Though there is no fixed data, but based on the survey done with the university, roughly 60% to 70% of the students go via agents while 30% to 35% go via direct online application.

items.statement: Employee cost expected at 2%-3% of revenue; tech cost ~4% combined; growth slower than revenue
items.quote: Roughly the employee cost should be between 2% and 3%. Plus tech cost added together would be roughly 4% altogether.

items.statement: Sector large with room for multiple players; China market has big competitors like Kaiser
items.quote: There will always be a competition so there are multiple companies, but the sector is very big and there is a room for everybody to grow.

items.statement: UK concentration risk acknowledged; diversifying to Middle East, Australia, New Zealand, Southeast Asia, India as destination
items.quote: We believe over the next 1 or 2 years, our numbers should go up quite big in both of multiple of the se geographies, which I have mentioned. And that should bring down the concentration further down and bring risk lower

items.statement: UAE subsidiary set up in last 6-8 months for Middle East expansion
items.quote: We have tied up with multiple UAE universities in the last six to eight months. The other thing what we have done is we have set up a subsidiary of Crizac in UAE for our expansion into Middle East and Gulf countries.

items.statement: Cost of services (agent commissions) variable and moves proportionally with revenue; limits operating leverage
items.quote: Our major expenses is cost of services, which we pay to our channel partners, which is more or less constant. So with increase in top line, our cost of services increase proportionately.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 17.94% in Q2 FY26, up 122 bps sequentially and 447 bps year-on-year
items.quote: EBITDA further improved in quarter 2 F '26 to 17.94%, plus 122 basis points sequentially and plus 447 basis points year-to-year.

items.statement: Management expects further margin improvement in Q3 and Q4 FY26 but cannot quantify in basis points
items.quote: So going forward, I think it is -- it should be a little better only from here. But we can't quantify any numbers in any basis points.

items.statement: Current margin trajectory is sustainable and superior to COVID-era 20% margin which was driven by one-off fuel price drop
items.quote: But sustainably, our margin trajectory was around 14% to 15% to 16%. So we have moved into a new orbit of margin. But when we will reach 20% or 21% -- because even that 20% is not comparable with this margin because this margin is based on the overall cost optimization.

items.statement: Management expects volume growth in Q3 FY26 (October-December) after flat H1
items.quote: we are pretty hopeful this quarter, October to December, we should have some volume growth. The exact number, we'd not like to say, but we should definitely have some volume growth this quarter.

items.statement: H2 FY26 will definitely have good volume growth after 0% growth in H1
items.quote: H1 was -- we had 0 volume growth. H2 will definitely have some good volume growth.

items.statement: No new capacity additions currently; focus is on running existing plants at 100% utilization
items.quote: We are not adding any capacity right now. The first focus is to run all our manufacturing plants to 100% capacity.

items.statement: Current manufacturing vs outsourcing ratio is 75:25; will outsource from Gujarat if demand increases
items.quote: And our current ratio is 25% outsourcing versus manufacturing. If the demand goes up, we'll immediately outsource from Gujarat and supplement the demand.

items.statement: Packing box reengineering across all plants yields INR 30-35 crores annual savings
items.value: INR30 crores, INR 35 crores on an annual basis
items.quote: reengineering of the packing boxes across all our plants across the country, which has resulted in substantial savings of INR30 crores, INR 35 crores on an annual basis.

items.statement: Cost savings accruing across raw materials, purchased finished goods, salaries, and administrative overhead
items.quote: So line item is -- like the savings will accrue in raw material, savings will accrue in purchase of finished goods, saving will accrue in salary, wages and saving will accrue in administrative overhead.

items.statement: Power and fuel cost per unit unchanged; lower absolute cost due to lower production volumes
items.quote: Power and fuel remains the same. Power and fuel is lower because of the lower production, Sneha. Cost is the same.

items.statement: Unified purchasing leveraging combined volumes for better negotiations with suppliers
items.quote: So with unification of sales, we have also unified our purchases and utilizing our power of volumes for better negotiations.

items.statement: Pricing gap between Kajaria and Morbi segment remains at approximately 20%
items.quote: Pricing gap between Morbi and Kajaria is about 20%, and that remains.

items.statement: Tile segment revenue flat at INR 1,051 crores; Bathware grew 14% to INR 102 crores; Adhesives grew to INR 32 crores from INR 18 crores
items.quote: Tile segment remained flattish year-to-year, at INR1,051 crores compared to INR1,054 crores in quarter 2 F '25. Bathware segment registered a 14% growth in revenue, reaching INR 102 crores compared to INR 90 crores in quarter 2 F '25. Revenue from Adhesives grew to INR32 crores in quarter 2 F '26 as compared to INR18 crores in quarter 2 F '25.

items.statement: Dealer unification completed: reduced from 3 sales people per dealer to 1-2; dealers very happy with simplified structure
items.quote: From the distributor point of view, they're very, very happy. So earlier, what used to happen was, three people used to go to a single dealer. And now we have reduced that to one. And if it's a very, very big dealer, maybe two.

items.statement: New architect/influencer team of 18-20 people onboarded to drive specification sales
items.quote: we started making a team, and we already have about 18, 20 people who are on board. And we're going to further strengthen the team. Their job is only to go and meet influencers, architects, interior designers and talk about Kajaria, Kerovit, Gresbond , whatever products we are offering.

items.statement: Sales incentive structure unified and made purely volume and growth-linked across all verticals
items.quote: Now everything is volume and growth linked, that only if you reach a certain growth percentage only then the incentive gets applicable. And the more you sell, the more you get more. So they should get a carrot and a stick.

items.statement: Current revenue mix approximately 70% retail, 30% projects (private + government)
items.quote: See, our current percentage should be about 70% retail, 30% projects. But we have to work on all the fronts, whether it is a dealer network or the project network to look at volumes.

items.statement: Management consultant engaged to identify non-performing dealers, white spaces, and optimize distribution network state-by-state
items.quote: we got a lot of information that where some dealers need to close, some white spaces are there where the dealers have to be made. So the consultant is going to structure the entire thing for us how we can penetrate further into the market and increase our market share.

items.statement: Target to increase exclusive showrooms from current 450 with 1,850 dealers over next couple of years
items.quote: Currently, we have 450 exclusive showrooms of Kajaria with 1,850 dealers. Our target is to increase that more in the next couple of years and get more exclusive distribution showrooms.

items.statement: Store branding unification underway: Prima Plus, Eternity, Galaxy etc. to be replaced by common Kajaria branding by Q4 FY26
items.quote: all Prima Plus, Eternity World, all those terminology will go. There will be a common name, maybe like a Kajaria Galaxy or a Kajaria World or whatever. So that work is already going on. We just got this consultant recently. So maybe in the next 1 or 2 months, we'll have the entire plan ready. And the last quarter, Jan to March, we will get everything implemented.

items.statement: Working capital days reduced to 56 days as of September 30, 2025 from 58 days on June 30, 2025
items.quote: As of 30th September '25, the working capital days reduced by 2 days, to 56 days, compared to 58 days on 30th of June '25.

items.statement: Industry exports grew 9-10% YoY to INR 8,300 crores in April-September 2025; full year FY26 expected at INR 18,000 crores
items.quote: Full year should be INR18,000 crores.

items.statement: Approximately 250 employees removed as part of cost rationalization; no increments given this year; hiring fresh talent for systems, IT, HR
items.quote: Plus we've also worked on reducing our purchase price and outsourcing of tiles of ceramic and polished vitrified, removed a lot of people, around 250 people.

items.statement: Promoter directors voluntarily forego salaries this year as part of lean organization drive
items.quote: One, we didn't give any increment to our people this time. So as a management, we said, let's not let the company become stronger.

items.statement: Dividend payout increased slightly vs last 2 years but remains within 40-50% of earnings policy
items.quote: We have a dividend policy to pay between 40% to 50% of our earnings. So we have -- this is not for the first time we have paid. We have been paying for the last 3, 4 years.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue INR 1,186 crores in Q2 FY26, marginal 1% YoY growth due to low tile volume growth and closure of sanitaryware division
items.quote: In quarter 2 F '26, our consolidated revenue stood at INR1,186 crores, a marginal growth of 1% year-to-year compared to the corresponding period last year, mainly due to low growth in tiles volume and absence supply sales due to the closure of this division.

items.statement: PAT grew 58% YoY to INR 133 crores in Q2 FY26
items.quote: PAT for the quarter grew by 58%, to INR133 crores in quarter 2 F '26 as compared to INR 84 crores in quarter 2 F '25.

items.statement: Nepal JV sold 0.7 million sqm in Q2; focus on inventory liquidation over profit; turmoil in country being monitored
items.quote: So we sold roughly 0.7 million square meters in quarter two. And you know there is a lot of turmoil also happening in that country. So we are just waiting and watching and trying to sell the capacity as we keep on going along.

items.statement: Abnormal rainfall caused crop losses and delayed harvesting, limiting pest infestation and increasing sales returns due to lower farmer demand.
items.quote: Abnormal and uneven rainfall distribution in Q2 of 2026 has led to significant crop losses in pre-agronomic consuming states. The heavy rain plus floods, water logging and submergence of large farmland areas, which severely affected crops like soybean, maize, cotton and pulses.

items.statement: Global agrochemical demand shows cautious optimism with gradual improvement, stable pricing, and strong export demand from U.S. and Brazil.
items.quote: Global signals for recovery in the agrochemical sector in 2025 show cautious optimism with gradual demand improvement supported by stable pricing and strong export demand, particularly from markets like the U.S. and Brazil.

items.statement: Export revenue grew 33% in Q2; H1 export revenue grew ~51% to INR312 crores from INR207 crores.
items.quote: H1 absolute number is INR312 crores, okay? And this would be more like 51% growth against last year, which was INR207 crores at H1 level, on a H1 level.

items.statement: Seed business EBITDA margin target is 23-25%; H1 margin close to target, Q3-Q4 may see slight dilution due to lower revenue base.
items.quote: Our target is that we should bring our seed business to -- in the range of 23% to 25% EBITDA margin. And first half, we are very close. Second cost, there could be slightly dilution because revenue will be smaller and the cost remains same.

items.statement: Domestic B2C gross margin improved marginally due to better cost and SG&A management.
items.quote: But our domestic B2C business actually on an overall basis because of the better cost management and all, and better SG&A management has shown marginal improvement from a GC perspective.

items.statement: Capex spend envisaged at around INR50 crores for the year.
items.quote: We envisage spends on capex would be around INR50 crores.

items.statement: Commercialized planned capacity expansion with new efficient technologies; Acephate capacity utilization improved in H1 FY26.
items.quote: We also have commercialized the planned capacity expansion with new efficient technologies. Acephate has also shown improvement in H1 fiscal year '26 in comparison to the same period of last year, improving capacity utilization.

items.statement: Launched new herbicide 'Deeweed' and fungicide 'Dodrio'; 8 new products YTD, volumes more than doubled on YTD basis.
items.quote: All I can tell you, these products were introduced towards in quarter 4 of last year as a test launch. And we actually have more than doubled their volume as we speak on a YTD basis. So it looks like good traction and good momentum in the market.

items.statement: Seed portfolio focused on 5 key crops (cotton, maize, millet, mustard, rice); cotton hybrid 'Diggaz' showing strong response.
items.quote: We are significantly pleased with the response we are getting for our cotton hybrid 'Diggaz', and we believe it has significant growth runway. Our focus is primarily on 5 key crops, cotton, maize, millet, mustard and rice for our seed segment.

items.statement: Export growth driven by new customers in existing geographies and early supplies to new geographies (France, Malaysia, Spain).
items.quote: Yes. So for the current product, I would say, bulk of our business still comes from existing geographies, but we have been able to add new customers in the same geographies. There is some growth in newer geographies, but I think those are early supplies. W e have to build on those businesses

items.statement: U.S. tariffs up to 60% on Chinese imports pushing manufacturing repatriation; Chinese players may shift volumes to Brazil causing pricing pressure.
items.quote: U.S.-China trade tensions, including tariff up to 60% are pushing U.S. manufacturing repatriation and reducing Chinese export competitiveness.

items.statement: Government regulation of bio-stimulants creating short-term challenges but long-term positive for organized players; supply issues now sorted.
items.quote: Yes. So I think, yes, what government is trying to do probably was overdue and that simply means that there are challenges for everybody in the short term. But from a long -term perspective, I see this as a positive development because it does help in bringing more, what you call, organized market players.

items.statement: 85% of U.S. export business is technical supply exempt from tariffs; only 15% formulation business impacted.
items.quote: So yes, I'll say this, U.S. is our primary business, right? Now U.S. has tariff challenges, but fortunately, for us, 85% of our business is technical supply that is not impacted by tariffs as of now. Only 15% of export business is impacted by tariff becaus e it is formulation based, right

items.statement: Inventory levels moderated and collections improved; healthy cash balance of INR454 crores as of 30th September.
items.quote: Our inventory levels have moderated. Collections have also improved. We have a healthy cash and liquid balance of INR454 crores as of 30th September.

items.statement: Domestic pricing subdued due to promotional schemes; bulk of 10% domestic revenue decline attributed to pricing pressure.
items.quote: Yes, bulk of it is pricing, there's some volume as well.

items.statement: Industry growth expected at low to mid-single digit for H1 FY26.
items.quote: So it's too early to comment because a lot of numbers are yet to come. But based on what I hear, that industry is not likely to grow beyond low to mid-single digit.

items.statement: Fertilizer shortage diverts farmer capital away from crop protection, creating receivable challenges for pesticide and seed companies.
items.quote: But when there's a shortage of fertilizer, a lot of market money which should come to pesticide and seed companies, tends to go to fertilizer players first. And that puts challenges on the receivables of the pesticide and seed companies.

items.statement: R&D budget INR60-70 crores annually; focus shifted to modern breeding tools (non-GM) and 9(3) registrations; wheat and rice herbicides planned for next year.
items.quote: Our R&D budget ranges from INR60 crores to INR70 crores per year. And I think what we're trying to do, not trying to cut on R&D, but trying to get it more focused.

items.statement: Rabi season prospects look slightly better due to residual moisture; extended kharif spillover of 10-15% into October expected.
items.quote: Yes. So two things can happen. I think there could be some spillover of kharif season 10%, 15% to October because there could be extended rabi season for some crops.

items.statement: CSM business <5% of H1 export revenue (INR312 crores); H1 CSM showed degrowth due to customer timing (Boeing order rescheduling).
items.quote: CSM, I said this H1 was relatively small. In fact, majority of the business has come from export of technical and domestic institutional business. CSM is relatively small this time.

items.statement: CSM margins remain intact despite revenue degrowth.
items.quote: Yes. But our CSM margins continue to remain intact.

items.statement: Soil & Plant Health revenue flat in H1 (INR225 crores annualized) vs 20% growth target; impacted by rain and regulatory changes.

items.statement: Illegal HTBt cotton adoption in South/Central India creating higher returns for organized seed companies; impact depends on harvest outcomes.

items.statement: Expect rabi season to be better than previous years; positive on Q3 and Q4 domestic offtake after fertilizer supply settles.
items.quote: I'm expecting rabi prospects look slightly better at this point of time. I know there are challenges in terms of fertilizer supply.
