items.statement: Channel inventory normalized in U.S.; demand stable but pricing pressure seen in export markets.
items.quote: I think given that channel inventory is normalized, I do not see pressure in the demand, I only see pressure on prices.

items.statement: Q3 disbursement guidance of INR800-850 crores conservative and INR1,000-1,100 crores aggressive
items.quote: we should end up disbursing anything around INR1,100 crores in Q3, which would be fairly close to what we had budgeted for. However, if this trend is not retained for long after Diwali, maybe we will have a conservative number of about INR800 crores, INR850 crores in Q3.

items.statement: Full year AUM target of close to INR4,000 crores for FY26
items.quote: So, we had initially given a guidance about INR4,000 crores, INR4,200 crores. So we will reach close to the INR4,000 crores number.

items.statement: Target ROE of 2-2.5% in next 12 months, scaling to 3.25% thereafter, and 4% ROA at INR10,000 crores AUM by 2028
items.quote: target ROE that we have taken as an internal as a three year targets, we want to operate at 4 percentage. As far as next one, one and a half years, we are expecting -- first target is to reach to 2 percentage to 2.5 percentage, which we want to be there in the next 12 months.

items.statement: Full year FY26 ROA target of around 2% on conservative basis
items.quote: For the full year, we are -- so right now, I'm expecting since the scaling of the business will be done from now onwards in the next six months, I am expecting somewhere around 2 percentage sir. On a very conservative side.

items.quote: credit cost, though from -- as far as the computation of ROA is concerned, I will be taking the same number for Q3 onwards -- for Q3 also, which is approximately in the range of 2% to 2.10%.

items.statement: GNPA 6.46% (incl. interest) and NNPA 3.07% in Q2; PCR maintained at 60%
items.quote: On POS, we are -- we have reported a GNPA of 5.94 percentage, whereas with interest accrual, we have reported a 6.46 percentage. The PCR remains the highest, which is 60 percentage.

items.statement: Fresh slippages reduced 6% QoQ to INR42 crores (0.67% of standard pool); NPA recoveries increased 69% to INR7-8 crores monthly
items.quote: the total slippages when we say additions to the NPA was INR46 crores in Q1. That has been dropped down to INR42 crores, whereas the book has also been increased, but by a small margin. The slippages, which used to be 0.991 percentage of my standard pool has now been dropped down to 0.67 percentage of my standard pool.

items.statement: eNACH penetration jumped to 92% from 75-80%; 77% of collections now digital vs 23% cash
items.quote: our eNACH penetration has jumped from the 75%, 80 % levels to 92% level. So now for the last 2 months, we are clocking 92% eNACH penetration. items.statement: Average LTV reduced to 80.22% from 84-85% earlier
items.quote: The average LTVs, which company was operating at 84%, 85% till Q1, that is now we are operating at 80.22 percentage.

items.statement: Customer base reached 570,000+ with 51,288 new customers added in Q2
items.quote: we have closed this quarter with INR535 crores of business, while acquiring 51,288 as our new customers. This has taken our customer base to 570,000 plus now.

items.statement: Market share improved to 2.47% pan-India from 2.36% in Q1; dipped slightly to 7.24% from 7.67% in operating locations
items.quote: We have, in fact, been able to improve our market share slightly from 2.36% in Q1 to 2.47% in Q2. This is on the overall pan-India numbers. However, in the locations that we are present, our market share dipped slightly from about 7.67% to 7.24% in Q2.

items.statement: Hiring done in Q2 to support scale-up; productivity gains expected from Q3 to amortize opex increase
items.quote: all the hirings that we have done in the Q2, the results of it will come from Q3 onwards. So therein in Q2 opex, it might seem to be on the higher side. But yes, it will be able to amortize itself while the top line of the company will start getting increased from the Q3.

items.statement: Summer products (ACs, fans, coolers) declined YoY due to shorter summer and high channel inventories; cables maintained steady growth driven by power cables.
items.quote: As regards to the Q2 results, we have delivered a decent overall performance. However, the summer products experienced weakness with overhang of shorter summer and higher channel inventories. Air conditioners, fans and coolers' revenue declined Y -o-Y.

items.statement: Higher working capital in cables and Lloyd reduced cash balances and interest income; expects normalization by Q4.
items.quote: Higher working capital levels, especially for cables and Lloyd has led to a reduction in cash and bank balance, impacting the interest income earned during the quarter. items.statement: GST reduction on ACs, TVs and solar welcomed as positive for consumer sentiment and demand.
items.quote: The recent GST reduction by the government has been a welcome step towards uplifting consumer sentiment and strengthening the demand. Amongst the Havells category, air conditioner, TV and solar has seen GST rate reduction.

items.statement: Channel inventories for summer products elevated; management expects manufacturer-level inventory to normalize by end of Q3.
items.quote: We have been working closely with our channel to increase consumer offtake, and we believe that the channel inventories will normalize by the end of Q3.

items.statement: Lloyd contribution margins declined due to consumer schemes and under-absorption of manufacturing overheads; improvement expected from Q3, real effect in Q4.
items.quote: Yes, we will start seeing improvement in third quarter, but real effect will come in fourth quarter. But ontribution margin is also greatly affected by the under -absorption of manufacturing overhead because as you can imagine, because of the high inventory levels at the end of the first quarter, the production levels were also scaled down.

items.statement: Cables and wires contribution margin target 15-16% blended; Q2 benefited from rising copper prices and inventory gains.
items.quote: I would say with our blend of cables and wires, 15% to 16% is the right contribution margin to assume and so that will continue to strive. Depending upon quarter-to-quarter, some variations may happen, but otherwise, that's what we are striving for.

items.statement: Switchgear contribution margin range 37-40% depending on product mix.
items.quote: I think switchgears, you can fairly assume contribution margin to be around 38%, sometimes 37%, sometimes 39%, 40%. So 37% to 40% is the right range to assume, depending upon the product mix in a particular quarter.

items.statement: Capex guidance: FY26 ~INR 1,450 crore; FY27 estimated ~INR 1,000 crore (final by March).
items.quote: FY 25-26 will be about INR1,450 crores. FY 26-27, right now, it's estimated about INR1,000 crores, but we'll know the exact numbers by end of March.

items.statement: Acquired 39-acre land parcel adjacent to Alwar cable plant for capacity expansion; execution on track.
items.quote: And in this reference, we have acquired a land parcel of 39 acres adjacent to the existing manufacturing facility in Alwar, Rajasthan.

items.statement: ECD: fan degrowth mid-single digits, cooler high degrowth; water heaters and small appliances growing well.
items.quote: We are seeing good growth in the water heater channel as well as the consumer small appliances. We have actually seen a degrowth of fans, not necessarily high single digits, but mid-single digits. But we've also seen a significant degrowth in the cooler because there was already high levels of inventory in the channel.

items.statement: Will pass on cost increases from new BEE norms (Jan 1) despite competitive intensity and inventory overhang; GST reduction benefit largely offset by upcoming price hikes.
items.quote: We are confident that whatever the cost increase will be there. Yes, there are challenges of inventory levels within the secondary trade, but we will be able to pass on. Of course, you can say it depends upon the competition also, but the kind of price increases, which will happen will have to be passed on to the consumer.

items.statement: Early festive demand showing positive momentum; rural growth returning; channel picking up stock and clearing old inventory.
items.quote: I think we definitely see positive momentum, especially also because of the fact that there was some pent -up demand. Until 22nd of September, there was a slowdown of sales. items.statement: B2B demand robust; B2C expected to improve in H2.

items.statement: Premiumization increasing across fans, appliances, water heaters, ACs; premium share high and rising.

items.quote: Havells stand -alone (excluding Lloyd) continues to be about 12% - 13% EBITDA margins, and this will further improve. So I don't think that's really concern about dilution of margins due to increased competition.

items.quote: If you look at switchgear or you look at lighting, for example, our contribution margins and our EBIT margins have remained stable. items.quote: I'm happy to share Heritage has been recognized as the Best Workplace in FMCG 2025 by the Great Place to Work Institute

items.statement: 42 branches opened in FY26 so far; 234 more branches approved and in operationalization pipeline for next 6-9 months
items.quote: Branch opening last year, we opened around 101 branches, last financial year. This year, in this financial year, we have already opened 42 new branches. And another around 240 branches are in the queue where all approvals have been given and they are in different stages of operationalization. And I do hope that these 234 branches also in another 6 to 9 months, they will come into existence and phy

items.statement: Return on equity improved to 19.95% in Q2 FY26, up 305 bps year-on-year
items.quote: There is a steep increase in the return on equity is 305 bps year-on-year currently and return on equity, 19.95% whereas for the last September 2024, it was 16.9%.

items.statement: CASA ratio at 40.52% in Q2 FY26; CASA deposits grew 4.17% year-on-year to INR 137,386 crores
items.quote: CASA grown in absolute terms to INR 137,386 crores with a year-on-year growth rate of 4.17%. CASA ratio as on September '25, is recorded at 40.52%.

items.statement: Credit-deposit ratio improved to 81.98% in Q2 FY26, up 789 bps year-on-year
items.quote: Globally, credit deposit ratio improved year-on-year by 789 bps and registered at 81.98%.

items.statement: Added 86 lakh new customers in last 2.5 years; 21 lakh added in H1 FY26
items.quote: As far as the new customer acquiring is concerned, almost last 2.5 years, we have added almost 86 lakh new customers, particularly in the current year, in the last 6 months, we have added almost 21 lakh customers.

items.statement: Transition to new tax regime expected in Q3 or Q4 FY26
items.quote: Most probably, we'll be doing it in Q3, sir, most probably, or in the worst scenario, Q4. But this financial year, it is certainly going to happen.

items.statement: IIB Malaysia winding up progressing; final regulatory approval expected this quarter; full INR 200 crores investment expected to be recovered with no loss
items.quote: So all the approvals almost started are in place, the final approval is supposed to be received by the local regulator. And local regulator, and if we expect it to come maybe in this quarter, it should come. The entire amount will come to us sir, around INR 200 crores. KPMG has already been appointed as liquidator and we are not expecting any hit on that. So around INR 200 crores whatever we have

items.statement: No official communication on PSB merger proposals; media reports appear periodically
items.quote: Sir, like you, we are also reading in newspapers. We do not have any communication from any of the authorities so far. And this type of things, I will say that it is not new. Every 6 months, it happens and it keeps coming up in the newspapers. But officially, we do not have any communication.

items.statement: No stress visible from US tariffs on MSME borrowers; borrowers have positioned well and expect resolution in couple of months
items.quote: On account of tariffs, see stress is not visible so far. We have been interacting with our borrowers. And everyone -- in fact, everyone has been able to find a way out to handle this tariff impact, and they are all pretty sure that it will be -- this issue will be over in a couple of months. But till that time, everyone has positioned themselves very well. And we do not see any stress so far in an

items.quote: credit card, Indian Overseas Bank October 16, 2025 we have entered into arrangements with two Fintechs and the terms of those credit card lending through those Fintech, that is highly lucrative. And through that, the source of income will be increased. Another way of increasing income in our focus on government business. The government transactions, which we are very aggressively doing and lots of

items.statement: ESG lending products (IOB Surya, IOB Tejas) launched 5-6 months ago; share in loan book not yet substantial
items.quote: The share of the ESG products in total loan book is not substantial. We have started recently only 5, 6 months ago. And it is taking off. It is catching the attention of the general public also. So share is not very substantial. But going forward, maybe in a couple of quarters, we'll be able to give you the good numbers.

items.statement: Income tax refund of INR 1,141 crores received; credited to tax paid account, not P&L
items.quote: So this income tax refund of INR 1,141 crores has come to us. It has not gone to P&L, sir, it does not go P&L and profitability they were impacted because of that. This goes to one GL Head, that is tax paid account. And whatever demands are coming that also goes there only. It has got nothing to do with P&L and clearly, our P&L is not impacted by that.

items.statement: Targeting 15%+ volume growth and 20%+ CAGR in revenue and profitability by 2030
items.value: 15%+ volume growth, 20%+ CAGR revenue and profitability
items.quote: We are rapidly enhancing our lead and copper capacity, while building a presence across adjacent Nonferrous segments with ambitions of delivering 15% plus volume growth and 20% plus CAGR in revenue and profitability.

items.statement: Maintain EBITDA margins above 8% and ROCE exceeding 20%
items.quote: This growth will be complemented by sustained margin expansion, driven by our focus on maintaining EBITDA margins above 8% and return on capital employed exceeding 20%.

items.statement: Targeting over 60% revenue from value-added products and 20%+ reduction in energy consumption
items.quote: We aim to derive over 60% of our revenue from value -added products and are targeting a (+20%) reduction in energy consumption, underscoring our commitment to operational efficiency and environmental stewardship.

items.statement: Confident of maintaining EBITDA margins at 8%+ for current financial year
items.quote: We are pretty much confident that we will be able to maintain the current margins Pondy Oxides and of 8% and higher, and that's how we are looking at it

items.statement: Expect gross margins in 12-14% range
items.quote: In similar levels, we are expecting our gross margins to be in the range of these 12%, 14% of gross margins is what we are expecting.

items.statement: Targeting 25% top-line growth for next 2-3 years
items.quote: We are looking at about 25% on the top line numbers.

items.statement: Minimum 20% year-on-year growth target going forward
items.quote: As a basic internal target that we have is a minimum of 20% is what we want to grow year-on-year going forward.

items.statement: Invested INR 14 crores in H1 FY26, expect additional INR 35 crores in H2 FY26
items.value: INR 14 crores H1, INR 35 crores H2
items.quote: During H1 FY '26, POCL invested around INR 14 crores in capital expenditure and expects to deploy an additional INR 35 crores in the second half of the fiscal.

items.statement: Lead Phase-2 CAPEX ~INR 20 crores in H2 FY26; Copper CAPEX ~INR 35 crores in H2 FY26 and INR 55-60 crores in FY27
items.quote: H2 on the lead side, it's approximately INR 20 crores. And in addition to that, another INR 35 crores approximately on the copper side.

items.statement: Lead Phase-1 (36,000 tpa) at 50-55% utilization in Q2 FY26, ramping to 70% in coming quarters; Phase-2 (36,000 tpa) commissioning H2 FY26
items.quote: Phase-1 began commercial production in Q1 FY '26 and operated at 50% utilization during Q2 FY '26, expected to ramp up to 70% in the coming quarters. Phase-2 is slated for commissioning in the second half of FY '26.

items.statement: Combined lead capacity utilization ~60% by FY26 end, targeting 80% in FY27
items.quote: For next year, we are targeting at 80%.

items.statement: Copper capacity expansion: 12,000 tpa value-added products in FY27, total 24,000 tpa by end FY27
items.value: 12,000 tpa FY27 H1, 24,000 tpa FY27 end
items.quote: So, we are targeting 12,000 plus 12,000. So, by end of FY '27, we should be having a capacity of 24,000 tons of this, which will reflect back in FY '28.

items.statement: Lead sales volume target 1.2 lakh tons for FY26; H2 FY26 target ~70,000 tons
items.quote: Volumes for lead, the volume we expect is close to 70,000 tons for the next 2 quarters, put together.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton lead increased 62% YoY to INR 19,970 in Q2, 48% YoY to INR 18,510 in H1
items.quote: EBITDA per tonne of lead increased significantly by 62% year-on-year to INR 19,970 per ton on a quarterly basis and 48% year-on-year to INR 18,510 per ton on half yearly basis.

items.statement: Margin improvement driven by operational efficiencies (1.5% margin increase), value-added products (1.5% margin increase), and fixed cost absorption
items.value: Operational efficiency 1.5%, value-add 1.5%, fixed cost absorption
items.quote: The first thing is that last quarter as well as this quarter, our operational efficiencies have increased by 1.5% of the overall margin increase, 1.5% has come from operational incre ase. And the value addition still remains at 70% plus levels. There also, we have got this 1.5%, which is typically about in INR terms, it is INR 6 per

items.statement: Exports contributed 61% of total revenue in H1 FY26
items.quote: Exports contributed 61% of total revenue, reaffirming POCL's strong global footprint and customer trust.

items.statement: Copper margins to increase with value-added product expansion; targeting INR 900-1,000 crores top line from INR 100-110 crores copper CAPEX
items.value: INR 900-1,000 crores top line from copper
items.quote: From this INR 100 crore CAPEX, give me a moment, please. We expect in the range of INR 900 crores to INR 1,000 crores top line.

items.statement: EPR implementation done but pricing not mature; holding EPR credits until sustainable prices
items.quote: So, the EPR implementation has been done. And right now, even though the trades are happening, they are still not happening at a mature price level and the whole system is still evolving.

items.statement: GST on lead scrap and e-scrap remains at 18%; RCM notified but no reduction
items.quote: GST, the RCM was notified, but for a small er amount, the reduction in GST numbers was not done for lead scrap and e scrap. So, it still remains at the full 18

items.statement: Fully hedged commodity (LME) and forex (banks) exposure; natural hedge from import-export
items.quote: Both in terms of our raw material is hedged with the broker, we have account with a direct London Metal Exchange broker. So, the commodity risk is hedged through LME. The FOREX risk is hedged through the banks.

items.statement: Inventory levels INR 170-200 crores sustainable benchmark; will increase with copper expansion
items.quote: INR 170 crores to INR 200 crores of inventory is something which we can have as a benchmark going forward.

items.statement: Achieved zero net debt with net cash balance of INR 71 crores
items.value: Zero net debt, INR 71 crores net cash
items.quote: POCL's balance sheet has strengthened having achieved zero net debt and holding a net cash balance of INR 71 crores.

items.statement: ACE Green Recycling acquisition for lithium-ion R&D; commercial entry targeted 2027
items.quote: So, basically, this is more of a interest in terms of understanding the technology and R&D happening currently with ACE Green, wherein they are doing their R&D on all kinds of lithium-ion batteries, all chemistries. And as and when their R&D is successful, we will be looking at deploying them on a pilot scale.

items.statement: Lead production up 8% YoY to 50,475 tons H1; lead sales up 9% QoQ to 26,308 tons Q2
items.quote: The production of lead has increased by 8% year-on-year to 50,475 metric tons on a half yearly basis and 9% quarter-on-quarter to 26,308 metric tons.

items.statement: Management reiterates FY26 sales guidance of INR 8,500 crores, aiming to do better
items.quote: we would stick to still our earlier gu idance of about INR8,500 crores of what we are doing. If we can do – I mean, we aim to do much better than that

items.statement: H1 FY26 real estate sales value INR 3,981 crores, up 30% YoY
items.quote: During the first half of this year, we achieved a real estate sales value of INR3,981 crores, which is higher by 30% compared to the last year in the same period.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 real estate sales INR 1,902 crores, 770 homes, Bangalore 70%
items.quote: In Q2 alone, we have achieved sales of INR1,902 crores, consisting of 770 homes with Bangalore contributing 70% of the sales despite any new significant project launch.

items.statement: Plan to launch 8-9 million sq ft across 7-8 projects in H2 FY26
items.quote: we are making our best efforts to catch up in the second half and launch at least 8 million to 9 million square feet for the entire financial year across 7 to 8 projects.

items.statement: Residential pipeline 15.96 million sq ft across 13 projects in 9 cities; commercial pipeline 0.74 million sq ft
items.quote: Overall, we have a strong residential pipeline of 15.96 million square feet across 13 projects in 9 cities and commercial pipeline of about 0.74 million square feet across all our operation cities.

items.statement: H1 FY26 land-related spend INR 632 crores, nearly 2x H1 FY25
items.quote: We spent INR632 crores on land-related activity, almost 2x the amount we allocated in H1 ’25, in line with our commitment to further strengthen future pipeline for growth.

items.statement: Project-level EBITDA margins on sold inventory estimated at 33-34%; overall margins to improve significantly from FY27
items.quote: the EBITDA margins in those projects are between 30% to 35% or – I mean, we estimate it to be closer to 33% to 34%. And those will start getting reflected in the – as we complete those projects.

items.statement: Gross project margins currently over 20%, targeting 30%+ by FY27
items.quote: our project level currently, we are at about over 20% on the gross margins and that we should be able to increase or move towards 30% subsequently, which is probably next year, we should start – I mean, move towards that.

items.statement: Q2 collections INR 2,046 crores, highest ever; H1 collections INR 3,824 crores, up 30.9% YoY
items.quote: For H1, we collected INR3,824 crores, recording a healthy 30.9% growth over H1 ’25.

items.statement: Net operational cash flow H1 FY26 INR 909 crores, up 79.1% YoY
items.quote: We generated INR513 crores of net operational cash flow in the quarter for the half year, and it was INR909 crores, registering a significant growth of 79.1%.

items.statement: Net cash position INR 751 crores at end of Q2; weighted average interest rate down 60 bps
items.quote: Company closed the quarter – closed the quarter with net cash position of INR751 crores, underscoring a very healthy and strong financial footing. Weighted average interest rate has come down during the quarter by 60 basis points.

items.statement: Unrecognized revenue from sold units INR 18,000 crores (Sobha share) as of Sep 30
items.quote: Our total balance revenue to be recognized from already sold unit as on 30th September was close to INR18,000 crores. This is Sobha share only.

items.statement: Future cash inflow from ongoing projects INR 22,867 crores; cost to complete INR 13,000 crores; marginal cash flow potential ~INR 9,800 crores over 4-5 years
items.quote: From all completed and ongoing projects, we expect total INR 22,867 crores of future inflow. The cost to complete this project is estimated INR13,000 crores, thereby generating marginal cash flow potential of close to INR 9,800 crores at project level post sales and marketing spend.

items.statement: Forthcoming projects (16.69 msf) expected to generate INR 7,100 crores marginal cash flow over 5-6 years
items.quote: Additionally, we expect to generate INR 7,100 crores of marginal cash flow from forthcoming projects of 16.69 million square feet, which shall be launched over the next 6 quarters and the cash flow realized over 5 - to 6-year timeframe.

items.statement: Bangalore pricing entering stable phase; expect inflationary increases rather than demand-supply driven spikes
items.quote: we are entering into a phase of steady demand and supply in Bangalore. And probably in some aspects, the supply might increase. And if that does, then from a pricing point of view, we should see a stable or an inflationary increase in the pricing than the kind of price rises we have seen in the last 4 years.

items.statement: Q2 sales driven by INR 2-3 cr ticket size in Townpark; sustained demand for end-user products
items.quote: the majority of the contribution has been from Townpark for 70%, right? And all of them are sustained sales. This shows good on-ground demand for the end user-based products. And particularly within the ticket sizes of INR2 crores to INR 3 crores.

items.statement: Gurgaon sales improving after organizational and channel changes; reasonable end-user demand seen
items.quote: we have made certain changes, and we are seeing reasonable end user demand for our products now, and we have made changes in our organization as well in terms of how – in terms of people and in terms of how we approach the channels that do provide impetus to the sales.

items.statement: BBMP restructuring caused approval delays; now resolved, no major delays expected
items.quote: The main reason for this was the restructuring of the BBMP, which is now Greater Bangalore A uthority. And that restructuring had taken a little bit of time for the actual – coming into effect and which has thankfully has come into effect

items.statement: Provision of INR 27 crores taken for ground rent demand from Bangalore authority for past OCs
items.quote: During the quarter, we have received demand for ground rent from Bangalore authority for OC granted in earlier years. So as an accounting principle, we have made provision of INR27 crores in the quarter itself.

items.statement: Mumbai launch planned for H2 FY26; significant approval progress made
items.quote: The Mumbai launch is indeed in the plans for second half. We have – there also, we have made significant progress in terms of approvals. So, we are hoping to do the first phase of the launch very soon.

items.statement: NCR H2 launches: 3 projects totalling ~3.5 msf (Gurgaon service apartments, Gurgaon residential phase, Greater Noida)
items.quote: There are 3 projects that we envisage to launch in NCR, one small service apartment kind of project in Gurgaon and one phase of a residential project in Gurgaon. And third is there is a project that we plan to launch in Greater Noida. These 3 projects are also part of this. All these 3 put together, it would be about 3.5 – roughly about 3.5 million

items.statement: Target 5.5 million sq ft completions in FY26; H1 completed 2.25 msf (591 homes in Q2)
items.quote: We aim to complete overall at least 5.5 million square feet in this financial year.

items.statement: Active BD in NCR, Mumbai, Bangalore, Hyderabad; pipeline ~40 msf; not disclosing GDV additions
items.quote: you can s ee in our pipeline itself, it ’s close to about 25 million plus 15 million, close to 40 million square feet, which is clearly out there

items.statement: Revenue recognition on completion basis (not percentage-of-completion); explains margin difference vs peers
items.quote: Ours is on completion, whereas some of the other years that we see in geographies like Bombay, it is more to do with percentage completion. So, there is an accounting difference also.

items.statement: India power demand grew 3.3% YoY in Q2 FY26 to 449 BUs; H1 up 0.8% YoY
items.quote: After a decline of 1.6% in Q1, we witnessed a significant uptick in power demand in Quarter 2, which grew by 3.3% year -on-year to 449 billion units and H1 demand was u p by 0.8% year on year.

items.statement: Total installed capacity reached 13.2 GW, up ~71% YoY; added 443 MW in Q2 including Kutehr hydro 240 MW, wind 148 MW, solar 56 MW
items.quote: During the quarter, we successfully added 443 MW of new capacity, taking our total installed capacity to 13.2 GW. This represents a remarkable year-on-year growth of approximately 71%, up from 7.74 GW in the same period last year.

items.statement: Target to close FY26 with generation capacity in excess of 15 GW
items.quote: With 2.3 GW of capacity already added in H1 FY26, we are well-positioned to achieve our generation capacity target in excess of 15 GW by the end of fiscal year.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 revenue up 55% YoY to Rs 5,300 crore; EBITDA up 67% YoY to Rs 3,200 crore; PAT down 17% YoY to Rs 705 crore; cash profit up 27% YoY to Rs 1,500 crore
items.quote: And all of this has led to the net generation for the quarter being up by 52% YoY, which translated to a total revenue which was up by 55% at over Rs. 5,300 crores. And the EBITDA for the quarter went up by 67% to Rs. 3,200 crores.

items.statement: Receivables at Rs 3,500 crore, DSO improved to 64 days from 70 days YoY
items.quote: The receivables trend continued to be very healthy. The total amount of outstanding receivable at the end of September was Rs. 3,500 crores, which translated to a day sales outstanding of 64 days. This was an improvement compared to 70 days at the same time last year.

items.statement: Coal prices averaged $91/tonne in Q2 FY26 vs $110/tonne in Q2 FY25; post-quarter prices softened to ~$81/tonne
items.quote: Coal prices continued to moderate, averaging $91 per tonne during the quarter, down from $110 per tonne in Q2 FY25. Post-quarter end, prices have further softened to around $81 per tonne.

items.statement: Acquired GE Power India's boiler manufacturing business; acquired majority stake in KSK Water Infrastructure; signed definitive agreement to acquire 150 MW Tidong hydro plant from Statkraft at EV of Rs 1,728 crore, expected commissioning by
items.quote: As part of our continued strategic growth, I'm pleased to share that we have signed a definitive agreement to acquire the 150 MW Tidong Hydro Power Plant from Statkraft at an enterprise valuation of ₹1,728 crore. Expected to be commissioned by October 2026.

items.statement: Battery assembly plant in Pune (5 GWh/annum) expected operational in Q3 FY26; green hydrogen project (3,800 TPA) at Vijayanagar near commissioning; signed BESS agreements for 680 MWh, total locked-in storage 29.4 GWh
items.quote: As previously communicated, we are in the process of establishing a battery assembly plant in Pune with a rated capacity of 5 GWh per annum. This facility, dedicated to supporting Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), is ex pected to be operational in Q3 FY26.

items.statement: GST rationalisation lowers capital costs for renewables and removes Rs 400/tonne compensation cess for domestic coal thermal plants; Renewable Consumption Obligation framework and draft Electricity Act amendment are sector positives
items.quote: The recent GST rationalisation has been a welcome reform. For renewables, it lowers capital costs and will translate into more competitive tariffs. For thermal power—plants using domestic coal—the removal of the ₹400/tonne compensation cess and the streamlined GST structure will reduce fuel costs and improve overall generation economics.

items.statement: Grid evacuation challenges for solar during solar hours; curtailment risk temporary (1-3 years) until connectivity improves; assets under GNA have revenue protection, TGNA assets do not
items.quote: So, I think it is if the scheduling system is proper, agile, vigilant, and the timely rescheduling and proper scheduling is happening, this can be minimized or avoided. Till now, at least we have not faced any such challenge in terms of curtailments , but yes, that this is one phenomenon a watch needs to come, but not I will say on a permanent basis, temporarily maybe for the next 1 year, 2 year,

items.statement: National wind PLF rose from 31.7% to 34.9% YoY; hydro generation surged 13% YoY to 68 BUs; merchant day-ahead prices averaged Rs 3.92/unit, down sequentially and annually
items.quote: Wind generation saw one of its strongest performances, with national PLFs rising from 31.7% to 34.9%. Hydro generation also surged, reaching 68 billion units —a 13% year -on-year increase —thanks to better hydrology and a favourable monsoon.

items.statement: Received LOA for 400 MW at 700 MW Utkal plant from Karnataka at Rs 5.78/unit at CTU periphery; plant near MCL mines ensuring attractive fuel cost
items.quote: Recently we have received an LOA of 400 MW for our 700 MW UTKAL plant, which is currently an open capacity – once this LOA is converted to PPA, it will further enhance our cashflow predictability, and take our open capacity from currently at 8% to 5%.

items.statement: Long-term capex guidance of Rs 1,30,000 crore by 2030 to achieve 30 GW capacity and 40 GWh energy storage
items.quote: We had earlier guided for a capital expenditure of ₹1,30,000 crore by 2030 to achieve a capacity of 30 GW and 40 GWh of energy storage.

items.statement: KSK Mahanadi 1,800 MW balance capacity (4th unit 40% complete, 5th/6th units minor work done) targeted for completion before 2031
items.quote: See, yes, we have been maintaining that this is an 1,800 MW operational plant and 1,800 MWs of which the balance of plant is fully ready and maybe the 4th unit 40% of the work is complete and also 5th and 6th units, minor work has already been completed. So, definitely we have plans to complete this before 2031.

items.statement: RE bidding volumes expected lower in FY26 vs last two years due to 40 GW backlog and grid constraints; plain solar/wind bids minimal, shift to hybrid/FDRE/solar+BESS; bidding pace to recover from FY27
items.quote: So, we see that current year we expect the overall bidding volume what we have witnessed in the last two fiscals is expected to be lower in the current year. But as I again said, this is temporary. Again, once the backlog starts coming down and the connectivity visibility is there, I think this will again gain pace maybe from next financial year is what is expected.

items.statement: 2.6 GW renewable LOAs pending PPA signing (only 900 MW pure solar); no improvement in PPA signing delays over last 6 months; thermal PPAs seeing uptake
items.quote: the thing is, as we discussed some time back also, and I replied to one of the questions that there is a pendency of 40 GW of bids which are LOA issued and PPA pending for signing. So, we cannot give any timeline for this whether it is 3 months, 6 months, 1 year

items.statement: GE boiler acquisition brings established technology, engineering team and skilled workforce critical for thermal expansion
items.quote: So, it is the technology is there . The skill set to do the people are there . The engineering team is there so that these are the prime reasons that we have gone for this.

items.statement: Revised FY26 revenue guidance upward to INR 1,150 crores plus from INR 1,050 crores
items.quote: Based on the strong performance and business momentum, the company has revised its annual guidance for FY '26 upwards from INR 1,050 crores to INR 1,150 crores plus reflecting our confidence in the demand outlook and operational scalability.

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA margin at 27.2%, PAT margin at 17.2%
items.quote: EBITDA for the period stood at INR 156.6 crores with margin of 27.2%, while profit after tax was INR 105.5 crores translating into a margin of 17.2%.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin at 27.1%, PAT margin at 17%
items.quote: For Quarter 2 FY '26, revenue stood at INR 323.3 cores while EBITDA came at INR 87.7 crores with a margin of 27.1%. Profit after tax for the quarter was INR 54.9 crores, reflecting a margin of 17%.

items.statement: Confident of sustaining healthy margins going forward
items.quote: So, looking ahead also for the coming quarters, we remain very confident in the structural strength of the business, of the products, and of course, the model and our ability to sustain the healthy margins.

items.statement: Total capital expenditure estimated at approximately INR 450 crores for capacity expansion and new geographies
items.quote: Additionally, for the other project, which we had announced earlier, so the total capital expenditure is estimated at approximately INR 450 crores.

items.statement: Capex to be funded through internal accruals, debt, and equity; structure to be finalized shortly
items.quote: We are actually in a very advanced discussion, and we expect to finalize the structure shortly. We will share the updates on the mode of financing for the project. But we are, of course, looking to evaluate the options for internal accruals, debt, and also fund it through equity.

items.statement: Current fractionation capacity 40,000 metric tons annually; upgrading to 52,000 metric tons annually
items.quote: As part of our operational planning, we have scheduled a plant maintenance and upgradation shutdown in Q3 FY 2025-26 to enhance efficiency and facilitate expansion in our current fractionation capacity from 40,000 metric tons annually to 52,000 metric tons annually approximately.

items.statement: Plant utilization at 80-85% for H1 FY26 on 40,000 tons capacity
items.quote: And the plant utilization level for H1, it is around 80%-85% combined.

items.statement: Additional 12,000 metric tons capacity expected to be live from Q4 FY26
items.quote: So, we will be taking this in December Q3 and maybe from Q4 we can see it.

items.statement: Revenue potential at 100% utilization of 52,000 tons capacity estimated at INR 1,800-2,000 crores
items.quote: On 52,000 tons, 100% capacity utilization, we see a revenue potential of around INR 1,800-INR 2,000 crores. Of course, provided everything goes well.

items.statement: Contracts typically 9-12 months with fixed volume and pricing; no price drift seen for CBE products
items.quote: Sir, to answer your question, if you see our contracts are usually for 9-12 months, and we are very firm with our contracts and order books and we do not see any price drift in our cocoa butter equivalent, Stearin or other, any of our specialty, value-added specialty fats and butter products.

items.statement: Value-added products contribute 70-75% of sales including CBE, stearin and other specialty fats
items.quote: So, our value-added product contribution to our sales is around 70%-75%, which includes cocoa butter equivalent, stearin and some value-added products.

items.statement: Top customers include Mondelez, Nestle, Hershey's; top 10 customers contribute ~40% of revenue
items.quote: So, we can share the figures for top 10 customers, which is around 40%. And top three customers are Mondelez, Nestle and Hershey's.

items.statement: Export contribution 58%, domestic 42% of topline
items.quote: 58% was the export contribution and 42% is the domestic.

items.statement: US export sales only 2-3% of total; no material impact from potential tariffs
items.quote: So, our export sales to US are around 2%-3%. It has no real impact on our topline and bottomline.

items.statement: Working capital days reduced from 151 to 97 days; targeting 75 days in next 2 years
items.quote: So, from 151 days, we have come to 97 days now and we target to 75 kind of days for our working capital cycle given the model of the business.

items.statement: Net operating cash flow of INR 189.07 crores in H1 FY26
items.quote: Additionally, net operating cash flow of INR 189.07 crores during first half FY '25-26, ensuring strong liquidity to fund growth and expansion initiatives.

items.statement: Net debt-to-equity ratio of 0.57:1 as of September 2025
items.quote: As of 30th September 25, ROCE stood at 49.9% and 36.9% respectively, with a comfortable net debt-to-equity ratio of 0.57:1.

items.statement: Volume growth expected at 25-30% YoY for FY26 driven by capacity utilization improvement from 63% to 85%
items.quote: If you see the capacity utilization was around 63% last year. So, we expect 85% this year. So, it is the growth of volume. It is around 25%-30%, approx.

items.statement: CBE realization at $5,500-6,000 per ton; contracts fixed for 9-12 months
items.quote: The realization, we already have shared for cocoa butter equivalent, which is $5,500-$6,000.

items.statement: CBE prices stable at $5,500-6,000/ton despite cocoa price volatility; no contract repricing expected
items.quote: Yes, that is in the range of that. So, when cocoa butter was trading at higher, $25,000-$30,000 kind of a dollar, our price was still the same. Now, maybe it is fluctuating as you are saying it is down through your channel checks, but still our prices are around that price only $5,500-$6,000 US dollars.

items.statement: Established subsidiaries in West Africa for Shea nut procurement; signed MoU with Burkina Faso government for processing facility
items.quote: Firstly, we have established subsidiaries in West Africa to streamline and strengthen the procurement of our raw materials like Shea Nuts, which are a key raw material for our operation. In addition, we also have signed a MoU, the Memorandum of Understanding, with the government of Burkina Faso for setting up a processing facility in the country.

items.statement: Entered agreement with DEKEL in Brazil to use their processing facilities for specialty fats manufacturing
items.quote: In Latin America, we have entered into an agreement with DEKEL in Brazil to utilize their processing facilities for manufacturing of specialty fats intended for that regional market.

items.statement: Signed MoU with Chhattisgarh government for potential investment in future plant capex project
items.quote: And additionally, also, we have signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Government of Chhattisgarh for potential investment in our future plant's CAPEX project.

items.statement: African backward integration facility planned for ~70,000 tons extraction and expelling capacity
items.quote: It is still an approximate figure, but it should be around 70,000 tons.

items.statement: No visible risks identified but acknowledges business always has risks including management failure
items.quote: Sir, business is business and business always has risk. So, there could be many risks which can come from many sources. So, as such, we don't see any known risk to us, but there could be management failure, there can be multiple types of mistakes.

items.statement: Established 8 subsidiaries globally in West Africa, Latin America, Brazil
items.quote: If you see, we have established 8 subsidiaries globally in the regions like West Africa, Latin America, Brazil.

items.statement: GST on cement reduced from 28% to 18%; company passed full benefit to consumers
items.quote: The reduction in GST on cement from 28% to 18% is a long-awaited fiscal relief and a very welcome step. As a responsible citizen, we had pledged to pass on the entire benefit to the consumers, and we have accordingly undertaken the same.

items.statement: Lower GST rate defers incentive accrual; FY26 incentive accrual expected at Rs 240 cr vs earlier Rs 300 cr guidance
items.quote: With the lower GST rate, th e accrual of incentives will now get deferred. Therefore, we expect total incentive accrual for the year to be around Rs. 240 crores compared to our earlier guidance of Rs. 300 crores

items.statement: Coal compensation cess removal to benefit Rs 20 cr in H2 FY26 and Rs 50-55 cr next full year
items.quote: However, at the same time, government has also removed the coal compensation cess, which will give us benefit of about Rs. 20 crores during H2 this year.

items.statement: Industry demand grew low-single digits in Q1 and Q2 due to heavy rains and GST transition; H2 expected to improve
items.quote: Both Q1 and Q2 demand grew at about low-single digits, driven largely by erratic and heavy rains and flash floods across the country.

items.statement: Long-term industry CAGR of 7-8% expected for the decade; cement growth typically 1.2x GDP growth
items.quote: While I believe that the Indian cement demand should continue to grow at a CAGR of 7% to 8% during this decade

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA per ton Rs 1,013; absolute EBITDA Rs 696 cr, up 60% YoY; EBITDA margin 20.4% vs 14.1% YoY
items.quote: During the quarter, our revenues improved by 11% Y-o-Y to Rs. 3,417 crores, while EBITDA grew by 60% Y-o-Y to Rs. 696 crores, which works out to be Rs. 1,013 per ton for the quarter.

items.statement: Cost reduction target of Rs 150-200 per ton over next two years remains on track
items.quote: Yes. That is on track.

items.statement: H1 FY26 capex Rs 1,189 cr; FY26 capex estimated at Rs 3,000 cr (lower than earlier due to better supplier credit terms)
items.quote: During H1 of FY '26, we have incurred CAPEX of about Rs. 1,189 crores and our CAPEX spend for FY '26 is estimated to be about Rs. 3,000 crores.

items.statement: FY27 capex expected around Rs 4,000 cr
items.quote: That we expect to be about close to Rs. 4,000 crores.

items.statement: Announced projects capex till FY28 estimated at Rs 10,000-10,500 cr; additional 6 mtpa Greenfield ~Rs 3,500-3,800 cr
items.quote: Based on the announcements which we have made currently, FY '28, you can expect the CAPEX to be about Rs. 10,000 crores to Rs. 10,500 crores.

items.statement: Belgaum and Kadapa expansions (12 mtpa) progressing as planned for West/South markets in next couple of years
items.quote: both Belgaum and Kadapa expansion projects are progressing as per plan, which will give us 12 million tons per annum of cement capacity for West and South markets in the next couple of years.

items.statement: Umrangso, Assam 3.6 mtpa clinker line trial run started Sept; commercial production expected Q3 FY26
items.quote: we have commenced the trial run production of the new 3.6 million ton per annum clinker line in Umrangso, Assam in Septembe r and are expecting commercial production to begin in Q3 of FY '26

items.statement: Jaisalmer Greenfield expansion decision by March 2026; land acquisition and EC work ongoing
items.quote: And, we have time up until March 2026 before which we can break ground and come back to you.

items.statement: Next Northeast split grinding unit (2-2.5 mtpa) to start after ramping up recently added 2.4 mtpa unit; couple of quarters away
items.quote: as we expand capacity and the clinker comes onboard and we ramp up utilization of our previously added unit, we will start work on the next split GU. So, I think we are still a couple of quarters away before we give clarity on that one.

items.statement: Cement prices held up in Q2 despite heavy rainfall; industry passed full GST reduction to consumers
items.quote: On the pricing front, cement prices largely held up during Quarter 2 as well, despite much heavier rainfall, which I believe is a big positive.

items.statement: Pet coke cost currently ~$116/t; blended fuel cost Rs 1.38/kcal; expect marginal increase next quarter
items.quote: The Pet Coke prices currently are around 116. So, naturally, pressure on the external front will be coming into the cost.

items.statement: Raw material cost per ton up 1% YoY to Rs 799 despite Tamil Nadu mineral tax; power & fuel cost per ton up 1% YoY to Rs 1,017
items.quote: Our raw material cost per ton of production marginally increased by 1% Y-o-Y to Rs. 799 per ton despite the impact of mineral tax imposed by the government of Tamil Nadu.

items.statement: RE share 48% on consumption basis; commissioned 93 MW RE this quarter; on track for 576 MW operational RE by end FY26
items.quote: We have commissioned 93 Megawatt of RE capacity this quarter mostly through group captive mode. And we are on track to scale our operational renewable capacity to 576 Megawatt by end of Financial Year '26.

items.statement: Trade share 62% in Q2 (down from previous quarter); premium product share 22% flat YoY
items.quote: Our trade share stood at 62%, while premium product share was at 22% during the quarter.

items.statement: GST cut eases channel working capital; incentive outstanding Rs 800 cr at end Q2; H1 accrual Rs 138 cr, collection Rs 91 cr
items.quote: At the end of Q2 of FY '26, our total incentive outstanding is Rs. 800 crores.

items.statement: Gross debt Rs 6,621 cr; net debt Rs 1,602 cr (up due to IEX share value drop); net debt/EBITDA 0.56x; cost of borrowing 6.9%
items.quote: At the end of the quarter, our gross debt during quarter end stood at Rs. 6,621 crores, and our net debt stood at Rs. 1,602 crores.

items.statement: Net debt/EBITDA to remain comfortably below 2x despite expansion capex
items.quote: Net debt, as we said earlier also, with all thes e expansions also will be comfortably below 2:1. Net debt to EBITDA will not cross two is to one

items.statement: Sold more than half of IEX stake; remaining to be liquidated as needed; SEBI order overhang on IEX
items.quote: We have already sold more than half our position. And the rest of it, we will liquidate as and when we need the money.

items.statement: Board declared interim dividend of Rs 4 per share
items.quote: Lastly, the Board has declared an interim dividend of Rs. 4 per share.

items.statement: Hired Anirudh Tara from BCG as Chief Strategy Officer (15 years building materials experience)
items.quote: We have hired a person who is our Chief Strategy Officer, and his name is Anirudh Tara. He has come from Boston Consulting Group, and he has 15 years of experience in building materials

items.statement: Logistics cost down 3.8% YoY to Rs 1,060/ton; lead distance 287 km; direct dispatch 60%
items.quote: Our logistic costs during the quarter declined by 3.8% Y-o-Y to Rs. 1,060 per ton. Our DD%stood at 60% this quarter, while lead dist ance was at 287

items.statement: Pet coke price volatility driven by geopolitical factors; no other major cost spikes seen
items.quote: I think we see some rise in Pet Coke cost recently, but again, it is very, very driven by geopolitical factors, which is quite volatile and uncertain.

items.statement: Targets Rs 25-50 per ton net realization increase in coming quarters via premiumization and geo-mix
items.quote: I am really targeting Rs. 25 to Rs. 50 per ton increase in net of discounted tax price for the Company going forward.

items.statement: Expects industry cement demand growth of 7-8% in coming months
items.quote: I see a demand uptick of close to about 7%-8% in the coming months and that should really augur well.

items.statement: Targets blended fuel cost of Rs 1.43 per Mcal in Q3 FY26
items.quote: By doing all these things, we are targeting a number again 1.43 in Q3, give or take 0.1 here and there.

items.statement: Targets Rs 50 per ton cost reduction in FY26 vs FY25
items.quote: In terms of the cost savings which I mentioned in the last call, we should target Rs. 50 in FY'26 over '25.

items.statement: FY26 total capex outflow ~Rs 550 crore (routine Rs 100-150 cr, Vadraj rebuild ~Rs 300 cr cash outflow in H2, East expansion ~Rs 50 cr in H2)
items.quote: Overall, I am looking at in H2, CAPEX outflow of close to about 370 plus 50, Rs. 420 crores as the cash outflow. And H1 has been close to 78 plus 45 is 123.

items.statement: FY27 capex ~Rs 750 crore (routine Rs 150 cr + Vadraj Rs 600 cr) plus East expansion Rs 120-150 cr
items.quote: Including 150 routine CAPEX and close to 600 of Vadraj CAPEX will be 750 next year plus capex for East expansion.

items.statement: FY28 capex ~Rs 600 crore Vadraj rebuild + routine Rs 150 cr
items.quote: Looking at close to about 680, 720 and 600, and routine CAPEX of 150, 150, 150.

items.statement: Vadraj Kutch and Surat plants on track for trial runs by H1 FY27, full commissioning by Q3 FY27
items.quote: The plants at Kutch and Surat along with associated equipment, including the jetty, are on track to be ready for trial runs by H1FY'27 with full commissioning targeted by Q3FY'27.

items.statement: East expansion 4 mtpa at <Rs 200 cr via 1 mtpa mill at Arasmeta + debottlenecking; 1 mtpa each in Dec 2025, Mar 2026, Jun 2026, FY27
items.quote: Out of this planned expansion in East, we are targeting capacity addition of 1 million tons each in December 2025, March 2026, June 2026 and FY '27.

items.statement: Vadraj Surat phase-1 2 mtpa grinding unit, target 3 mtpa within a year; Kutch 2.5 mtpa mill
items.quote: Our target is the mill which we commission in Surat as phase -1, we will commission as a 2 million ton but I guess within a span of a year or so, we should take it up to 3 million ton.

items.statement: Next expansion priority: Chittorgarh brownfield over Gulbarga greenfield; evaluation around Q4 FY27
items.quote: Hence, Chittor comes in the scheme of things. We need capacity, we need to spend low cost and hence in the end, priority will be Chittor unless and until the market conditions in North of Karnataka and Maharashtra dramatically changes by higher price, we may look at even Gulbarga at the time.

items.statement: Q2 volume growth ~2% YoY; industry growth estimated 2-4% in Q2
items.quote: But I think from our perspective, we had handsome growth in north. East was a little bit subdued. But overall, I am looking at growth between 2% to 4% kind of a number.

items.statement: H2 FY26 volume growth target 7-8% YoY; aims to match industry growth, outgrow 1.2-1.5x in key markets (Chhattisgarh, Haryana, Rajasthan, Gujarat)
items.quote: I am looking at a close to about, industry, our view is close to 7% growth and Y oY H2 versus this year, I am really looking at 7%-8% growth.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA Rs 371 cr, up 62% YoY; revenue per ton up 1% QoQ
items.quote: Despite facing this headwind, we sustained our Y OY improved performance by achieving a higher second quarter EBITDA of Rs. 371 crores, reflecting a year-on-year increase of 62%.

items.statement: Passed full GST cut benefit (28% to 18%) to customers; no price hikes in short term unless major raw material cost event
items.quote: As mentioned by Bishnu, as our commitment to nation building and as per the expectations of the union government for the basic decision to reduce GST, we passed on the entire benefits to the customers as a part of our corporate governance philosophy.

items.statement: Spot prices flat QoQ excluding GST impact; prices holding in core markets post-GST
items.quote: It has not dropped since GST other than what we have passed. As of now, there has not been price drop in the market ever since GST has happened other than the, what do you call, GST pass-on.

items.statement: Blended fuel cost rose to Rs 1.46/Mcal in Q2 from 1.43; targets 1.43 in Q3 via AFR increase to 12% and kiln efficiency
items.quote: Our 1Q and 2Q number changed from 1.43 per million cal to 1.46 per million cal, but I think we are kind of really doggedly attacking this number because Petcoke may not help us in the short run.

items.statement: Premiumization at all-time high 44% in Q2; trade mix 74%; targets 25% premium volume growth in Q3 vs Q2, 10% in Q4 vs Q3; aims 150-200 bps premium mix increase
items.quote: Premiumization reached a high of 44% in Q2 FY '26, while trade mix remained at a favorable level of 74%.

items.statement: CK ratio in East ~2.1, scope to increase to 2.3 by shifting from PPC to composite cement
items.quote: We operate at close to about 2.1 CK ratio, I won't name the company but there's another company which operates higher CK ratio than us in East, so there is an opportunity for us to increase the CK ratio from 2.1 to 2.3.

items.statement: Committed to never reduce dealer discounts; dealers are principal stakeholders
items.quote: Never ever we will reduce our discounts to our dealers. That is our commitment because they are an important part of our growth and we are obligated, we are very proud for our dealers and we will never ever reduce the discount scheme just to make some short-term gains.

items.statement: Net debt up only Rs 18 cr QoQ despite seasonality due to working capital management
items.quote: Moreover, thanks to significant efforts in managing working capital, the Company has contained working capital requirements, resulting in net debt increasing by only Rs. 18 crore quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Like-to-like net debt down Rs 1,009 cr YoY to Rs 3,492 cr; Vadraj bridge loan Rs 1,200 cr to be replaced by CCDs (two Rs 600 cr tranches, 3-6 yr maturity, call/put options)
items.quote: During the quarter, the Company lowered like-to-like net debt by Rs. 1,009 crore year-on-year to Rs. 3,492 crore.

items.statement: CCD issuance to reduce interest expense from Q3; Nuvoco share count unchanged as CCDs issued at Vadraj level
items.quote: So, in the P&L, you will see some impact of it in Q3. So, you will see the impact of this positive impact in Q3.

items.statement: GST rate cut from 28% to 18% structurally positive; passed full benefit to customers
items.quote: However, having said that, the reduction of GST rate on cement from 28% to 18% is a structurally positive move for the sector.

items.statement: Railway siding clearance received for Kutch; Odisha and Sonadih sidings completed enabling efficient service to East UP, East MP, West Bengal, Odisha
items.quote: We have also received initial project clearance for railway siding at Kutch from Indian Railways.

items.statement: Lead distance 331 km; road-rail mix 60:40 in Q2
items.quote: Quarter lead distance at 331, road at 60%, rail at 40%.

items.statement: Monsoon arrived early and extended late; festive season concentrated in Q2 causing demand disruption
items.quote: The monsoon arrived earlier than usual and extended well into the latter part of the quarter.

items.statement: Carbon emissions 454 kg/ton cement in FY25; customer portal handles >95% orders; AI used for predictive maintenance, heat loss prediction, fuel blending
items.quote: Carbon emissions at 454 kg per ton of cement as of FY'25 demonstrates the Company's ongoing efforts to promote environmental responsibility while maintaining industry excellence.

items.statement: No specific revenue or earnings guidance provided; expect Q3 moderation then sharp Q4 recovery
items.quote: We do not provide specific revenue or earnings guidance.

items.statement: Sequential growth returned across all three verticals; aerospace and industrial heavy machinery up 14% in USD
items.quote: We continue to see strong performance in aerospace, which alongside the industrial heavy machinery vertical, delivered 14% revenue growth in US dollar terms.

items.statement: Automotive vertical stabilized with 0.5% sequential growth in USD terms
items.quote: The automotive vertical also regained positive momentum, recording a 0.5% sequential increase in US dollar terms, a clear sign of stabilization and improving demand.

items.statement: Closed three large deals: Tier 1 automotive supplier data harmonization, Scandinavian OEM heads-up display, first direct German OEM body engineering
items.quote: We also closed three large deals during the quarter: One, with a Tier 1 automotive supplier where Tata Technologies has been engaged to harmonize its product data and information technology landscape across a series of recent acquisitions.

items.statement: Reported EBITDA margin 15.7%; normalized margin 16.4% after adjusting for ~Rs 10 cr cyber incident expense, up 30 bps QoQ
items.quote: Adjusting for this exceptional item, our normalized EBITDA margin came in at 16.4%, reflecting a 30-basis points improvement quarter-over-quarter.

items.statement: Expect Q3 margin pressure from salary revisions and temporary customer operation headwinds
items.quote: Looking ahead in Q3, we anticipate some margin pressure due to the upcoming salary revision and some temporary headwinds in our customer operations as they continue efforts to restore their systems.

items.statement: Opened new office in Munich to expand European footprint
items.quote: We expanded our European footprint with a new office in Munich, strengthening our engagement with OEMs in the region.

items.statement: BMW JV scaled to over 1,000 employees ahead of December target
items.quote: We scaled our BMW joint venture to over 1,000 employees.

items.statement: Signed definitive agreement to acquire ES-TEC (300+ engineers) for Volkswagen access, Germany leadership, ADAS/embedded software capabilities; expect Q3 close
items.quote: A major strategic milestone this quarter was the signing of a definitive agreement to acquire ES-TEC, a move that significantly advances our European presence and automotive engineering capabilities.

items.statement: Headcount stable at 12,402; trailing 12-month attrition rose to 15.1% from 13.8%, driven by engineering talent moving to GCCs and OEMs
items.quote: Our trailing 12-month attrition rate rose modestly to 15.1% compared to 13.8% in the previous quarter, reflecting natural market movements and industry normalization.

items.statement: Trained 7,200+ employees in quarter, including 1,200+ in generative and agentic AI
items.quote: We also invested in employee development, training over 7,200 employees in this qu arter, including 1,200-plus in generative and agentic

items.statement: DSO increased to 109 days from 87 days QoQ due to broader conditions and customer-specific temporary situations; expect gradual reversion to historical range
items.quote: In terms of collection efficiency, we saw an uptick in DSO, which stood at 109-days as of September end from 87 days in June.

items.statement: Remain debt-free; net cash position $123 million at September end vs $159 million at June end
items.quote: Our net cash position as a result stood at $123 million at the end of September compared with $159 million at the end of June. We continue to, however, operate as a debt-free balance sheet company.

items.statement: Services revenue grew 5.1% QoQ to Rs 1,013 cr (3% constant currency); Technology Solutions grew 10.6% QoQ
items.quote: Our services business that contributes 77% of our total revenue, grew 5.1% sequentially to Rs. 1,013 crores, and by 3% in constant currency.

items.statement: Total revenue Rs 1,323 cr, up 6.4% QoQ (4.5% constant currency)
items.quote: I am pleased to report that we delivered a sequential revenue growth of 6.4%, reaching Rs. 1,323 crores this quarter.

items.statement: JLR IT system restoration may cause near-term impact in Q3; visibility only in next 2-3 weeks; cannot quantify impact
items.quote: As you may have read in the press, JLR's IT systems are in the process of being carefully restored, and we are at the moment grappling with the implications of that.

items.statement: Expect Q3 moderation due to seasonal factors, festivals, holidays, and JLR situation; anticipate sharp recovery in Q4
items.quote: While Q2 performance was solid, we anticipate some moderation in Q3, followed by a sharp recovery in the fourth quarter.

items.statement: Aerospace growing across aero structures, interiors, propulsion, MRO, and digital manufacturing throughput; double-digit growth across domains
items.quote: We are developing capability in aero structures and interiors. We are developing capability in propulsion systems. We are developing capability in MRO systems.

items.statement: First direct deal with German OEM for body engineering across all future vehicle programs
items.quote: And the third is our first direct deal with a German OEM, focused on traditional body engineering services that will contribute to all future vehicle programs.

items.statement: ES-TEC acquisition provides direct access to Volkswagen, world's leading automotive R&D spender
items.quote: ES-TEC's longstanding relationship with Volkswagen, the world's leading automotive R&D spender, together with Tata Technologies' industry-leading automotive services portfolio, opens the door to deeper collaboration.

items.statement: ASPICE Capability Level 3 Certification achieved, reinforcing credibility with global automakers
items.quote: We achieved ASPICE Capability Level 3 Certification, reinforcing our credibility and readiness to collaborate with leading global automakers.

items.statement: Launched WATTSync digital battery passport platform using blockchain and AI to help manufacturers meet global sustainability regulations
items.quote: We launched WATTSync, our digital battery passport platform, which combines block chain-based traceability and AI-driven insights to help manufacturers meet global sustainability regulations.

items.statement: Constant currency revenue growth 4.5% vs reported 6.4%; unrealized forex gains declined to Rs 18.5 cr from Rs 25.3 cr QoQ
items.quote: On a constant currency basis, our total revenues were up 4.5%.

items.statement: Strategic partnership with Synopsys for virtual validation in software-defined vehicles
items.quote: We announced a strategic partnership with Synopsys to enable virtual validation in software-defined vehicles, accelerating OEMs ability to integrate and validate software more efficiently.

items.statement: Partnered with Government of Maharashtra for Center for Invention, Innovation, Incubation and Training
items.quote: We partnered with the Government of Maharashtra to establish a Center for Invention, Innovation, Incubation and Training, deepening our commitment to developing future-ready engineering talent.

items.statement: Targets mid-to-high-teens EBITDA growth for FY26, on track to achieve
items.quote: We remain on track to achieve the mid-to-high-teen EBITDA growth in FY'26 in line with our earlier guidance.

items.statement: Targets approximately Rs 2,000 crores EBITDA by FY30
items.quote: With a strong pipeline of over 1,500 keys, we are well-positioned to capture this opportunity as we target approximately Rs. 2,000 crores in EBITDA by FY'30.

items.statement: Board approved 25% stake acquisition in Dubai Palm Jumeirah resort for ~$49 million (INR 437 crores)
items.quote: For a 25% stake, Leela will acquire an upfront capital investment of circa $49 million, circa INR 437 crores.

items.statement: Leela to co-invest 50% in BKC Mumbai hotel with CAPEX of ~INR 800 crores over 4 years
items.quote: Under the new structure, Leela will co-invest 50% in only the hotel with our share of CAPEX circa INR 800 crores, including land and construction.

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA margin 45%, up 5.6pp; 77% incremental revenue flow-through to EBITDA
items.quote: While EBITDA grew by 34% to INR 289 crores, our EBITDA margin expanded by 5.6% to 45%, reflecting strong operating leverage and effective cost management.

items.statement: Q2 RevPAR grew 13% to INR 13,262; H1 RevPAR up 16% to INR 12,616, 3x luxury industry growth
items.quote: In Q2 FY'26, our RevPAR grew by 13% to INR 13,262, driven by balanced improvement across both ADR and occupancy.

items.statement: Retail segment 58% of room revenue in Q2, grew 23% driven by direct sales and brand.com
items.quote: Further, in the same quarter, we delivered 23% growth in retail segment on the back of our dynamic pricing and focus on direct sales channel with a high growth coming from brand.com.

items.statement: ADR grew 10% in H1; occupancy improved 3.8pp to 66%
items.quote: For H1, RevPAR is up by 16% to INR 12,616, supported by ADR growth of 10% and occupancy improvement of 3.8 percentage points to 66%.

items.statement: Net debt/EBITDA 0.5x, net debt/equity 0.2x; >INR 10bn cash; AA Stable rating
items.quote: net debt to EBITDA stands at 0.5x. Our net debt to equity at 0.2x, reflecting a robust balance sheet and capital structure. With more than IN R 10 billion of cash sitting in the balance sheet and a strong A A Stable credit rating

items.statement: Refinanced debt: avg cost reduced from 9.1% to 8.4%, tenure extended from ~8 to ~15 years
items.quote: We have also strengthened financial flexibility through refinancing, lowering our average cost of debt from 9.1% to 8.4% and extending the loan tenure from about 8 years to nearly 15 years.

items.statement: Acquiring 25% stake in operating beachfront luxury resort on Palm Jumeirah, Dubai (546 keys, 23 acres)
items.quote: Firstly, we are excited to announce that we have received Board approval to acquire a 25% stake in an operating beachfront luxury resort on The Palm Jumeirah, Dubai.

items.statement: NPS 86 in H1 FY26, highest in sector; retention ratio improved to 79%
items.quote: Our Net Promoter Score remains the highest in the sector, improving year after year with a strong score of 86 in H1 FY'26.

items.statement: HMA fees grew 14% YoY in H1; F&B revenue up 11% YoY
items.quote: Our HMA fees a capital light and high-margin revenue stream grew by 14% Y-o-Y, reflecting healthy managed portfolio traction.

items.statement: ARQ members club launched in Bengaluru, rolling out to Delhi, Chennai, Mumbai in H2
items.quote: This invite-only club is witnessing a strong traction and will be rolled out across other key cities such as New Delhi and Chennai in the second half of this year and Mumbai to follow thereafter.

items.statement: Relaunched 34,000 sq ft luxury retail wing at Bengaluru adding ~INR 10 cr annualized EBITDA
items.quote: This retail wing will house India's leading luxury brands like Sabyasachi, Zoya, in line with the taste of Leela's discerning clientele. The luxury retail wing will also add annualized EBITDA of approximately INR 10 crores.

items.statement: Commissioned 2.25 MW solar plant at Chennai; 65% energy from renewables; Net Zero target 2050
items.quote: During Q2 FY'26, we have successfully commissioned 2.25 Megawatts solar plant at The Leela Palace, Chennai. Leela now uses 65% energy from renewable sources.

items.statement: Dubai renovation phased over multiple wings; rebranding to Leela in 2027; residences sale post-renovation

items.quote: With GST reforms, we anticipate volumes to go up, the early signs of which are already visible as we have witnessed increased traction from our customers both in terms of leads and conversion of leads.

The other bit in terms of people is very clearly, rather than focus on headcount, it is reallocation of our employees an

items.statement: Focus on absolute VNB delivery; aim to offset GST margin impact via higher volumes from GST reforms and cost levers; commission renegotiations ongoing with all distribution partners.

items.statement: 61st month persistency drop due to definition change allowing policies to remain on book even if not premium paying; 13th month persistency normalised after high non-linked savings base in March 2023.

That's a technical definition that has caused the drop in persistency there.

items.statement: GST impact on EV to be treated as assumption change in year-end EV waterfall, not variance; group and retail business lines cannot be practically offset against each other due to different distribution, products.
items.quote: On the first one, that will be an assumption change. It will not be a variance, it will be an assumption change, which we will disclose at the end of the year. And essentially, whatever expenses are directly attributed to retail business, you cannot really set that up directly against group business.

items.statement: Expect decent growth in H2 FY2026 on benign base, stronger business underpinnings, and GST reform-driven demand pickup; early signs visible in website traffic and conversion improvement.
items.quote: Very clearly, as you rightly pointed out, H2 is more benign than H1 for us. So, given that we have put in a lot of underlying, the underpinnings of the business are far stronger, much more robust, I believe w e should be able to deliver some decent growth into the coming half year. Additionally, given that the GST notifications have also come about, reforms I believe are expected to spur growth.

items.statement: Management expects H2 to be more benign than H1 and sees early signs of demand pickup from GST reforms, including higher website traffic and improved conversion.
