items.statement: VNB margin of 24.5% for H1 includes the known GST input tax credit impact; H2 margin impact depends on ability to adjust via distribution negotiations and demand growth.
items.quote: Yes, we have taken in what we know of GST into the 24.5%.

items.statement: Management aims to offset GST margin impact through higher absolute VNB driven by demand growth rather than cutting customer benefits.
items.quote: Our focus will be on growing the absolute VNB, taking advantage of the environment that offers to us.

items.statement: GST input tax credit disallowance impacts non-par and protection most, then unit-linked slightly, and par minimally; commission renegotiations with distributors are underway across products.
items.quote: The impact of GST input tax credit disallowance is felt most on non -par. And if I am looking at the savings line of business, and I look at the severity on the margin impact, it will be highest on the non -par. It will then come through to unit linked, which will be of small impact. And then par, of course, is a very, very small impact because it cycles through the fund.

items.statement: No commission renegotiations have been finalized yet; discussions with distributors are ongoing and no impact has been passed on so far.
items.quote: No, nothing has been passed on to distributors yet. As Amit also mentioned, this is a set of renegotiations that are on at this point. Nothing has come to close.

items.statement: Product mix has shifted from roughly 2:1 par to non-par to broadly 50-50 par to non-par in H1.
items.quote: For the full year, I think it was roughly about 2 :1 on the par to non-par. We are now broadly at 50-50 on the par to non-par.

items.statement: ICICI Bank banca channel stable at ~100 crores per month; overall banca flat in H1 after 30% growth last year, 2-year CAGR ~13.5-14%.
items.quote: The ICICI bank has been stable at the 100 crores per month range. It broadly stays there. That's not so much of a change in the share of ICICI bank as part of our retail mix.

items.statement: Bancassurance flat due to high base last year, unit-linked sensitivity to market, and multi-partner ecosystem challenges; added 2 new small bank partners in H1.
items.quote: Last year, growth was close to 30% and this year is flattish. So, ICICI Bank is half of 30, which is 15%. And remaining 15% is fairly distributed. You took an example of IndusInd Bank, but we have other bank partnerships as well.

items.statement: Retail protection APE grew 20%+ in Q1 but declined in Q2 due to high base (31% growth in Q2 last year) and GST cut anticipation; underlying demand strong with website traffic up.
items.quote: Q2 for us last year was a fairly strong base, and we had grown at 31% in Q2 last year. So, against that base, this minor growth number clearly is something that I think we should be able to go past that into the coming quarters.

items.statement: Early claims ratio improved to ~22%, indicating improving mortality experience.
items.quote: Look at the ratio of early claims that has started to improve quarter after quarter and we are now at about 22% share of claims as early claims.

items.statement: Continued investment in technology and digitalisation; onboarding of distribution partners now under two weeks via ICICI Pru Stack.
items.quote: We have not stopped investing in technology. That continues. I think that will become a game changer as you look at the coming quarters and the years ahead.

items.statement: GST reform (input tax credit disallowance) effective from 22nd September; EV and VNB include known impact on existing book; full EV walk at year-end.
items.quote: Broadly with the impact of this GST on the existing book to the extent that we know has been factored in as part of the declared VNB. The full walk, we will do that at the end of the year.

items.statement: Persistency has pockets below assumptions; management aims to bring them back by year-end, residual variance taken as assumption change.
items.quote: There are certain pockets that are lower than assumptions and that is what our endeavor will be to bring them back up towards the end of the year so, that there does not remain a variance.

items.statement: Credit protect (MFI) segment still declining but rate of decline reducing; hopeful of recovery as MFI industry picks up.
items.quote: We still continue to see declines in the MFI portion. But what I can tell you is that the sort of decline that we have seen in the earlier periods that has started to reduce.

items.statement: Cost rationalisation focuses on resource reallocation and digital productivity gains, not cutting muscle; technology investment continues.
items.quote: What we have been doing is ensuring that there is further alignment of our resources to where we are able to drive value. Now, be that in terms of reallocation of our organisation structure, reallocation of our people into more productive areas.

items.statement: Management reiterates exit operating margin guidance of 40-45% for Q4 FY26 and long-term target of 45-50%
items.quote: On the OPM guidance, yes, we continue to have the same guidance at exit, we want to be at 40% to 45% OPM, and we are well on our way to that path from everything that we can see.

items.statement: Long-term operating margin target of 45-50% as businesses scale
items.quote: Long term, we should be able to achieve 45 - 50% operating margins as we go along and grow the businesses.

items.statement: Pricing simplification expected to add Rs 50-60 crore annually to net profit at current run rate
items.quote: we expect that on a yearly basis, at current run rate, it should have about ₹ 50 to ₹ 60 crores upside on a net basis to us.

items.statement: Burn for incubating asset management and wealth management businesses remains around Rs 100 crore annually
items.quote: the burn remains in that range of about ₹ 100 crores annual for the two new businesses that we are incubating the asset management and the wealth management business.

items.statement: Credit disbursals rose to Rs 4.6 billion in Q2 FY26, up 97% QoQ, taking cumulative disbursals to nearly Rs 14 billion
items.quote: Credit adoption is also accelerating with nearly ₹ 4.6 billion disbursed this quarter, up 97% sequentially, translating into an annual run rate of ₹ 18 billion

items.statement: Ionic Wealth AUM reached Rs 61 billion with 1,250+ clients across 9 cities
items.quote: Since our inception in 2024, we have reached an AUM of INR 61 billion with 1,250 plus clients across 9 cities.

items.statement: AMC AUM stands at Rs 4 billion across nearly 1.4 lakh folios in over 15,700 pin codes
items.quote: Our AUM now stands at ₹ 4 billion, spread across nearly 1.4 lakh folios, reaching investors in over 15,700 pin codes.

items.statement: Client base crossed 34 million with 1.74 million new clients in Q2 FY26, up 12.2% QoQ
items.quote: Our client base crossed 34 million with over 1.7 million new clients this quarter, higher by 12.2% sequentially.

items.statement: Demat market share rose to 16.5%; retail equity turnover market share increased 71 bps to 20.5%
items.quote: Our Demat market share rose to 16.5% and overall retail equity turnover market share increased by 71 bps to 20.5%

items.statement: Reported EBDAT margin at 34.5%, up 1,270 bps QoQ; normalized EBDAT up 6.1% QoQ to Rs 3.2 billion
items.quote: Our reported EBDAT margin at 34.5% is higher by 1,270 basis points over Q1 FY '26. However, on a normalized basis, adjusting for the IPL spends, our EBDAT is higher by 6.1% quarter-on-quarter to ₹ 3.2 billion.

items.statement: Net interest income grew 4.6% QoQ to nearly Rs 2.9 billion despite 12.4% increase in finance cost
items.quote: As a result, net interest income grew by 4.6% quarter-on-quarter to nearly ₹ 2.9 billion.

items.statement: Pricing simplified to 0.1% with max Rs 20 and min Rs 5 for both delivery and intraday cash segments
items.quote: What we have done is that across both delivery as well as intraday, we have made it 0.1% with max of 20 and min of 5.

items.statement: MTF interest rate unchanged at 14.99%; interest income growth lagged MTF book growth due to lower FD yields and temporary client margin decline
items.quote: There hasn't been any change in the interest rate that we charge from the clients on MTF. So it remains same at 14.99%.

items.statement: Direct business share in net broking revenue expanded 84 bps to 77%, underscoring digital platform strength
items.quote: The share of direct business in net broking revenue expanded by 84 basis points to 77%, underscoring the strength and scalability of our digital platform.

items.statement: 46% of gross revenue from F&O broking, 8% from cash, 6% from commodities, 32% from interest income
items.quote: 46% of our gross revenues came from broking commissions in the F&O segment, followed by 8% from the cash segment and 6% from commodity derivatives segment. Interest income from client funding book and fixed deposits with clearing corporations accounted for nearly 32% of our total gross income.

items.statement: Distribution income grew nearly 28% QoQ driven by 2x jump in credit product sales, robust IPO market, and sustained MF growth
items.quote: Our distribution income witnessed a very strong growth of nearly 28% during the quarter, driven by nearly two-fold jump in sale of credit products, robust IPO market and sustained growth in mutual funds through our assisted channel.

items.statement: AP channel contributes 24-25% of client acquisitions; no feet-on-street model
items.quote: the AP -- the clients acquired through the AP channel contribute about 24 - 25% of the total acquisitions that we do in any quarter.

items.statement: 50% of mutual fund customers also invest in equities, demonstrating cross-pollination
items.quote: nearly half of this cohort also invests in equities, showcasing the cross-pollination power of our platform.

items.statement: GIFT City branch setup planned subject to regulatory and statutory approvals
items.quote: We are excited to announce that we will set up a branch in GIFT City, a strategic move that opens up new growth avenues. This will be subject to regulatory and statutory approvals.

items.statement: Management declines sensitivity analysis on potential SEBI expiry contract tenure changes due to speculation
items.quote: there's a lot of speculation in this area. So it's best for us to not add to that and talk about it because we don't know what is going to happen or if there is anything that is going to happen.

items.statement: No plans to raise equity capital; debt capacity sufficient to fund MTF book growth to Rs 10,000-12,000 crore
items.quote: we can easily double this book from where we are today without having to raise any additional capital. And as you would have seen, the gearing ratio for us is pretty low debt equity ratio. So we don't have any challenge there.

items.statement: AI chatbot 'Ask Angel' resolves 80%+ queries without escalation with 67% reduction in resolution time for 95% of cases
items.quote: The chatbot's architecture leverages our proprietary Agentic AI framework and the results have been exceptional with over 80% of the users resolving their queries without escalation and 67% reduction in resolution time for 95% of the cases.

items.quote: YoY basis, the revenue decline is primarily on 2 fronts. items.statement: Target double-digit PAT growth annually and quarterly going forward
items.quote: we have given as a target that our PAT annually and quarterly should grow in double digit. That is what we are striving for.

items.statement: H1 FY26 agreements signed of over INR 45,000 crores across renewable energy, transmission, coal mining, industrial infrastructure
items.quote: INR 36,000 crores of agreements were signed within 3 days of the last 4 days of this H1, that is between 26th to 29th of September, touching nearly more than INR 45,000 crores in H1 for the sectors like renewable energy, transmission, coal mining and industrial infrastructure, etc.

items.statement: NIM improved from 1.42% in FY25 to 1.55% by end of H1 FY26 due to diversification into higher-margin assets
items.quote: Our NIM, which was in last FY standing at 1.42%, has now improved to 1.55% by the end of H1. This shows that our planning of going for diversification and for the assets where there are better margins are already reflecting in our NIM.

items.statement: Diversified lending margins at 100-120 bps (2x-3x railway margin of 40 bps); NIM expected to improve further

items.statement: Zero NPA record maintained; lending only to government/CPSE entities with near-zero risk perception
items.quote: Through all of this, IRFC maintains a zero NPA record, rare hallmark and the kind of business that we're picking up in diversification also, we intend to maintain our unblemished record of zero NPA.

items.statement: No MAT liability expected for next 5-7 years due to INR 3,000 crores unabsorbed depreciation and future lease asset depreciation
items.quote: As of now, around INR 3,000 crores of unabsorbed depreciation is still with me for which I can take benefit in future years. And these assets would get capitalized in coming years and against which I'll have a good amount of depreciation in my P

items.statement: Board declared interim dividend of INR 1.05 per share for FY26
items.quote: the Board has declared a record breaking interim dividend of INR 1.05 paisa per share, further enforcing the trust and confidence of our shareholders.

items.statement: Team expanded from ~40 to ~60 (50% growth); added experts from railways on deputation, lateral hires from CPSEs, veterans/consultants
items.quote: our motley team has grown by 50% now from 40 odd, we are nearly 60, and we want to grow by attracting depth of the talents.

items.statement: Diversified client base: NTPC, GAIL/Coal India/Rashtriya Chemicals JV, state Gencos, CONCOR/RVNL/Odisha govt JV; all government/CPSE entities
items.quote: My first 4 assets came from NTPC. Now I don't have to speak about NTPC. They are AAA rated asset and their subsidiaries are also that well rated. So if I'm funding to NTPC, you and I both know that what kind of risk I'm going to have. Second flavor, maybe we funded one joint venture promoted by GAIL, Coal India and Rashtriya Chemicals.

items.statement: Target AUM mix of 75% railway / 25% diversified in next 5 years; current AUM INR 4.6 lakh crores
items.quote: right now, you can add total AUM is INR 4.6 lakh crores. Out of that disbursement has started. So slowly, but surely, the target is that in next 5 years, we should have a mix of 75% - 25%. That is 75% should be from the railways and 25% should come from the diversified thing.

items.statement: RBI single borrower limit 30% of net worth (~INR 16,500 crores), group limit 50% (~INR 27,500 crores); net worth ~INR 55,000 crores
items.quote: RBI has made a mandate for everybody that 30% of my net worth for a single entity So today, my net worth is nearly INR 55,000 crores. So you can put 30% number. So one client or one state, I cannot do more than that. So that is a cap from RBI. And for a group of the company, it is 50%.

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio cooled to near 7x; net worth growing >INR 4,000 crores annually; CRAR and Tier 1 capital comfortable after dividend
items.quote: Our debt equity ratio has also cooled down to near to 7. So overall, we are sitting in a very sweet spot that is the thing that we have no exposure to anybody except railways. So next 5 years of time, we are in a very good position that anybody with a good asset is coming to us, we are there to cater to them.

items.statement: No equity dilution needed; internal profits and net worth growth fund expansion; CRAR and Tier 1 capital strong
items.quote: You are absolutely right. After paying highest ever dividend, interim dividend of INR 1.05 paisa, we are still pretty happy with our CRAR, our Tier 1 capital. So that is the beauty Rishi that we are having with the grace and best wishes of more than 55 lakh shareholders of this company.

items.statement: Business development head from NTPC; added ~20 experts from railways on deputation and sibling CPSEs laterally; consultants/mentors with 35+ years NBFC experience
items.quote: We have already added around 20 odd very good talents from the railways on deputation as well as from the other sibling companies on lateral basis. We have added many consultants also. And going forward also, as the need arises, we'll be looking for the best of the class executives in the ecosystems with us.

items.statement: No internal segment caps; only RBI concentration limits apply; cherry-picking best government/CPSE assets to maintain zero NPA
items.quote: for this company is there is no cap for any segments. So per se, theoretically, I can have 100% of my AUM from the railway ecosystem on diversification. Now Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC) October 16, 2025 where is the limitation? Limitation comes from the RBI guidelines

items.statement: H1 FY26 PAT INR 3,523 crores (double-digit growth YoY); Q2 PAT INR 1,780 crores; EPS INR 5.39; net worth >INR 56,000 crores
items.quote: In Q2 FY 25-26, as you all know, we delivered a PAT of nearly INR 1,780 crores, marking more than 10% growth while H1 profit touched INR 3,523 crores, again, a double-digit leap vis-a-vis last H1, highest ever which is highest ever in the IRFC journey. Our net worth has touched a record, more than INR 56,000 crores with the EPS of INR 5.39.

items.statement: Flooded with requests from almost all states; 70% of India's capex from government sector; railway capex appetite >INR 2.5 lakh crores/year
items.quote: We are flooded with requests from almost all states of the country. And because they now know that through all of you that we are l ending to the railway ecosystem and there's hardly anybody in the government system who are not having any linkage with the

items.statement: Cost of funds 6.5-7%; lending to government entities at ~8-8.2% (100-120 bps margin) vs market rates >9%; competitive advantage in government funding
items.quote: We are very happy, as you mentioned our cost of capital 6.5% to 7%. We are very happy lending them with a margin of 100 bps to120 bps as it's a very good margin when you're finding that the risk is nearly zero for these kinds of assets.

items.statement: Project financing on milestone basis linked to borrower COD plans; monitoring via PERT/CPM charts
items.quote: For Project financing w e are doing based on the milestone and whenever we do credit appraisal, we ask from the prospective borrower what would be your plan for achieving this COD and based on their PERT network and their CPM chart, we will generally determine the milestone and based on that we are monitoring and we are appraising the thing

items.statement: Banks and peers lending at higher rates (>9%) to government entities; IRFC's low-cost funding (6.5-7%) enables competitive 8-8.2% lending
items.quote: Nobody was getting a loan less than 9% in the ecosystem we found. We are very happy, as you mentioned our cost of capital 6.5% to 7%. We are very happy lending them with a margin of 100 bps to120 bps as it's a very good margin when you're finding that the risk is nearly zero for these kinds of assets.

items.statement: Overheads kept minimal despite team expansion; focus on cost discipline
items.quote: While doing everything, we still want to be having our overheads at the minimum.

items.statement: Expect marketing spend to remain elevated in the near term, at least for the next quarter
items.quote: So, till the point that we keep seeing this trend, we will keep investing however much that we can to basically power more growth. So, you should expect this to continue in the next quarter as well.

items.statement: Expect year-on-year NOV growth to remain above 100% for the next one or two years
items.quote: Currently if you look at the growth rate, it's much higher at 137%. So, I do expect the year-on-year growth to remain above 100% for the next one or two years at least.

items.statement: Plan to operate around 2,100 stores by December quarter and 3,000 by March 2027
items.quote: you have mentioned that you plan to operate around 2,100 stores by the December quarter and 3,000 by March 2027.

items.statement: Expect District business growth around 30% year-on-year with profitability percentage improving but absolute losses range-bound at current levels
items.quote: we should expect growth to be around the current level of ~30% year-on-year. That is what we are expecting right now and profitability in percentage terms should improve. But as we mentioned also in question 11, we expect the absolute losses to sort of remain range bound around the current levels.

items.statement: Expect District business losses to improve in FY27 versus FY26, inflection in next few quarters
items.quote: FY27 should be better than FY26, in terms of losses in the business. That's how I would put it without really pinpointing a particular quarter, but it should happen in the next few quarters.

items.statement: Long-term food delivery growth guidance remains 20%+ but unlikely to achieve in FY26, expecting ~15% YoY growth this year
items.quote: in the last letter we did say that for this financial year, we're unlikely to be at 20%, and we're expecting a 15% sort of year-on-year growth. But longer-term, our view on 20% remains as of now.

items.statement: Full 1% margin accretion from 1P transition will take four to six quarters to fully realize
items.quote: What we mean by four to six quarters is the timeframe to fully realize it. What we meant last time and maybe we can clarify if there was any confusion is that the realization of the margin gains will start happening immediately, which has happened even in this quarter. items.statement: New consumer cohorts acquired at reasonable marketing cost, driving higher MTU additions

items.statement: Acetyl chloride de-bottlenecking completed to increase efficiency
items.quote: We are also undertaking a de-bottlenecking initiative, which is also complete, for acetyl chloride. This is one of the product lines that were completely sold out. So, we undertook a de-bottlenecking operation, which is complete now and that will increase the efficiency of our business.

items.statement: Nanovace pilot plant on track; process patent granted in US, pending in Japan, Korea, Europe
items.quote: On the battery chemical side, Nanovace's pilot plant project is on track. Process patent for the nano-silicon for battery applications already granted in US and likely to be received in Japan, South Korea and Europe over the next two quarters.

items.statement: Nanovace pilot plant commissioning by FY26; customer approvals expected in 6-9 months after
items.quote: Sir, we are waiting for the pilot plant of ours to get commissioned and once the pilot plant is commissioned, we will be sending the approval grade material to a lot of customers and then we hope that in the next 6 to 9 months post sending of the approval grade material, we will be able to get product approval.

items.statement: Aquapharm expanding distributor partnerships in Africa (Solevo) and Latin America
items.quote: We are also entered in to have new distributor partnerships in Africa with Solevo and a couple of other distributors which we are currently appointing in the Latin American market.

items.statement: Senior industry expert onboarded as Head of R&D and Innovation Center at Aquapharm
items.quote: We also recently onboarded a very senior level industry expert as H ead of our R&D and innovation center, a very experienced guy from the industry and we are now going to steer our innovation efforts also for the

items.statement: US tariffs on Chinese phosphonates and green chelates create opportunity for Aquapharm
items.quote: Geopolitical tensions continue to remain elevated, as we understand, and the recent 100% tariffs imposed by U.S. and China actually created some good opportunities for Aqua pharm's phosphonate and Green Chelates business, because the U.S. customers are now also looking forward to diversifying sourcing beyond China

items.statement: US tariffs on Indian biocides and select polymers create temporary headwinds for Aquapharm
items.quote: At the same time, the recent application of tariffs by the U.S. on India, especially on the biocides and select polymers exported from India, has impacted a portion of our business, which leads to some temporary headwinds in the near term.

items.statement: Board confident to maintain strong dividend payout policy given healthy cash generation
items.quote: The fact remains that we are running at over 99% capacity utilization on the carbon black business. And in a matter of, going forward, you would see significant improvement in the performance. So, cash generation is likely to remain healthy and that probably gives the confidence to the board to maintain a strong dividend payout policy.

items.statement: Committed to double-digit revenue and EBITDA growth for FY26 and FY27
items.quote: At the start of the year, we have shared our projections , that we will deliver double -digit revenue and EBITDA margins. We remain committed to achieving that.

items.statement: Targets 15% EBITDA margin and 15% revenue growth by FY27
items.quote: I think that's a realistic expectation. As we have committed at the start of the year, Tanmay, we want to deliver double -digit revenue and EBITDA.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin improved to 14.3% driven by utilization and productivity
items.quote: For us, the entire margin improvement as we've been sharing over the last several quarters , is consistent and predominantly driven by utilization and productivity.

items.statement: Sees path to 15% EBITDA margin by FY27 through operational efficiencies
items.quote: Yes, we have the opportunity. That's what we are seeing in terms of growth, and we do believe. Our fixed costs will remain the same, because we have already put the team in place.

items.statement: US demand growing at unprecedented speed with AI-driven manufacturing investments
items.quote: Absolutely, in U.S., the demand is growing at a speed I've never seen before. A lot of positive things are happening across the manufacturing industry.

items.statement: Europe slow last quarter but poised for growth on data center, cloud, AI investments
items.quote: In terms of Europe, the last quarter has been slow for us, but I do believe Europe is also on the verge of growth because they also will have to invest heavily in data center, cloud, and AI.

items.statement: Invested INR 18 crores in infrastructure upgrades across delivery centres
items.quote: Our capex investment so far has been approximately INR 18 crores, and we are well positioned to support the offshore growth we anticipate from our clients for the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Headcount stable at 2,525; expects 10-20% increase over next couple of years
items.quote: As I've mentioned in previous earnings calls, we expect our headcount to remain relatively stable over the next couple of years, with a possible 10 –20% increase.

items.statement: DSO at 73 days with target of 65 days
items.quote: DSO continues to remain under control at 73 days with a target to be at around 65 days, which I believe is a good balance for us.

items.statement: LTM attrition declined to 15.49%
items.quote: Attrition continues to decline quarter-on-quarter. Our LTM attrition for Q2 stood at 15.49%.

items.statement: Reduced client base to 70+ clients; targets 50-60 clients at INR 500-1000 crore scale
items.quote: We are down to about 70-plus clients today. And as I've told before, I believe the sweet spot for a company of our size, between INR 500 crores and INR 1,000 crores is about 50 maybe 60 clients.

items.statement: 90-95% revenue from direct OEM clients, <5-10% from Tier 1
items.quote: But if I were to broadly guess, I think, it would be about 90%, 95% would be our direct OEM clients and about less than 5% or less than 10% would be Tier 1 clients.

items.statement: Time & material revenue share increased to 89% from 85%
items.quote: you mentioned yourself that you're keen on more time and material projects and we've gone from 85% to about 89% now time and material.

items.statement: Revenue per employee increased significantly due to shift from India (INR 500/hr) to export markets ($18/hr)
items.quote: the average bill rate for India client is about INR 500 an hour, while the same is at $18 an hour in support of the export market.

items.statement: Two clients confirmed furloughs for Q3; furlough visibility only by mid-December
items.quote: As of today, we only have two clients who have sent an e-mail saying they plan to continue furlough from last year because they have to save costs.

items.statement: Trump tariff situation viewed positively; US companies investing heavily in capex and R&D
items.quote: I have seen during my recent visit to US, it's very progressive. Companies are excited, they are investing and are spending huge amounts of capital on capex and are back into investing in R&D and innovation.

items.statement: Board discussed buyback; CFO mandated to evaluate options
items.quote: It's something the Board has discussed. It was discussed this morning as well. We will evaluate all the options, and our CFO has been mandated to do that.

items.statement: Tax rate expected to stabilize after one-off Canada credit in Q1
items.quote: I think it should be fairly stable going from now , where it is. Last quarter, we shared that as well in the details. We had the one-off tax credit, which is why the tax rate came down.

items.statement: Healthcare vertical targets 1-3 clients crossing $1M revenue by next year
items.quote: By the next yea r, I would like to see at least one to three clients cross $1 million per year. That's the ambition for the team.

items.statement: Not entering high-tech/semiconductor until Transportation & Healthcare verticals ramp up
items.quote: As soon as the 2 of the verticals, transportation & mobility and healthcare starts ramping up, then we will start looking at new verticals.

items.statement: Dollar impact approx 5% negative this quarter
items.quote: In terms of the dollar, I don't think there's been any benefit because I believe the dollar impact has been approx. 5% negative this quarter.

items.statement: Order book described as very good and exciting; no transactional data shared
items.quote: Current order book is very good, very exciting. We do not share transactional data.

items.statement: Differentiated by focus on time & material engagements vs peers' fixed-price preference
items.quote: The difference between us and everybody else is , the larger companies prefer fixed price and we are very focused on time and material engagements.

items.statement: Upgraded Pune and Chennai facilities fully operational; Bangalore and Hyderabad centres new and operating well
items.quote: Our Bangalore and Hyderabad centres are relatively new and operating very well , while o ur Pune and Chennai facilities have been upgraded substantially. Both offices are now fully operational

items.statement: Expects North America EBITDA to reach double-digit or mid-double-digit margins at $28-30 million quarterly run rate
items.quote: as we move forward and as we grow from here, come closer to like a $28mn - $30mn run rate in North America, that's when it will start going up to double digit or mid - double-digit kind of EBIT numbers

items.statement: 12-month order backlog at $280 million, up 2.2% sequentially and 6.8% year-on-year
items.quote: Our 12-month order backlog stood at around $280 million, representing a 2.2% sequential growth and a 6.8% year -on-year growth, supported by heal thy deal conversions and renewals across all geographies, especially U.K.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin improved 50 bps QoQ to 15.5%
items.quote: Our operational EBITDA landed at INR 145.5 crores, 6% quarter- on-quarter improvement and 1.7% year-on-year growth, translating to an operating EBITDA of 15.5%, which is up 50 basis points from the last quarter.

items.statement: DSO reduced to 80 days from 82 days in Q1 and 95 days in Q2 FY25
items.quote: DSO improvements continue to be a key area of focus and we have now brought down the DSO to 80 days versus the 82 days in quarter 1 and versus the 95 days in quarter 2 last year, reflecting a strong cadence on working capital discipline.

items.statement: UK healthcare and secured government services seeing strong demand with long-term contracts and renewals
items.quote: U.K. healthcare continues to see very strong demand. We see that the government is executing on its policy and investment decisions, which is leading to a strong view of the demand as we go forward as well as strong spending.

items.statement: Won GBP 50 million-plus AI-led engineering services deal in UK secured government services and $15 million-plus AI-led modernization deal with large financial services client
items.quote: This quarter marked a GBP 50 million-plus deal, which is an AI -led engineering services deal to deliver modernization as well as efficiency for the secured government services sector

items.statement: AI for tech driving efficiency gains; AI for business transformation engagements with ~12 customers, execution expected early FY27
items.quote: We are seeing some very strong initial trends there and working with almost a dozen of our customers in terms of building their AI for business transformation road map. As we deliver this road map, we look forward to getting into execution in some part of early FY '27.

items.statement: New CFO candidate expected to join early next month; new North America leader Sourabh Mukherjee joined from top 4 IT services company
items.quote: We have a candidate who we are expecting to join early next month, and I'm pretty confident to have a partner with me on this call starting next quarter.

items.statement: ~10 bps margin improvement from FX, rest from operational efficiency
items.quote: As far as the bottom line performance is concerned, around 10 basis points was the impact of FX and the rest of it is operational efficiency.

items.statement: Investing in North America sales & marketing ahead of revenue growth; holding investments for $28-30M quarterly run rate target
items.quote: there is clearly a heightened S&M spend as compared to our current business, which is in anticipation of the growth that we look at. As the business comes closer to its optimal number, which will be $3 million to $4 million growth from where we are today, you will start seeing the EBITDA numbers move significantly up.

items.statement: North America decision-making shifting right; clients signing shorter 6-12 month deals instead of 3-5 year contracts
items.quote: the decision-making, especially with our U.S. customers is shifting right, and we've been seeing that as a phenomena at least for the last 2 -3 quarters. Having said that, it's not that the deals are going away, it's just that the decisions are slower as compared to where they were.

items.statement: Industry trend toward outcome-based/fixed-price contracts from AI efficiency gains; commercial models still fluid
items.quote: AI as far as AI for technology is concerned, which is the AI that is impacting the productivity and efficiency of technology services, it is definitely delivering more and more efficiency every day than what we had seen in our previous months or quarters. And that efficiency is what is leading to customers as well as partners trying to move towards a fixed price or an outcome-based contract so tha

items.statement: AI efficiency gains partly passed to customers, partly reinvested in AI for business capabilities
items.quote: Hundred percent, so if you have to do business right, you will have to pass on some of the savings back to the customers. At least our vision is making some tangible growth for us on our size of business to demonstrate and get a seat on the table for larger transformations.

items.statement: Revenue per resource consistently improving over last few quarters
items.quote: which is demonstratable by our improvement in terms of revenue per resource that we've been continuously demonstrating over the last few quarters.

items.statement: Macro uncertainties causing deferred decision-making and shorter contract durations across geographies
items.quote: the market still has a lot of macro and global uncertainties, which is leading to some deferment of decision making. However, we continue to navigate those uncertainties with a strong and robust bottom line performance

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents increased to INR 656 crores from INR 549 crores in Q1
items.quote: Our cash position, which is cash and cash equivalents currently stand at INR 656 crores as compared to the INR 549 crores in Q1.

items.statement: Oracle partnership strengthening with Oracle Health cloud migration and AI infrastructure opportunities
items.quote: We are one of the very few partners globally who do that kind of work for Oracle. And that's an area of business which we see as a really good chance to improve our healthcare business beyond back office to more Oracle Health and especially cloud and managed services within the Oracle Health segment.

items.statement: APAC/Middle East won $5 million-plus multi-year AI-led healthcare transformation deal with large provider
items.quote: It's an AI -led transformation for one of the largest healthcare provider organizations in the geography. It's a multiyear deal to deliver AI -led business transformation for the account. It's a $5 million -plus already.

items.statement: AMEA one-off: $0.5M revenue delivered but not recognized due to conservative accounting; costs recognized
items.quote: We don't have an exact number with me, Mahak, but closer to the tune of like $0.5 million.

items.statement: Not reducing headcount but using attrition to improve revenue per resource; revenue per resource trending up
items.quote: our strategy is, we are not necessarily going and reducing any head count, but we are also using attrition to our advantage and not backfilling with the exact same numbers, which is leading to constant eff iciency and growth. I believe in the long run, we will see the revenue per resource go up consistently.

items.statement: Expects positive H2 FY26 despite macro uncertainties
items.quote: looking forward to a good positive H2 as we move forward.

items.statement: Winning market share in UK private sector through AI-led efficiency against competitors
items.quote: the private sector continues to also see good demand. And again, many new l ogos adding to that sector. This quarter also marked a new $15 million-plus AI-led modernization, transformation deal with one of the large financial services customers in the vertical.

items.statement: UK government executing policy and investment decisions driving healthcare demand
items.quote: We see that the government is executing on its policy and investment decisions, which is leading to a strong view of the demand as we go forward as well as strong spending.

items.statement: Data & AI horizontal growth slower in North America but accelerating with new leadership and targeted campaigns
items.quote: our growth of our Data service lines within North America specifically is still slower to where we expect it to be. As we speak with a new leader and team in place, we are now driving much more targeted campaigns around Data, especially Data and Data modernization-led areas.

items.statement: AI efficiency gains being reinvested into AI for business solutions, assets, and proof-of-concepts
items.quote: a lot of the savings are being plowed back into AI for business kind of investments today.

items.statement: AMEA DSO significantly reduced alongside profitability focus
items.quote: We have brought down our DSOs significantly, as I mentioned earlier in the call. And we are also looking at only profitable growth in the geography.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target INR750 cr
items.quote: Considering the first half sales, on hand orders of approx imately INR300 crores plus and ongoing discussions with our customers for new orders, we are on track to achieve our target meeting sales of INR750 crores for year FY '25-26

items.statement: FY27 growth 10-20%
items.quote: No, there will be some growth. So generally, what happens is in Q1 and Q2, there is always a slow movement. So for FY '27, we will try to increase that capacity. So we'll be growing by about 10% -- 20% or so for FY '27.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 31% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA margins for Q2 stood impressively at 31%, remaining in line with levels achieved in Q2 FY '25.

items.statement: Margins maintained despite US tariffs
items.quote: So I mean, we don't see any issue. We'll be able to maintain the margins which we have and we've been doing so over the last two years, and all our customers, I mean, they have not placed any orders on hold or they have not cancelled any orders.

items.statement: Order book INR300 cr as of Oct 1
items.quote: So we have an order book of INR300 crores. And we are currently under negotiation with a lot of our customers and we are very confident that we will be able to achieve our target of INR750 crores this financial year.

items.statement: Order book split: domestic INR175 cr, export INR125 cr
items.quote: Domestic is about INR175 crores, export is INR125 crores.

items.statement: Gavasad expansion INR90 cr, 6,500 MVA by April 2027
items.quote: This will be the largest capacity addition in our company's history, adding 6,500 MVA and bringing our total to 14,000 MVA by April 2027. This expansion is funded entirely through internal accruals with a capital outlay of approximately INR90 crores.

items.statement: Capacity utilisation 90-95% in Q2 and FY26
items.quote: So FY '26, we are expecting about 90% to 95% capacity utilization. And for Q2, it was about, again, 90% to 95%.

items.statement: Full capacity revenue potential INR1,400-1,500 cr at 14,000 MVA
items.quote: So with the new expansion, we will be able to -- at full capacity, we'll be able to do a turnover of anywhere between INR1,400 crores to INR1,500 crores.

items.statement: Target 60-70% utilisation in first year of new plant (FY28)
items.quote: So we'll -- I mean as much as we can. And we'll be happy if we can, in the first year, achieve 60%, 70% capacity

items.statement: New facility to make 100 MVA, 220 kV class transformers
items.quote: So we'll be able to manufacture up to 100 MVA , 220 kV class of transformers at this new manufacturing facility.

items.statement: 220 kV transformers to be bundled with inverter duty transformers for solar parks
items.quote: So we are planning to -- I mean, all the -- [Inaudible 0:07:01] in these solar parks, so we are targeting to offer these transformers as a package along with the inverter duty transformers.

items.statement: Domestic solar capacity addition 21.7 GW in H1 FY26 driving order inflows
items.quote: According to Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, India commissioned approximately 21.7 gigawatts of solar capacity in first half of FY '26. This strong sectorial momentum is translating directly into sustained order inflows and robust visibility across the domestic segments positioning us well for further growth.

items.statement: US demand strong post tariffs, customers absorbing full 50% duty
items.quote: The customers are ready to pay for it as of now because our competitors for these markets, they are in different countries, which also have tariffs.

items.statement: Export geographies: Middle East, Africa, Europe, Far East
items.quote: So rest of it is mainly Middle East, some in Africa. And we have started recently exporting to Europe also and we do export some very less quantity to Far East as well.

items.statement: US customers taking full brunt of 50% tariff, no price relief given
items.quote: No, they are only taking the full brunt of the duty.

items.statement: No raw material bottlenecks, multiple domestic vendors
items.quote: No. Most of our raw material is sourced from India only. And most of the items there are multiple vendors. So there is no bottleneck in terms of sourcing any materials.

items.statement: US tariff 50% implemented Aug 27, competitors also face tariffs
items.quote: The new tariff measures implemented from August 27 have introduced some uncertainties. Despite these developments, underlying demand and customer engagements in the United States remain strong.

items.statement: NSE listing timeline before new year
items.quote: So we'll be able to -- I mean, time line we have fixed it before the new year, we'll be listing in NSE. We are already working on it.

items.statement: No overcapacity risk seen for next 3-4 years
items.quote: Yes, but we don't see that happening for next at least three, four years. I mean next three, four years, it should be good.

items.statement: No product diversification planned, focus on transformers only
items.quote: No, not as of now. We are focusing on making this expansion, where we'll be manufacturing 220 kV class. So it is a, I mean, different type of manufacturing altogether. So we'll be focusing on that only. We are not looking at any other product.

items.statement: No outsourcing planned to maintain quality control
items.quote: No, we don't plan to do that as well because we want to have control on our quality. And because of that only we have built a good reputation in the market.

items.statement: Domestic revenue 80% from solar/wind generation segment
items.quote: Yes. It will be about 80% of domestic revenue.

items.statement: 220 kV transformer lead time 22 weeks from order to dispatch
items.quote: I think from order to dispatch, it would be about 22 weeks.

items.quote: The retail book has grown quarter-on-quarter, even during this quarter and a year-on-year growth is about 6.6%. As I did mention, we do expect that in the second half, retail growth should improve.

items.statement: B&K transaction revenue ~15-16 crores/month (~40-45 crores/quarter); Q1 15 crores, Q2 ~45 crores
items.quote: it's approximately in the region of 15 to 16 crores a month. So around 40 to 45 crores a quarter.

items.statement: MD & CEO Imtaiyazur Rahman to step down on 1 Feb 2026; Vetri Subramaniam appointed as incoming MD & CEO; Rahman to serve as Strategic Advisor until 12 Jun 2026
items.quote: the Board has unanimously decided to appoint Mr. Vetri Subramaniam as an incoming MD and CEO of UTI AMC with effects from 1st February 2026. 1st February marks UTI AMC's Foundation Day and I believe it is a fitting moment for me to pass the baton to Vetri.

items.statement: Voluntary Retirement Scheme (VRS) approved for 479 eligible employees (351 in sales-related functions) effective 1 Oct 2025; applications close 31 Oct 2025
items.quote: the Board of Directors of UTI AMC approved the implementation of the Voluntary Retirement Scheme (VRS) for select categories of employees effective from 1st October 2025. As per the scheme, eligible employees can submit their VRS applications till 31st October 2025.

items.statement: Family pension revision under VRS creates one-time actuarial charge of Rs. 25 crore booked in Q2 FY26; additional Rs. 6.5 crore actuarial impact from salary revision also booked
items.quote: The one -time financial aspect of this revision as well as the actuarial valuation is Rs. 25 crores which has been fully accounted in the financial results for this quarter.

items.statement: Full-year other expenses guidance maintained at 7-8% growth despite Q2 volatility from CSR cash accounting
items.quote: for the full year, we maintain a guidance of close to around 7 %-8% for the other expenses. Some volatility because the CSR expenses is actually accounted on a cash basis.

items.statement: VRS cost to be fully charged to P&L in Q3 FY26; tax amortisation over 5 years will raise effective tax rate to 26-27% for FY26
items.quote: The entire VRS cost will be booked in the P&L in the 3rd quarter itself as per the accounting standard. There is some impact as far as the taxation is concerned, that these expenses need to be amortized over a period of 5 years as per the Income Tax act.

items.statement: SIP AUM Rs. 42,267 crore (up 5.98% YoY); SIP inflows Q2 Rs. 2,338 crore (up 12.04% YoY); H1 FY26 SIP inflows Rs. 4,599 crore (up 17.70% YoY)

items.quote: UTI was able to capture a market share of 6.2% of the gross sales of the industry during this quarter and market share of 6.4% of the gross sales for the first half of the financial year 2026.

items.statement: Consolidated core income Rs. 390 crore (up 5% YoY, 3% QoQ); Normalised consolidated core PAT Rs. 127 crore (down 5% YoY, up 4% QoQ); Standalone normalised core PAT Rs. 124 crore (up 7% YoY, 5% QoQ)

items.statement: Yields: Equity/hybrid ~75 bps; ETF/index ~8 bps (up from 6 bps); Cash/liquid ~9 bps; Fixed income ~19-20 bps (marginal reduction due to shorter duration)

items.quote: Our products, particularly the multi-asset fund and the aggressive hybrid fund are already approved on several platforms. So we are pushing both for sales through lump sum mode as well as through the SIP mode. The balance advantage fund is a much younger fund for us, just about 2 years of track record, but it has done well over that period.

items.statement: UTI Multi Cap Fund launched May 2025; AUM Rs. 1,576 crore as of 30 Sep 2025 (67% above NFO collection)
items.quote: As of 30th September, the fund had asse ts of Rs. 1,576 crore s, around 67% more than what we collected during the NFO.

items.quote: If you look at as of September 2025, 89% of our total gross sales in the quarter came from the digital platform. And in the last 4 quarters, an average of around 92% of the gross sales are coming through the digital channel.

items.statement: SIP channel mix: MFDs ~50%, RIAs ~19% (up 40-45% YoY), Fin-techs up 40-45% YoY; 75% of new SIPs from digital
items.quote: The highest share of SIP flows that we are getting is still coming from the MFDs, which is about 50% of our SIP flow and this is followed by RIAs, which is close to about 19%. And the rest is coming through direct , Fin-tech and BND. items.statement: UTI Pension Fund plans to expand branches from 31 to 40 in FY26; added 119 clients in H1 FY26
items.quote: We currently operate through 31 branches across India and plan to take the total number of branches to 40 in FY26. In the first half of FY26, we added 119 clients.

items.statement: UTI Pension Fund AUM Rs. 3.89 lakh crore (up 15.82% YoY); manages 24.62% of NPS industry AUM; H1 PAT Rs. 28 crore (down 3.4% YoY)

items.statement: UTI International AUM USD 2.66 bn (Rs. 23,647 crore); UTI India Dynamic Equity Fund AUM USD 874 mn; decline due to Phoenix Fund maturity and mark-to-market impact of ~Rs. 2,000 crore

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin guidance 28% to 30%

items.quote: The pilot plant capex is proceeding as per plan and is expected to be completed by Q3 FY '26.

items.quote: So out of INR250 crores capex plan for FY '26, INR40 crores we are expecting towards maintenance capex and rest is from the growth -- for the growth capex only. out of which around INR180 crores for the full year was planned for electrolyte additive capex and INR30 crores was planned for pilot plant capex.

items.quote: No, no. It cannot go 100% in 1 year. It will take around 3 years' time to reach an optimum level of capacity.

items.statement: CDMO projects expected to start contributing by end of FY26 subject to regulatory approvals
items.quote: Our ongoing CDMO projects are progressing in line with expectations and expected to start contributing by end of FY '26, subject to regulatory approvals.

items.quote: In our battery chemical business, we have successfully secured multiple customers across diverse geographies. Production is expected to commence in Q4 FY '26 once our ongoing capex is completed.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 gross margin expanded 1,232 bps YoY to 55.8%
items.quote: The gross margin expanded by 1,232 basis points Y-o-Y to 55.8%. Gross margin was driven by improved product mix and operational efficiencies.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 31.1%, up 1,130 bps YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margins were at 31.1%, up 1,130 basis points Y-o-Y. EBITDA margin was driven by expansion in gross margin as well as operating leverage.

items.statement: Margin improvement driven by product mix restructuring, operational efficiency, and solar power contribution

This has resulted in better product mix leading to better margins.

items.statement: Solar power plant 5 MW commissioned in Q2 FY26, part of 16 MW total
items.quote: Because the 5-megawatt project was commissioned in this quarter, it was partly accounted in this quarter for 5 megawatt out of the total 16 megawatt.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 working capital improved to 100 days, 28 days better than Q1 FY26
items.quote: Our working capital for the quarter improved to 100 days, which is 28 days improvement compared to Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: Full year FY26 working capital expected 95-105 days
items.quote: For the full year, we believe working capital would be around anything between 95 to 105 days.

items.statement: Net cash and cash equivalents INR240.6 crores as of 30 Sep 2025
items.quote: Net cash and cash equivalents were at INR240.6 crores as on 30th September 2025.

items.quote: So noncontrolling stake, we paid some premium to a noncontrolling stake that is showing as a goodwill. So goodwill of around INR16 crores has been generated for this quarter for investment we have done in Indichem.

items.quote: In South Korean JV, we are the investment partner with 75% investment and 25% is with our Korean partner who will bring their technology, their market as well as the production capability. Naresh Patel: Supplier of starting material. Abhishek Patel: As well as the supply of starting

items.statement: Project payback period expected 3 to 3.5 years
items.quote: For this -- any of the project, we expect the payback to be around 3 to 3.5 year kind of payback.

items.statement: Electrolyte additive plant output completely for export market, no domestic supply

items.quote: Management has introduced a lot of system digitalizations, KMPs are introduced time to time required for each segment. So this is a part of the business cycle, and this is part of the business to grow from one state to another state.

items.statement: Semiconductor chemicals revenue contribution not disclosed for next 2-3 years
items.quote: No, that we are actually not disclosing anywhere for the future businesses.

items.statement: Management reiterated confidence in achieving 15%+ sales growth, 15% PAT margin and 30% EBITDA margin
items.quote: Overall, I think we're safe -- we continue to feel confident in our guidance that we will grow at a 15% plus rate and also produce a profit after tax of the 15% and an EBITDA in the 30% range.

items.statement: No major headwinds seen for H2; GST cuts and stable wedding calendar should support steady demand
items.quote: The good news is, look towards this quarter, we see none of those factors coming into play. On the contrary, we do see the fact that the GST reductions have taken place to create and spur more demand for our products.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 40 bps YoY in Q2; EBITDA grew 12% standalone and 10% consolidated, in line with sales growth
items.quote: I'm pleased that we were able to drive sales growth while increasing our gross margins by 40 basis poin ts over the previous year. On the EBITDA side, we grew by 12% for the stand -alone and 10% for the consolidated business for the quarter, which is very much in line with our sales

items.statement: Net 38 stores added in Q2 (42 openings, 4 closures); 10 Walkway stores opened (highest ever); 4 Foot Locker stores opened
items.quote: 42 stores. We had 4 closures, bringing us to a net new store addition of 38 stores. Of this, we had 4 high-profile Foot Locker stores opened in the quarter as well. items.statement: Clarks launched in 200 Metro/Mochi doors; plan to expand to 300 doors next quarter; full supply chain stabilization expected in 2-3 quarters
items.quote: We were also able to launch Clarks footwear into 200 of our Metro and Mochi doors, and it has done extremely well. We plan on expanding this to 300 doors in the next quarter.

items.quote: We've seen as much as 11% reduction in footwear priced between INR1,000 and INR2,500. And a 6% reduction for footwear under INR1,000.

items.quote: If you compare it with September '24, our overall increas e, I think, is around INR80 crores, INR85 crores Second point is, obviously, the inventory that we carry is also in line with all the new store additions that we are planning to add over next 2 quarters

items.statement: BIS issues for FILA/Foot Locker not fully resolved but considerable headway; expect resolution by early next calendar year

items.statement: Walkway targets Tier 2/3 towns and unorganized market (70% of industry); model now validated after 2-year pause; 10 stores added in Q2
items.quote: We also think that's a play where we're able to start tapping into the unorganized market, which is, as you know, in our business, in our industry, it's almost 70% of our business is done in the unorganized market.

items.statement: Crocs network addition of 10% per year for next 3-5 years easily achievable
