items.quote: For FY 2025, we raised our dividend payout to 26.3% from 25.5% last year, in line with our goal of crossing 30% dividend payout by FY 2030.

items.statement: Niyant Maru appointed CFO from October 28, 2025 for interim 9-month period, Gandharv Tongia resigned
items.quote: I would also like to take this opportunity to welcome Mr. Niyant Maru, who will join us as the Chief Financial Officer from October 28, 2025, following Gandharv's resignation. He will serve in this role for an interim period of 9 months, until a suitable successor is appointed.

items.statement: No increase in competitive intensity seen; pricing premium vs peers sustained
items.quote: We are not seeing any particular increase in competitive intensity, and that is perhaps visible in the gross margin that we are delivering. Our pricing premium compared to the other players in the industry continues to be as it is.

items.statement: Wires & Cables volume growth in high-teens, revenue growth 21% YoY on high base (28% YoY last year)
items.quote: The Wires & Cables business delivered a 21% YoY revenue growth, supported by high-teen volume expansion during the quarter.

items.statement: FMEG solar products standout performer driven by central/state rooftop incentive schemes
items.quote: The solar products category was once again the standout performer, driven by robust demand under central and state solar rooftop incentive schemes.

items.statement: US export outlook uncertain due to tariff negotiations; ongoing trade talks may resolve by end-November
items.quote: U.S. is a developing situation. So, it will be very difficult for us to comment at this point of time what we can expect perhaps by the end of this quarter, or maybe in the next quarter or so. We don't know what the tariff number will be by next month either. Hopefully, the ongoing trade negotiations get resolved by the end of November.

items.statement: Income tax search matter: CIT(A) allowed appeals in full, NIL tax demand; order effect pending
items.quote: During the quarter ended 30th September 2025, the CIT(A) allowed the Company's appeals in full, resulting in NIL tax demand. The order giving effect to the CIT(A) decision is currently pending before the assessing officer.

items.statement: HVDC cables not pursued currently; limited domestic projects, no local manufacturing capability, imports used
items.quote: As of now, there are very limited projects in the country that requires HVDC cables. None of the players in the country have the tech to manufacture them, and whatever cables are being utilized or will be supplied for those projects will be imported.

items.statement: Special purpose cables (defense, auto, railway coaches) in low single digits but fastest-growing vertical; demand ~2.5-3% of sector capex
items.quote: You can apply a percentage of about 2.5% to 3% to the capex, which are currently getting committed in these sectors, and that would represent the demand for cables generated from those sectors.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY26 EBITDA guidance of INR 5,500-6,000 crores
items.quote: All-in-all, ladies and gentlemen, we reaffirm our FY '26 EBITDA guidance in the range of INR 5,500 crores and INR 6,000 crores.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR ~47,000 crores (~24 GW) as of September 30, 2025
items.quote: Our order book continues to be strong at INR ~47,000 crores as of September 30, 2025.

items.statement: Total module capacity reached ~18.7 GW (India ~16.1 GW, US 2.6 GW); cell capacity fully operational at 5.4 GW
items.quote: Our total module capacity has touched ~18.7 gigawatts, and our cell capacity is now fully functional and operational at 5.4 gigawatts, the largest cell manufacturing facility of its kind in India.

items.statement: Board approved additional INR ~8,175 crores capex; total capex plan INR 25,000+ crores over next 24 months, back-end loaded
items.quote: Our overall capex program continues with additional INR ~8,175 crores approved by our Board of Directors.

items.statement: Target module capacity 26.7 GW by FY26; cell capacity 15.4 GW and ingot/wafer 10 GW by 2027
items.quote: We intend to operationalize the remaining module capacity expansion in FY '26 to take it to 26.7 gigawatts. Further, by 2027, we intend to scale up our cell capacity to 15.4 gigawatts and ingots and wafer facility of 10 gigawatts by 2027.

items.statement: BESS capacity being scaled from 3.5 GWh to 20 GWh with INR ~8,000 crores investment; first phase 3.5 GWh commercial production expected FY27
items.quote: We are augmenting our battery energy storage system capacity from 3.5 gigawatts hour to 20 gigawatts hours.

items.statement: Acquired 76% stake in Racemosa Energy India (smart meters), 64% in Kotsons (transformers), and Meyer Burger US solar assets
items.quote: We have also made three strategic acquisitions. Smart meters are going to be extremely important components of renewable value chain and hence we have announced 76% stake in Racemosa Energy India. We have acquired 64% stake in Kotsons Private Limited, which marks our entry into the world of transformers. And recently, we have acquired solar manufacturing assets of M eyer Burger in the US, further

items.statement: India solar capacity projected to more than double from ~127 GW to ~280 GW by 2030; US solar to reach ~500 GW by 2030; data center demand to surge from 33 GW to 176 GW by 2035
items.quote: India's solar capacity is projected to move more than double from ~127 gigawatts to around 280 gigawatts by 2030.

items.statement: ALMM extended for cells from June 2026 and ingots/wafers from June 2028; GST cut from 12% to 5% expected to improve affordability
items.quote: The regulatory environment continues to be conducive with initiatives like extension of ALMM for cells since June 2026 and for ingots and wafers from June 2028, aiming further strengthening India's domestic value chain from ingots to modules and reduce rel iance on

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin expanded to 25.17% from 17% YoY; DCR segment carries 300-350 bps higher margin than non-DCR
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin has also expanded to 25.17 % versus 17% year-on-year basis.

items.statement: US module realizations 26-30 cents/watt vs India non-DCR 16-17 cents/watt; tariff costs passed to customers via change-of-law clauses or negotiation
items.quote: So, the US, typically we have about anything between 28–30 cents. That is the range which is ongoing.

items.statement: Inventory spike to INR ~1,300 crores (vs normal INR 300-400 crores) due to goods-in-transit for export orders; will normalize next quarter
items.quote: This is finished goods. But this time, there's a bump up to almost INR 1300 crores. So, you see that will taper out.

items.statement: Domestic sales mix ~19-20% retail, rest large institutional; retail growing and not fully captured in order book
items.quote: About 19 % to 20% is retail and the rest is large institutional customers, roughly.

items.statement: Order book split ~60% overseas, 40% domestic; Q2 revenue split 53% domestic, 47% overseas; US IRA benefits INR 1.6B in quarter
items.quote: We already spoke about order book and it stands roughly at 24 gigawatts, of which approximately 60% is overseas and balance 40% is domestic.

items.statement: Board approved interim dividend of INR 2 per share
items.quote: I am pleased to mention that the Board has approved an interim dividend of INR 2 per share, reaffirming our commitment towards rewarding our shareholders.

items.statement: US AD/CVD investigation ongoing; early days, cooperating fully; supply chain configured to avoid FEOC entities and minimize tariffs
items.quote: I can -- what I can say is that I definitely confirm that the probe is on. Now, it's early days for the probe. So, we really don't know in which direction and what manner will it proceed.

items.statement: Highest ever quarterly module production 2.64 GW; cell production 0.6 GW ramping up in H2
items.quote: We have recorded the highest ever quarterly production of 2.64 gigawatts.

items.statement: Expanding into BESS (20 GWh), inverters (4 GW), electrolyser (1 GW), green hydrogen (2027), transformers, smart meters; signed 413 MW PPAs, secured 6.1 GW connectivity
items.quote: We are augmenting our battery energy storage system capacity from 3.5 gigawatts hour to 20 gigawatts hours. The electrolyser manufacturing capacity is being augmented to 1 gigawatt and the inverter manufacturing facility from 3 gigawatts to 4 gigawatts.

items.statement: Partnership with IIT Bombay to train 3,000+ individuals in perovskite and advanced solar cell technologies
items.quote: Our partnership with IIT Bombay will train over 3 ,000 individuals in deep technology and advanced solar cell technologies, particularly the perovskite technology.

items.statement: Completed divestment of 88.2 lakh Indosolar shares via OFS generating INR 523 crores profit classified as other equity
items.quote: Waaree Energies has completed its divestment of about 88.2 lakh equity shares of Indosolar through OFS, and this has generated a profit of about INR 523 crores, and this has been classified as other equity in the consolidated balance sheet.

items.statement: Managing gross margins by back-to-back sourcing; input costs trend with prices with small lag; US supply chain configured to avoid entity-of-concern sources
items.quote: We are always managing Waaree at the gross margin level, because the input cost, as you know, also trends in the direction of the prices.

items.statement: INR 25,000+ crore capex plan excludes acquisitions like Kotsons, Racemosa, Meyer Burger; these are over and above
items.quote: In terms of whether our INR 25,000+ crores capex includes these, the answer to that is no. That is over and above.

items.statement: Ingot-wafer and cell capacity expanded from 6 GW to 10 GW each; projects on schedule for 2027 completion
items.quote: You must have seen that we have actually upped our capacity from 6 gigawatts to 10 gigawatts for ingots and wafers as well as for cells. And so, those projects are moving right on schedule and on time for cells 2027 and for ingots and wafers 2027 completion.

items.statement: Module utilisation 80-85%, cell utilisation 85-90% of nameplate capacity as thumb rule
items.quote: So, like a thumb rule for that, for modules, it is going to be in the region of 80% to 85%. And for cells, it will be, say, 85% to 90%. Thumb rule.

items.statement: Chikhli cell facility to reach 80-85% utilisation within current quarter after key event
items.quote: So, we were waiting for a very important event where the capacity would jump and that event has happened. So, we will make sure that now the amount of production jumps quite dramatically. And yes, within this quarter, we will see that it kind of gets to 80%, 85% utilization pretty quick.

items.statement: Indosolar facility utilisation currently 75%; ramp-up via training, retention, equipment tuning, power stability
items.quote: Utilization of the facility is in the region of around 75%.

items.statement: US facility fully booked; sourcing cells globally meeting FEOC requirements; manufacturing panels for US from both India and US
items.quote: From an overall supply chain, we source cells from all across the world for the US facility, which first of all pass the test of US law. So, there are FEOC requirements, which we need to take care of. So, supply chain is aligned in that manner, number one. And number two, we do send, so I don't know if I made it very clear, but we do manufacture panels for the US from India as well as from the US.

items.statement: Target blended EBITDA margin 22-25% post backward integration; module alone 18-19%, cell adds 300-350 bps
items.quote: The margin should bump up between 300 to 350 basis points overall on a sustained basis. And, of course, you can play with a mix of exports and retail, etc. So, anything between 22% to 25% is a good margin to look at on the backward integration. And that's what we really want to maintain at around like 24%, 25%.

items.statement: North Star EBITDA target INR 5,500-6,000 crores; margin managed to this target regardless of geography
items.quote: The way we manage it is we manage it to our North Star of EBITDA, INR 5,500 crores to INR 6,000 crores. And that's how we would like to deal with it.

items.statement: DCR and non-DCR module margins expected to remain in similar range; pricing may decline slightly with efficiency gains
items.quote: I think it might go down a little bit as manufacturers get better and better in their efficiencies and their own costs kind of go down. But from a margin perspective, I think we will continue to be in a similar range as what we are at this point in time.

items.statement: PM Surya Ghar market growing from 3 GW last year to 10 GW this year, more next year; targeting 25-30% market share
items.quote: Last year, it was 3 gigawatts. This year, 10 gigawatts. Next year, probably much more than that. And so, our attempt is to capture a fairly large element of that. Now, I don't want to put an exact number to it, but it would be safe to say that I would like to be somewhere between 25% and 30% of the market share for that.

items.statement: US CBP anti-dumping probe on cells just begun; internal review suggests limited liabilities but outcome uncertain
items.quote: So, that probe by CBP has just begun. And so, it'll be incorrect for us to really comment on potential likely outcomes. Our internal review suggests that we may not be facing a whole host of liabilities as far as that is concerned. But it's best that we wait and understand as the ADD investigation goes ahead.

items.statement: Inverter manufacturing beyond assembly - proper electronic manufacturing with clean rooms; not mere assembly
items.quote: Your question on what level of manufacturing we will be getting into, it is going to be well beyond assembly. You know, we are actually having proper electronic manufacturing equipment, again, clean rooms that are required for doing that. So it is not mere assembly. It is actually a proper assembly of components and related manufacturing.

items.statement: Already in HJT technology via Meyer Burger US facility; production lines flexible for new technologies; actively investing in R&D
items.quote: We actually already are in HJT. We have actually supplied several of these HJT modules. The Meyer Burger facility that we have actually acquired in the U.S. is an HJT facility. So, we are already there as far as that is concerned. But our production line is fairly flexible to take different kinds of technologies, as well.

items.statement: Meyer Burger acquisition (INR 18M) includes manufacturing facility and reasonable cell inventory; cell line not acquired (INR 11M was for inventory only)
items.quote: So, Deepak, I think the number that you mentioned for Waaree, like around INR18 million that you have paid it for, it includes the entire manufacturing facility, right, as well as the some good amount of inventories of cells as well. So ours does not only include the only the manufacturing facility, but along with it, the reasonable amount of quantity of cells as well.

items.statement: Subsidiaries like Indosolar may be consolidated over time; currently focusing on ramping capacity and optimizing operations
items.quote: For any organization which is growing at the pace at which we are growing, we will have subsidiaries and step-down subsidiaries which get created. And over a period of time, we might actually think of consolidating some of them as well. At this point in time, predicting how it is going to be would not be a good thing to do.

items.statement: Other expenses rose to 9% from normal 6-6.5% due to higher export mix (freight and duties); expected to normalize
items.quote: So, basically, the other expense also consists of freight and duties, and we have a good mix of our exports this time. So, that has come into play. Normally, you will see when there is a normal spread in terms of the segment, it ranges about 6% and 6.5%. And so, now, this quarter, it is 9%. But of course, we eventually expect it to come down.

items.statement: Substantial cash on balance sheet; forecasted earnings plus undrawn bank borrowings to fund capex; financial closures done ahead of spend
items.quote: As far as the overall support on the capex side, you see a substantial amount of cash lying in the balance sheet even today. And then the earnings that we have forecasted should add up to that to be able to do the entire capex. Also, as you know, that our balance sheet discloses few borrowings that we have taken from the bank, but the drawdown has not happened.

items.statement: Material revenue from new verticals (BESS, inverters, transformers) from FY28 onwards; progressive quarterly commissioning benefits before that
items.quote: So, the actual benefit if you ask me on the announced capex is the last leg of capex is getting completed in FY28. So, FY28 on wards you will see the complete benefit of the announced capex so far. But certainly, quarter on quarter you will see the previous capex getting closed out and benefit start coming in the financial statements.

items.statement: PLI not baked into plans; treated as cherry on top; current performance without PLI
items.quote: We typically don't bake in PLI in our overall plans. It's going to be a cherry on the top as we move forward.

items.statement: Top three risks monitored: cybersecurity, ESG, regulatory environment changes
items.quote: You know, we have all seen what has happened to Jaguar Land Rover. And so, cybersecurity tends to be one of the very important discussions that we have internally to ensure that it is taken care of. ESG and the various elements that go with it is the second risk that we track. And the third risk is the regulatory environment changes that are required -- I mean, that happen all around us and have a

items.statement: BESS technology evolving similar to solar; line configured for lithium-ion but adaptable to sodium-ion; energy density key pacing item
items.quote: From a technology perspective, Nirali, it's very, very similar to solar. It's a continuously evo lving technology. The key pacing item as far as battery technology is concerned is the energy density. How much energy can you pack in a given volume? And that keeps getting better and better and better

items.statement: BESS financial metrics expected similar to Waaree Energies; payback 3-5 years; ROCE/ROE ranges maintained
items.quote: In general, our paybacks are always in between three years to five years range . So, whatever capex that we do on the manufacturing front, we believe this should be no different than what it is today. So, you may continue to see the similar range of ROC E and ROE that you see over a period of time at Waaree Energies level

items.statement: Acquired businesses (Kotsons, Racemosa, Meyer Burger) have Waaree as big internal customer; immediate synergies and alignment
items.quote: I think these are all adjacencies. So from a business perspective, all of these businesses have a big customer. That is the big internal Waaree as a customer. And that's where synergies immediately play out. And that's where the alignment also immediately plays out.

items.statement: Indosolar ramp-up dependent on training, talent retention, equipment fine-tuning, and grid power stability in Noida
items.quote: Our capacity is in the region of – I mean, capacity utilization is in the region of around 70% to 75%. And typically, the way you ramp up is, number one, as your people get more and more trained and understand how to manufacture, it goes up. So, training is a very important component of that. Retention of talent is a very important component of that.

items.statement: Vision to be energy transition major of choice across solar, BESS, hydrogen, transformers, smart meters, inverters
items.quote: From a vision perspective, it's very clear. We want to be the energy transition major of choice , r ight? So, whatever technology, whatever components, whatever ideas are required for energy transition, we should be there and we should be the supplier or vendor of choice

items.statement: PAT target doubled from FY24 Rs 411 cr to Rs 800+ cr by FY27; already at Rs 369 cr in H1 FY26, on track to achieve in 2 years instead of 3
items.quote: We have earlier guided that our ambition was to dou ble our PAT from FY24, which was Rs. 411 crores by FY27. Today, with our progress in just 2 years, we are already nearing this milestone, well ahead of plan

items.statement: Expect double-digit growth in FY27 once capacity additions contribute
items.quote: Yes. Definitely, we see double-digit growth.

items.statement: Speciality carbon black brownfield expansion to 130,000 MT by end Q3 FY26, total carbon black capacity 250,000 MT
items.quote: In speciality carbon black, the brownfield expansion project is progressing well, set to more than double our capacity to 130,000 MT per annum by the end of Q3 FY26, Positioning Himadri as the world's largest single-site producer of speciality carbon black, this expansion will take our total carbon black capacity to 250,000 MT per annum.

items.statement: Anthraquinone and carbazole facility expected commissioning by Q2 FY27
items.quote: In parallel, our new speciality chemical segment is gaining momentum with the upcoming facility of anthraquinone and carbazole production that is expected to be commissioned by Q2 FY27.

items.statement: LFP cathode active material 40,000 MT plant on track for Q3 FY27 operations; phase capacity 200,000 MT
items.quote: Targeting a phase capacity of 200,000 MT per annum, the in itial 40,000 MT per annum plant is already under development and on track to commence operations by Q3

items.statement: Coal tar pitch distillation capacity increasing from 500,000 MT to 600,000 MT
items.quote: Our current capacity is 500,000 MT. We are going to become 600,000 MT.

items.statement: Birla Tyres PCR plant installation to commence within next 12 months
items.quote: For the passenger car radial unit designed for EVs and SUVs, the installation of plant and machinery is scheduled to co mmence within the next 12 months

items.statement: Speciality carbon black expansion to more than double capacity to 130,000 MT by end Q3 FY26
items.quote: In speciality carbon black, the brownfield expansion project is progressing well, set to more than double our capacity to 130,000 MT per annum by the end of Q3 FY26

items.statement: Coal tar pitch capacity increasing from 500,000 MT to 600,000 MT; utilization impact from Q3, full from Q4/Q1
items.quote: Our current capacity is 500,000 MT. We are going to become 600,000 MT. Sanjesh Jain: How should we think this utilization? Anurag Choudhary: This utilization from Q4, it will start. Q3 will have some impact and Q4 and then from Q1

items.statement: Birla Tyres expects 30-40% capacity utilization next year from current 10%
items.quote: Currently suppose we are running at 10% capacity utilization, next year we expect at least 30% to 40% capacity utilization.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA Rs 243 cr up 21% YoY, PAT Rs 187 cr up 39% YoY; H1 EBITDA Rs 477 cr up 23%, PAT Rs 369 cr up 43%
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter came in at Rs. 243 crores, a growth of 21% year-on-year, over Rs. 201 crores in Q2 FY25. PAT stood at Rs. 187 crores, reflecting a 39% increase year-on-year compared to Rs. 134 crores in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Margin improvement driven 65-70% by high value-added product mix, 30% by operational efficiency
items.quote: High value-added products contributed around 65 %-70% and 30% was in account of operational efficiency.

items.statement: Margins sustainable, not dependent on raw material price movements; 100% pass-through mechanism
items.quote: 100%. Whether price goes up or down, what difference it will make is only in terms of percentage of margin and in terms of top line. Not in terms of absolute margin

items.statement: Raw material price correction 13-15% YoY impacted revenue; 100% pass-through to customers
items.quote: Corresponding quarter last year, the average raw material price was 13% higher than current prices, 13% to 15%. So, when the prices came down, the realization also came down. That resulted in lower turnover.

items.statement: Volumes at peak capacity utilization; demand strong, no softness; volume growth from Q4 with new capacity
items.quote: The volumes are at the same level basically because we are more or less at peak capacity utilizations. With the new capacity being added in next quarter for speciality ca rbon black and de-bottling neck for the coal tar pitch also happening, then we can see volume growth from Q4 onwards

items.statement: Global demand strong across 54 countries; no significant positivity or negativity
items.quote: See, for us, demand has been strong only. Reason being that our volumes of carbon black are fully sold. So, we do not see any significant positivity or negativity in the demand side earlier also and even today.

items.statement: Over 60 new speciality carbon black grades launched
items.quote: With over 60 new grades launched, we are strengthening our leadership and product diversity in this critical segment.

items.statement: LFP cathode material supplied to IBC for Prabal 2000 cells; encouraging feedback from demo plant
items.quote: IBC is a clear example. So, IBC is coming out with a cell Prabal 2000 with LFP cathode material. For which we sent them the sample, and they tested the material. And they were so pleased to see the quality of the material that we had detailed discussion, and interactions.

items.statement: Achieved ISCC-Plus certification for Mahistikry plant; CDP Supplier Engagement 'A' rating; EcoVadis Platinum (top 1% globally)
items.quote: This quarter, Himadri achieved the ISCC-Plus certification for our Mah istikry plant, reaffirming our dedication to responsible manufacturing and circular economy principles. We earned an ‘A’ rating in CDP's Suppliers Engagement Assessment, reflecting strong supplier collaboration on environmental performance. It's also worth highlighting that we have previously received the prestigious Platinum r

items.statement: Working capital at 31% of topline; expected to remain at same levels for next 3 quarters
items.quote: See, current working capital is 31% of the top line and we expect this to remain in the same levels

items.statement: Short-term borrowings increase due to commercial papers issued against bank deposits; no leveraging
items.quote: So, actually these are commercial papers we have issued against which we have done deposits with banks. So, there is no leveraging we are doing.

items.statement: Strategic investments: Sicona Battery Technologies 17.6%, International Battery Company 16.2%, Invati Creations 40%
items.quote: our strategic investment in Si cona 17.6%, International Battery Company 16.2% and In vati Creations 40% give us access to cutting -edge technologies, R&D capabilities and a presence across the entire LIB value chain for anode and cathode materials to cell manufacturing

items.statement: EBITDA per kg carbon black improved from Rs 15 to Rs 17 over last year
items.quote: We have increased in last one year, the EBITDA per kg from Rs. 15 rupees to Rs. 17.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 8-10% annually for FY26 and FY27 before new capacity comes online
items.quote: We should continue for the next two years to grow in a range of around 8% to 10% every year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improvement guidance of 1-2% over next 24 months before new projects start
items.quote: we should be able to further enhance our EBITDA margins ranging around 1% to 2% in next 24 months before the other project starts coming in.

items.statement: Total capex of Rs 1,900-2,000 crore planned through March 2028 across all projects
items.quote: So the total is 900 plus. T hat is somewhere around Rs. 1,900 to Rs. 2,000 crores of CAPEX happening in March '28

items.statement: Greenfield glass plant in Madhya Pradesh capex of Rs 700 crore, operational by March 2027
items.quote: the overall capital expenditure in terms of land and building and other expenses is odd Rs. 700 crores.

items.statement: Aluminum beverage can plant phase 1 capex of Rs 850 crore, commercial production by Q3 FY28
items.quote: The total outlay in the first phase is around Rs. 850 crores. A major chunk will be spent by that time, or by December 2027.

items.statement: Debottlenecking and other expansion capex of Rs 120-150 crore in next one year excluding major projects
items.quote: The overall spend in the next one year, I think, on a rollin g basis excluding Gwalior plant or Aluminum beverage CAN, should be in range of odd Rs. 120 crores to Rs. 150 crores

items.statement: North India greenfield glass plant adding 500 TPD (25% increase) to reach 2,600 TPD total by March 2027
items.quote: The project is on track to be operational by March 2027 and will add 500 TPD of new capacity — a 25% increase in our overall glass production — taking our total to 2,600 TPD.

items.statement: Aluminum beverage can plant in UP with 950 million cans annual capacity initially, scaling to 1.6 billion by FY30
items.quote: The facility will be developed in two phases, starting with an annual capacity of 950 million CANS and scaling up to 1.6 billion CANS by FY30.

items.statement: Container glass debottlenecking from 1,850 to 1,900 TPD and specialty glass from 154 to 200 TPD by March 2026
items.quote: Our Container Glass capacity will increase from 1,850 TPD to 1,900 TPD, while our Specialty Glass capacity will see a significant expansion from 154 TPD to 200 TPD

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin at 24.9%, up 250 bps sequentially from adjusted Q1 margin of 22.4%
items.quote: Our Q2 EBITDA margin (excluding other income) was a healthy 24.9%. This represents a significant 250 basis point jump compared to the adjusted Q1 margin of 22.4%

items.statement: Specialty glass EBITDA margin expansion potential of 4-5% over next 18 months
items.quote: for the EBITDA margin expansion, you can easily consider maybe 4% to 5% over the next 18 months happening on the specialty glass.

items.statement: Term loan prepayment of Rs 193 crore in July 2025 reduced term borrowings to Rs 233 crore as of September 2025
items.quote: We have demonstrated our commitment to financial prudence by completing a term loan prepayment of ₹193 crore in July 2025. This has substantially reduced our term loan borrowings to just ₹233 crore as of September 2025

items.statement: Peak debt expected at Rs 1,000-1,200 crore by March 2028 even without equity issuance
items.quote: Rs. 1,000 to 1,200 crores around that.

items.statement: Board approved equity raise resolution, seeking shareholder approval, may execute in next 3-6 months
items.quote: The board passed a resolution to raise equity through various instruments. And we are in process of seeking shareholder approval also and I think it is already up with the shareholders.

items.statement: Current assets holding days increased ~15 days as of Sept 2025, expected to normalize in 1-2 quarters
items.quote: There has been a temporary increase in our current assets holding days by around 15 days as on 30th September 2025 as compared to corresponding last year's figures. These current assets holding levels will normalize during next 1-2 quarters

items.statement: Inventory build-up for Q3-Q4 seasonal demand; receivables delay due to customer software issue, resolved post-quarter
items.quote: the inventory is on account of our continuity of the production, because the upcoming season of 3rd Quarter and 4th Quarter. So we stock the finished goods to be ready when the seasonal market demand in Q3 & Q4.

items.statement: Prices linked to major raw material inputs with time lags of weeks to up to one year depending on contracts
items.quote: we are having an understanding with our customers, with our buyers, that these prices will be linked to the input prices of the major raw material. So, whatever is good, yes , there can be a time lag.

items.statement: Currently using over 40% cullet (recycled glass), expect percentage to increase further with municipal corporation improvements
items.quote: Yes, we are using more than 40% of the cullet. And we will be using more also in the times to come.

items.statement: Current export share 5-7% of revenue; aspiration to reach 10-15% overall and 40% in specialty glass
items.quote: As on today, our export percentage falls anywhere between 5% to 7%. We have an aspiration of increasing our export to 10% to 15%, total. In a specialty glass, this percentage is quite high. And we have an aspiration of taking this percentage to 40% in the s pecialty glass

items.statement: Demand stable with end-user industries (beer, liquor) growing 8-9%; company at peak capacity utilization ~95%
items.quote: the beer industry, they have indicated that they wil l be growing by around 8% -9%. Liquor industry will be growing by 8% -9% a nd same thing with the other industries.

items.statement: H2 FY26 capitalization of INR 17,000-18,000 crores capex to yield INR 2,800 crores annual EBITDA run-rate; transmission INR 1,800-1,900 crores, distribution INR 250-275 crores, smart metering INR 800 crores
items.quote: So, all in all, we will capitalize about INR17,000 to INR18,000 crores of capex, which will contribute about INR2,800 crores of EBITDA on an annual run-rate basis.

items.statement: H1 FY26 consolidated EBITDA INR 4,144 crores (+13% YoY); adjusted PAT INR 1,096 crores (+42% YoY) excluding INR 314 crore deferred tax reversal in prior year
items.quote: The total EBITDA, that is the consolidated EBITDA, has increased to INR4,144 crores, which is a 13% increase on a year basis. Our consolidated PBT has grown to INR1,404 crores, which is 34% increase over the previous year.

items.statement: AEML deleveraging: bought back $44M bonds in Q2, $49.5M in Q1, $120M earlier; repaid INR 400 crores short-term loans; consolidated leverage at 4.4x end-Q2, targeting ~4x by year-end
items.quote: During the last quarter, we bought back $44 million of the USD dollar bonds. This is in line with our efforts to reduce our cost of capital and increase the debt maturity, which is currently seven and a half years.

items.statement: Transmission 2026 USD bonds maturing next year to be refinanced well ahead via mix of dollar and rupee bonds; AA+ rated rupee bonds pricing sub-8%
items.quote: Yes, basically, currently, if you look at it, A A+ plus or AAA+ bonds are generally priced sub 8%. So, in that region, it would get priced.

items.statement: No equity fundraise planned; only project debt for under-construction projects and refinancing of existing bonds
items.quote: No, there is no such plans of any fundraise except for whatever debt which we have to take for the projects which we are at under construction stage. And of course, refinance.

items.statement: Applied for parallel distribution licenses in Navi Mumbai, Mundra, Ghaziabad/Jewar; Navi Mumbai and Mundra regulatory proceedings complete, orders expected soon; Navi Mumbai capex INR 10,000 crores over 5 years
items.quote: We applied for parallel license for Navi Mumbai, Mundra area, as well as Ghaziabad or Jewar district in the UP. The regulatory process for Navi Mumbai and Mundra part is over. We are expecting order from Regulatory Commission very soon.

items.statement: Draft electricity amendments propose enabling second licensee to use existing network; AESL prefers building own network for reliability and service quality differentiation
items.quote: The draft amendment proposed that the second license, new licensee can use existing distribution network of the existing licensee as well. So, it is clearly a good sign for the distribution sector, and it will create a lot of opportunity for private sector players.

items.statement: Transmission bidding pipeline of INR 80,000-90,000 crores over next 1-1.5 years identified by CTU and central government; Maharashtra state additions possible
items.quote: But in next 1 year to 1.5 year the projects which have been identified by CTU, and the central government are of the order of INR 90,000 crores. There could be addition from a few states as well, like Maharashtra. So nearly INR 80,000 crores to INR 90,000 crores of bidding opportunity or pipeline will be there in transmission.

items.statement: Smart meter addressable opportunity of ~10 crore meters in next year from Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Telangana, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab; Tamil Nadu technical evaluation ongoing, Karnataka/Telangana RDSS approvals pending
items.quote: As far as the addressable market is concerned, there is about 10 crores smart metering opportunity that we think that will come in a year or so. Essentially from Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Telangana, Madhya Pradesh, and Punjab.

items.statement: HVDC Khavda-Olpad: L1 in reverse auction, awaiting PFC response; underground cabling at Vashi Creek critical path; targeting December 2025 commissioning
items.quote: So, HVDC is all going perfectly all right. All approvals are there. All ROW issues sorted out. The critical work which is going on is the underground cabling on the Vashi Creek. And we expect that to get commissioned somewhere in December.

items.statement: Bhadla-Fatehpur HVDC: SPV and LOI received, contracts finalized, construction started at Bhadla land, transmission line erection starting next month
items.quote: Bhadla-Fatehpur, we already got that SPV, LOI, we have finalized all the contracts. In fact, the construction work has already begun at the Bhadla land. We will also start transmission line erection activity in the next month itself.

items.statement: Launched own training facility from November 1 to train 1,200 people for transmission line erection; will supply trained manpower to EPC partners to address skilled labor shortage
items.quote: And this year, we have taken a very unique initiative by starting our own training facility. It is going to be online from 1st of November this year. We will be training about 1200 people for transmission line erection. And with that, all of our requirements should be met.

items.statement: Right-of-way and skilled manpower remain key transmission execution risks; using hybrid approach of direct farmer negotiation and legal routes; new GOI ROW compensation policies notified by most states but collector process involves public
items.quote: So, right-of-way, all the required legal framework is now in place. So, after last year's policy intervention from Government of India, most of the state has notified that the policy for right -of-way. Essentially, these policies are targeting to give fair compensation to the landholder. To use this policy framework, you have to go through that process of getting order issues from collectors. That

items.statement: Data center opportunity with Google tie-up: AESL to provide energy solutions and connectivity infrastructure (similar to Microsoft data center); too early to quantify monetizable opportunity
items.quote: Yes. So, probably we will have an opportunity for AESL in terms of providing energy solutions and timely connectivity. Because like what we did last time as well for Microsoft, when they were developing a data center, we created connectivity in infra for them.

items.statement: VoNB margin guidance maintained at 26-28% range for FY26
items.quote: So, our guidance for the margin remains what we had given earlier in the range of 26% to 28%.

items.statement: APE growth guidance for FY26 is 13-14% on individual APE basis
items.quote: APE growth, as we have mentioned, it will be in the around 13% to 14%. And we are talking about individual APE for the overall for FY '26.

items.statement: Protection business share expected to exceed 10% of total APE
items.quote: The company expects to increase its protection share to above 10% of APE, and it is in line with our H1 growth.

items.statement: H1 FY26 VoNB margin at 27.8%, up 98 bps YoY; Q2 FY26 margin at 28.0%
items.quote: VoNB margin stands at 27.8% for the period ended September 30, 2025, a gain of 98 basis points.

items.statement: GST impact on H1 VoNB margin is 80 bps; annualized impact estimated at 174 bps if product mix unchanged
items.quote: So if you see, we have clarified this total GST impact is 80 basis points for the H1. Out of that, the business written on 22nd and onwards has impact of only 20 basis points.

items.statement: ULIP margins expected to improve slightly due to longer premium paying terms and rider attachment
items.quote: In fact, we expect the ULIP margin slightly go up given the product that we launched has a longer premium paying term. And secondly, we have also introduced the rider at taching to those

items.statement: Non-par and par segments driving growth; ULIP maintained at same level in early Q3
items.quote: If you look at the growth of our various lines of businesses, the entire growth is coming from the non-par and par segment.

items.statement: Protection APE grew 33% YoY; individual pure protection APE up 143%
items.quote: The Protection segment recorded robust performance with a 33% year-on-year growth on an APE basis.

items.statement: Non-par saving products contribute 20% of individual APE; participating products saw 57% Q2 vs Q1 NBP growth
items.quote: As on September '25, our guaranteed non-par saving products are contributing 20% on individual APE basis.

items.statement: Individual and group new business sum assured grew 76% and 107% YoY respectively
items.quote: Individual and group new business sum assured registered a growth of 76% and 107%, respectively, compare d to corresponding period last year

items.statement: Banca and agency channels back on track with ~15% IRP growth in September and October
items.quote: If you look at the individual September month numbers, the growth was around 15%. And we are happy that the same trend is continuing in the month of October also.

items.statement: 9.6 lakh new policies issued and 11.9 million lives covered in H1 FY26
items.quote: During the half year ended September 30, 2025, total 9.6 lakh new policies were issued. Number of lives covered during the half year ended September 30 is 11.9 million.

items.statement: Death claim settlement ratio at 99%; mis-selling ratio at 0.02%, among lowest in private industry
items.quote: Death claim settlement ratio stands at 99% for the half year ended September 30. Our mis-selling ratio stands at 0.02%, which is one of the lowest in the private industry.

items.statement: Opened 44 new branches and added 3,500+ employees in H1 FY26
items.quote: We have opened 44 new branches this year. The expansion is aligned with our vision to create infrastructure that supports the long-term development of our agency channel.

items.statement: Branch expansion and hiring driving higher operating expenses as planned
items.quote: The increase in expenses, you can also attribute to our planned expansion of our branches that we had guided for. We have opened 44 new branches, and there is increase in employee count by more than 3,500 during first half year.

items.statement: Bancassurance (SBI+RRBs) contributes 57% of total APE; non-SBI banca ~3% of individual APE
items.quote: With strength of more than 58,000 CIFs, the bancassurance business of SBI and RRBs contributes 57% of the total APE business.

items.statement: Agency channel added 64,000+ agents gross; productivity at INR 2.7 lakh per agent on individual NBP
items.quote: During the half year ended, the company added more than 64,000 agents on a gross basis.

items.statement: Other channels (direct, brokers, online) grew 36% YoY on individual NBP; contribute 14% of total APE
items.quote: As mentioned in opening remarks, the other channels, direct, corporate agents, brokers, online and web aggregators grew at 36% in terms of individual new business premium and contribute 14% of total APE.

items.statement: 99% individual proposals submitted digitally; 59% processed via automated underwriting
items.quote: The company continues efficient usage of technology for simplification of processes with 99% of individual proposals being submitted digitally. 59% of the individual proposals are processed through automated underwriting.

items.statement: No changes to distributor commissions planned; managing GST impact via product mix and operational levers
items.quote: No. As of now, we are not considering any changes in the distribution commission and company will be utilizing other levers on operational side and the product mix side to manage this impact.

items.statement: Indian Embedded Value at INR 760 billion, up 15% YoY; operating RoEV at 17.6%
items.quote: Embedded value for the company as on September 30, 2025, stands at INR 760 billion, growth of 15% over corresponding period and operating return on EV is at 17.6%.

items.statement: Assets under management at INR 4.81 trillion, up 10% YoY
items.quote: As mentioned in my opening remarks, asset under management stands at INR 4.81 trillion as at September 30, 2025, having a growth of 10%.

items.statement: Solvency ratio at 1.94 vs regulatory requirement of 1.50
items.quote: Solvency ratio at 1.94 as against the regulatory requirement of 1.50.

items.statement: Total annuity and pension new business at INR 37.8 billion
items.quote: Total annuity and pension new business underwritten by the company is INR 37.8 billion.

items.statement: Non-par saving products repriced to pass on yield curve benefits to customers; margins maintained
items.quote: Our endeavour is to maintain the margins at the current level. So in case yield curve movement move down, we will go and reprice the product.

items.statement: GST impact on renewal premiums creates 60 bps drag on H1 margin; annualized impact 174 bps if mix unchanged
items.quote: So even if we've not done anything, the margin impact will not be 1.74%. It will be around 1% kind of things which is 60%.

items.statement: No assumption changes in EV; only economic assumption changes from yield curve movement
items.quote: Yes. So you're right. So we have not made any changes in the assumption. So assumption remains the same. Only this is economic assumption is just a matter of the movement in the yield curve that we have taken.

items.statement: Management targets 1.5x industry growth; if industry grows 12-13%, company aims for 20%; if industry grows 8-9%, target is 13-14%
items.quote: We intend to grow at 1.5x the industry growth. So, if industry growth is around 12-13%, we should grow at 20%. If industry growth is at 8-9%, we would be targeting to grow at 13-14%.

items.statement: Extended monsoon and early Diwali caused EPC execution delays, leading to flat order book around Rs.720-730 crores for three quarters
items.quote: this year actually has been some extraordinary monsoon period was there and due to which our customers, which are typically the EPC players, who kind of do the project execution work on the ground, they were not able to work properly and there were some delays in their execution process and that is why back-to-back impact came on our order book also

items.statement: Management expects project execution to pick up aggressively in Q3 and Q4 after monsoon and festival season
items.quote: I think the project execution should start aggressively now in the third and the fourth quarter.

items.statement: Gross margin improved ~50-60 bps in Q2 due to favorable customer and product mix; margin traction expected to continue from new projects and private utility/smart metering orders
items.quote: it is a slight increase of I think around 50 to 60 basis points in this quarter and that was largely attributable to the customer mix and the product mix.

items.statement: Business model described as 80% raw material, 10% admin/employee cost, 10% EBITDA margin; quarterly variation of 0.5-1% normal
items.quote: What I always say is that it is a 80-10-10 business roughly; 80% is raw material consumption, 10% is our admin and employee cost, and 10% is our EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR 721 crores as of 30th September 2025, providing strong revenue visibility
items.quote: As of 30th September 2025, our order book stands at INR 721 crores, providing strong revenue visibility.

items.statement: Export orders constitute Rs.90-100 crores of current order book (~14-15%)
items.quote: Around I think Rs.90 to 100 crores is export in the current order book.

items.statement: Debottlenecking capex of ~Rs.15 crores completed mostly in FY25; new Greenfield plant capex Rs.40-45 crores (Rs.25 crores spent in H1, Rs.15-20 crores planned in H2)
items.quote: Around Rs.40 crores to 50 crores. So, in H1, we have done around Rs.25 crores and I think in H2, we will be doing an additional Rs.15, 20 crores.

items.statement: Post-debottlenecking capacity is Rs.135 crores/month; new plant commissioning expected end of H2 FY26, capacity available from FY27
items.quote: our ongoing capacity expansion plan is progressing well and remains on schedule for commissioning in second half of FY26.

items.statement: Current utilization ~70% in Q2; optimum utilization targeted at 85-90% due to seasonality and customization
items.quote: in the current quarter, if you do math, it comes to around 70%.

items.statement: H1 FY26 revenue mix: HV cables 55%, LV cables 37%, conductors 8%; solar cables currently 10-15% of revenue, targeting higher share post new plant with DC cable capability
items.quote: Product wise contribution in H1 FY26 was, HV sales 55%, LV cable 37%, conductors 8%.

items.statement: H1 FY26 customer mix: government 12%, private 78%, exports 10%; strategy to reduce government share, increase private share, maintain export share
items.quote: Customer-wise contribution in H1 FY26 was, government sales 12%, private sales 78%, exports 10%.

items.statement: Exports ~10% of H1 sales (Rs.56 crores); full-year export target 10-15% of revenue; margins similar to domestic; US market entry delayed due to tariff uncertainty
items.quote: It would be in the range of 10% to 15% only, because in our order book also, if you look at it, around 14%, 15% of our order book is our export order.

items.statement: Cable inventory stuck with both company and customers due to monsoon-driven execution slowdown; clarity expected in November-December
items.quote: Both ways. So, cable inventory is stuck with us, also with our customers also.

items.statement: Volume growth 20-23% in H1 FY26; revenue growth matches volume growth as aluminum prices stable
items.quote: So, H1 volume growth is around 20% to 23%.

items.statement: Smart metering contributed ~10% of H1 revenue with healthy order book; margins similar to power distribution cables
items.quote: we have a fair bit of around 10% of our business is being contributed in H1 from smart metering.

items.statement: EHV cables not in near-term plans due to high capex, long gestation, lower asset turnover; focusing on low-hanging fruits in LV/HV/specialty cables
items.quote: EHV as a segment is a completely different ballgame, because it requires specific technology and it has a very niche market in the overall wire and cable space if you talk about.

items.statement: US market entry on hold awaiting clarity on 50% tariff announcement; product approvals continuing in parallel
items.quote: we will have to wait for this clarification on the tariff side before we get into the US market. So, we are just waiting for these clouds to shut out first and then probably we will be able to get it.

items.statement: Monsoon execution delays may cause H2 slowdown vs last year; tender pipeline strong but conversion to orders depends on EPC execution pickup
items.quote: the only problem is that the execution has slowed down a bit. And because of this, the conversion of the EPC contracts or the tendering is not flowing into the cable orders.

items.statement: Employee/admin cost increase due to incentive bookings and new hires for new technical tie-ups and ventures; annual cost ~10% of revenue (+/-0.5%)
items.quote: there were some new joinees in this half as we are venturing into the new areas, we are seeding new technical tie-ups and all those things.

items.statement: Indo Krates provided corporate guarantee and mortgaged immovable property as collateral for Dynamic Cables' working capital facilities
items.quote: Indo Krates has a immovable property, which is mortgaged with the bank as a collateral security for the working capital facility which Dynamic cables avails.

items.statement: Data center opportunity being pursued via vendor registration and cable development; meaningful contribution expected in 2+ quarters
items.quote: we are also targeting that area which in our earlier calls also we have discussed about trying to be a relevant player in this entire data center ecosystem, for which we have started taking steps like vendor registration and all those things.

items.quote: But as of now, for the next at least 2 to 3 quarters, our focus is essentially to get the credit cost d own to a reasonable number before we start looking at the growth parameters

items.statement: Diketene derivatives maintain growth momentum
items.quote: Diketene derivatives also maintained its growth momentum across both quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year basis, reflecting consistent performance and market traction.

items.statement: Cosmetics and Semi-conductor Chemicals segments show increasing traction

items.statement: Specialty Chemicals segment margins at 25%+ in Q2 FY26
items.quote: The Specialty Chemicals segment continued on its revenue trajectory and reported 25%-plus margins during the quarter.

items.statement: Nutrition segment pricing softness partially offset by volume growth
items.quote: While pricing softness partially offset revenue growth, the underlying volume performance remains robust.

items.statement: Nutrition segment expects price premium for EU choline exports vs. domestic market
items.quote: We are expecting to get price premium vis-a-vis domestic market in choline.

items.statement: INR100+ crore annual lean savings program on track
items.quote: Our INR100 crore plus per annum lean savings program remains firmly on track driving efficiency across the value chain.

items.quote: In Bharuch, a new boiler is scheduled for commissioning in Q3 FY '26.

items.quote: We are excited to announce plans for the state-of-the-art Semi-conductor R&D facility in Greater Noida.

items.quote: Post this acquisition, I'd say between 24 to 26 is what we try to do.

items.quote: So, with that, netting that off , our net order book now stands at ₹236 billion, and the EV share continues to remain high at 70% of this order book.

items.statement: First order for Mexico driveline plant adds ₹2.6 billion with production starting Q2 FY28
items.quote: This program has added 2.6 billion to our order book with production expected to start in the second quarter of FY 28.

items.statement: Two new suspension system nominations worth ₹8.2 billion lifetime value starting production Q2 FY27
items.quote: These two nominations have an order value of, as you can see on the screen, about ₹8.2 billion in the lifetime, and they're expected both to start production in Q2 of FY 27.

items.statement: BEV revenue declined 17% in Q2 and 21% in H1 due to single customer and single model drop
items.quote: BEV revenue has declined by 17% in the last quarter. The revenue share because of this has fallen to 32%.

items.statement: Growth primarily from trains, tractors, and traction motors; other segments flattish to moderate
items.quote: In terms of end markets, I'll keep it short. The growth has primarily been from trains, tractors, and traction motors. So, the railway segment, the off-highway segment, and electric two -wheelers, these are where we see growth. The other ones are flattish to moderate growth.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin down 2.3% YoY to 25.3% due to product mix and operating leverage; H1 margin down 3.2%
items.quote: Our EBITDA has grown by 13% in the same period to ₹289 crore. EBITDA margin is lower by 2.3% compared to the same quarter last year, and that's primarily due to product mix and operational leverage.

items.quote: we generated ₹340 crores as cash from operations in the first half of the year and spent about ₹198 crores on CAPEX. Besides this, in the first half, we also saw major cash outflows on account of railway business acquisition and last tranche payment of NOVELIC acquisition, aggregating to nearly ₹1,700 crore. items.statement: Non-automotive revenue share increased from 10% to 29% in H1; hybrid share 24% of automotive revenue
items.quote: Revenue share from non -automotive sectors has gone from 10% to 29% in H1 of this year.

items.statement: Hybrid vehicles contribute 24% of automotive revenue
items.quote: The answer to that hybrid question, basically we have 24% revenue share of automotive products from hybrids.

items.statement: Developed rare-earth-free ferrite-assisted synchronous reluctance motor for 2W, 3W, LCV; tested in lab and road conditions
items.quote: We have successfully developed and tested rare-earth-free traction motors. These ferrite-assisted motors are based on synchronous reluctance technology. For both mid -drive and hub motors, as the name suggests, these motors do not use rare earth magnets and therefore are not dependent on China raw materials and manufacturing.

items.statement: Top 5 customers contribute 51% of revenue (down from 62% in FY22); top 10 contribute 72% (down from 80%); largest customer and 2 of top 5 added since FY22
items.quote: In Q2, the top 5 customers contribute 51% of total revenue. This is down from 62%, 3.5 years ago in FY22. Additionally, the contribution from our top 10 customers has been reduced to 72% from 80%. And the biggest points to note are th ese: our largest customer, plus 2 of the top 5 customers and 3 of the top 10 customers, were not even present in our customer base in FY22.

items.statement: Three European driveline competitors filed for insolvency; unprecedented increase in inquiries from European customers
items.quote: In the past 6 months, 3 of our direct competitors in Europe have filed for insolvency proceedings. This has resulted in an unprecedented increase in inquiries from European customers to us.

items.statement: US extended tariff relief on US-assembled vehicles for 5 years, benefiting Sona's US customers
items.quote: the recent decision by the US administration to extend tariff relief on vehicles assembled in the US for 5 years should benefit our US customers , who are predominantly assembling their vehicles locally within the US.

items.statement: China JV with JNT put in abeyance due to geopolitical factors; will resume if lead indicators change
items.quote: After careful consideration, we have decided to put a proposed joint venture with JNT in China in abeyance. This decision is based mostly on geopolitical factors and the need to prioritize other active capital allocation decisions.

items.statement: India largest end market at 45% of H1 revenue; North America 30%; Eastern markets exceed Western for first time since listing
items.quote: Today, geographically, India is our largest end market in H1. It accounts for 45% of our revenue for the first half. North America has become our second largest market, contributing 30%, and significantly, and for us it's quite a shift. For the first time since we went public, we've achieved higher revenue from the eastern markets than we do from the West.

items.statement: Railway business has different working capital terms; focusing on improving cash conversion cycles

We are trying to bring that rigor, that TQM approach, that theory o f constraints type reviews so that we can improve every week a little better than we were before.

items.quote: ROE and ROC E have declined to 13% and 16% Sona Comstar – Q2 FY26 Earnings Call respectively, and this is because of the equity capital issue that we did in September 2024, and the full -year effect has come into the denominator now. items.quote: Yeah, so good that both of these are low risk for us , given our exposure to what kind of customers, what kind of models, etc., but we are monitoring them actively.

items.statement: Collaboration with Neura Robotics Germany for joint development of robots, cobots, humanoids; several roadmap products moving to prototype phase
items.quote: We recently signed an MOU with Neura Robotics of Germany. Neura is a pioneer in the field of cognitive robotics. This strategic collaboration aims to jointly develop advanced te chnologies, components, and sub -assemblies, as well as industrialization of robots and humanoids for India and mutually agreed markets.

items.statement: Suspension motor revenue buildup gradual; binary takeoff when large volume OEM adopts; 0-5 years for some revenue, 5-10 for massive revenue
items.quote: So, 0 to 5 to get to good or some revenue, and 5 to 10 to go to massive revenue. That's usually the scale.

items.statement: Raised FY26 constant currency revenue growth guidance to 21%+ and adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to close to 25%
items.quote: But now given the good momentum that we are seeing, I'm pleased to increase the revenue guidance in constant currency to 21% plus and an adjusted EBITDA guidance of close to 25% for the full fiscal FY 2026.

items.statement: Organic constant currency growth guidance maintained at low to mid-teens for FY26
items.quote: Previously, we are guided to see the organic constant currency growth of low to mid -teens is a range that we are still committing to.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin at 26.2%, up year-on-year
items.quote: Operating profitability remained rob ust with adjusted EBITDA at INR 4,352 million or $49.8 million representing a year-on-year increase of 25.6%. So this EBITDA translates to an EBITDA margin of 26.2%, very robust.

items.statement: Medium-term EBITDA margin baseline goal of 24% to 25% range
items.quote: So overall, I would continue to be bullish on margins. We'll guide closer to the start of every fiscal year. But I would think the 24% to 25% range would be at least our baseline goal, even in the medium term.

items.statement: Clients under profitability pressure driving larger deal constructs and wallet share gains
items.quote: The market is going through a lot of change, right? Our specific clients in the health care industry, especially payers, a lot of them are going through profitability pressures. So today, the focus is how can you help me take out more cost from my operations, right?

items.statement: Q2 FY26 new wins: $34 million ACV from 24 existing and 5 new clients
items.quote: During the quarter, we secured business from 24 existing clients, and we also added fi ve new clients. The aggregate annual contract value won from new and existing clients stands at $34 million.

items.statement: ACV is incremental revenue, not including renewals; $32M ACV should generate $32M over four quarters
items.quote: So all of these wins are essentially incremental revenues. And in the normal course of business, $32 million ACV should generate $32 million over a period of four quarters, and it should be recurring year-on-year, right?

items.statement: Deployed 25 distinct AI use cases across nine clients, up from 18 use cases last quarter
items.quote: In addition to the 18 use cases that we spoke about last quarter, I'm happy to announce that we've successfully now deployed 25 distinct AI use cases across nine clients.

items.statement: AI agent pricing at 25-35% of offshore human agent cost, 10-15% of onshore human agent cost
items.quote: If you take a traditional offshore geography, the broad math woul d be an AI agent could probably be anywhere between 25% to 35% of a human agent. Whereas the same AI agent, if the human were to be based onshore, could be as low as 10% to 15% or 10% to 12% of the human agent, right?

items.statement: Consolidated sites to optimise operational costs; fixed asset additions prudent
items.quote: Our additions to fixed assets have been very prudent, and we have consolidated some sites, which has actually helped us in an optimising operational cost.

items.statement: External commercial borrowing at 8% coupon from parent; full repayment by end of FY27; scheduled repayment in H2 FY26
items.quote: As I said, we have a repayment of debt that is likely to happen in the last quarter of this year. And by end of next fiscal, the entire debt will be cleared.

items.statement: Interim dividend of 5 paise per share approved for Q3 FY26 payment
items.quote: I'm also happy to announce that the Board has announced as approved , an interim dividend of 0.05 or 5 paise per share to be paid in Q3.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 revenue: INR 16,585M ($189.4M), up 25.2% YoY INR, 20% CC; organic growth 16% INR, 11.1% CC
items.quote: Consolidated revenues for Q2 came in at INR 16,585 million or $189.4 million. Marking a year -on-year expansion of about 25.2% in INR ter ms and 20% in constant currency.

items.statement: H1 FY26 revenue: INR 31,974M ($369.9M), up 25.5% YoY INR, 21.4% CC; organic growth 16.9% INR, 13.2% CC
items.quote: We are pleased to report that H1 FY '26 registered a year-on-year revenue growth of 25.5% in INR terms and 21.4% in constant currency terms. And during the first half of the year, we recorded revenues of $369.9 million, which tr anslates to INR 31,974 million.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 adjusted PAT: INR 3,010M, up 84% YoY; H1 FY26 adjusted PAT: INR 5,007M, up 62.4% YoY
items.quote: Half yearly adjusted EBITDA of INR 8,039 million grew 26% year-on-year, while our adjusted PAT of INR 5,007 million grew 62.4% year-on-year.

items.statement: ROCE stable at 50%+ on trailing 12-month basis
items.quote: ROCE is stable at 50% plus and we didn't have any debt repayment in this quarter.

items.statement: Q2 FX tailwind: ~1.1% adjusted EBITDA improvement (~$6M) from higher average FX rates vs Q1
items.quote: The average FX rates in Q2 was much higher than the Q1. The impact was almost 1.1% improvement in adjusted EBITDA close to about 6 million.

items.statement: Pursuing acquisitions selectively to enrich capabilities and expand market access
items.quote: We will as always pursue acquisition selectively. And in those acquisitions, we seek to not only enrich our capabilities, but also expand our market access.

items.statement: H2 FY26 seasonally stronger (53-54% of revenue); BroadPath skew even more to Q3; AEP season kicked off Oct 15
items.quote: If you look at historically our business, if you look at the revenue split, it's roughly 53% to 54% in H2 compared to a 46% to 47% in H1, right. So that's the typical split of our revenue.
